tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

|---|---|

## 4. Media-handling decisions (APPROVED) [APP p.11–12, 18]

| Media | Decision | ID |
|---|---|---|
| General | Handle PDFs, infographics and videos **only when they hold unique information essential to MVP coverage**. Use the **simplest extraction method** suited to each content type | REQ-SRC-008 |

Videos don't expand the MVP | REQ-SRC-011, REQ-SCP-009 |

## 5. Policy nuances flagged for structured reasoning [APP p.21–22]

All are **AUTHORED-FACT (unverified)** and come from the project approach, not from a frozen
source. Each must be verified in Phase 2 before it is used as a fact, rule or benchmark label.

| Nuance | Paraphrase of claim to verify | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| HFE validity and timing | The HFE letter is valid for nine months from issue. A valid letter is needed to apply for a new flat. Changes to household details may affect eligibility or invalidate the letter | Core |
| Income assessment | The assessment period is 12 months, ending two months before the HFE application month. For employed persons, the average depends on months worked in that period, not necessarily on dividing by 12 | Core (documentation/follow-up only, D-013) |

conditions, exceptions, effective dates and source references are structured metadata
wherever possible (REQ-ARC-006).

Missing applicant information** | The applicant hasn't given a detail needed to identify the relevant preparation requirements | One partner's citizenship status is unknown; HFE application/approval status is unspecified; prior flat ownership or application is not stated; employment information is needed but not supplied | Ask a targeted follow-up, or name the information to prepare. **Never assume missing values** |
188	| **B. Missing policy information in the corpus** | The frozen KB lacks enough authoritative evidence to answer reliably | A linked FAQ with an exception was never included; an accordion condition wasn't extracted; an infographic has a step absent from the text; the policy changed after capture; the passage exists but retrieval missed it | Don't invent an answer. Flag insufficient evidence or unsupported coverage and direct the user to the official source |

191	The runtime contract is in [04 §3](04_architecture.md).

198	| Scenario | Description | Capability shown |
199	|---|---|---|
200	| A — Straightforward applicant | A fictional first-time couple gives a complete profile. BTO Buddy identifies the relevant preparation requirements and links official sources | Straightforward guidance |
201	| B — Missing information | A couple gives incomplete employment or household information. BTO Buddy asks targeted follow-ups instead of making an unsupported determination | Missing-information handling |
202	| C — Policy misconception | An applicant assumes something incorrect about application consequences. BTO Buddy retrieves the official guidance, explains the distinction and flags uncertainty where needed | Verification layer |

204	- **APPROVED constraint:** the demo examples must represent actual system behaviour. Don't
205	  pick only unusually easy cases that hide known failure modes.
206	- The original text called Scenario C valuable for the "PolicyProof-inspired" verification
207	  layer. That label is HISTORICAL (D-015).
208

210	
211	- **REQ-SCP-012:** a small system that handles **4–5 policy areas** accurately, with a
212	  rigorous baseline comparison, beats a broad, unreliable assistant.
213	- **REQ-SCP-011:** never claim comprehensive coverage of all current and historical BTO
214	  policies. Rules vary by application date, flat classification, applicant category and
215	  policy changes. A statement can be correct for one sales exercise and wrong for another.
216	
217	## 10. Positioning against the brief's illustrative sketches [ASM p.5–6]
218	
219	The brief offers optional, anonymised problem sketches, and choosing any of them is not
220	required. The nearest ones are:
221	- profile-driven benefits matching;
222	- citizen-enquiry triage with escalation;
223	- out-of-knowledge-base robustness for RAG ("I do not know" vs confabulation).
224	
225	*(Author note: neither source document says which sketch, if any, BTO Buddy derives from.
226	The developer should confirm the wording before using this in the README.)*

## 7. Missing information: two distinct categories — REQ-SCP-013 (APPROVED) [APP p.18–19]

These must be kept separate in the architecture, the benchmark and the documentation.

| Category | Meaning | Examples | Required behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Missing applicant information** | The applicant hasn't given a detail needed to identify the relevant preparation requirements | One partner's citizenship status is unknown; HFE application/approval status is unspecified; prior flat ownership or application is not stated; employment information is needed but not supplied | Ask a targeted follow-up, or name the information to prepare. **Never assume missing values** |
| **B. Missing policy information in the corpus** | The frozen KB lacks enough authoritative evidence to answer reliably | A linked FAQ with an exception was never included; an accordion condition wasn't extracted; an infographic has a step absent from the text; the policy changed after capture; the passage exists but retrieval missed it | Don't invent an answer. Flag insufficient evidence or unsupported coverage and direct the user to the official source |

The failure sub-types of category B are listed in [05 §8](05_evaluation.md).
The runtime contract is in [04 §3](04_architecture.md).

## 8. Demo archetypes — REQ-SCP-014 [APP p.20–21]

These are for the 3–5 minute video. They are **not** the evaluation dataset and can still be
refined.

| Scenario | Description | Capability shown |
|---|---|---|
| A — Straightforward applicant | A fictional first-time couple gives a complete profile. BTO Buddy identifies the relevant preparation requirements and links official sources | Straightforward guidance |
| B — Missing information | A couple gives incomplete employment or household information. BTO Buddy asks targeted follow-ups instead of making an unsupported determination | Missing-information handling |
| C — Policy misconception | An applicant assumes something incorrect about application consequences. BTO Buddy retrieves the official guidance, explains the distinction and flags uncertainty where needed | Verification layer |

- **APPROVED constraint:** the demo examples must represent actual system behaviour. Don't
  pick only unusually easy cases that hide known failure modes.
- The original text called Scenario C valuable for the "PolicyProof-inspired" verification
  layer. That label is HISTORICAL (D-015).

## 9. Scope discipline and non-claims (APPROVED) [APP p.28]

- **REQ-SCP-012:** a small system that handles **4–5 policy areas** accurately, with a
  rigorous baseline comparison, beats a broad, unreliable assistant.
- **REQ-SCP-011:** never claim comprehensive coverage of all current and historical BTO
  policies. Rules vary by application date, flat classification, applicant category and
  policy changes. A statement can be correct for one sales exercise and wrong for another.

## 10. Positioning against the brief's illustrative sketches [ASM p.5–6]

The brief offers optional, anonymised problem sketches, and choosing any of them is not
required. The nearest ones are:
- profile-driven benefits matching;
- citizen-enquiry triage with escalation;
- out-of-knowledge-base robustness for RAG ("I do not know" vs confabulation).

*(Author note: neither source document says which sketch, if any, BTO Buddy derives from.
The developer should confirm the wording before using this in the README.)*

  decisions are never forced into binary rules (for example, unwed-parent cases are assessed
  holistically).
- **Benefits:**
  - deterministic, unit-testable checks;
  - clear separation of policy facts from model explanations;
  - a defensible architecture for a consequential public-service domain.
- **Example** (original APP p.15, updated per D-006):

  ```yaml
  rule_id: HFE_REQUIRED
  scope: new_flat_application
  condition:
    requires_valid_hfe: true
  outcome:
    preparation_step: "Obtain a valid HFE letter"
  source_fact_id: HFE-REQUIRED-001     # D-006: reviewer-accessible fact ID
  # source_passage_id: hfe_application_001   # SUPERSEDED (private passage ID; may be kept as provenance)
  requires_human_review: false
  ```

## 4. Dataset C — independently labelled evaluation scenarios [APP p.15–16]

The full design is in [05_evaluation.md §3](05_evaluation.md).

- **REQ-DAT-016:** Dataset C is kept **separate from the knowledge corpus and from the
  runtime verifier**.
- **REQ-DAT-017:** profiles are fictional and use synthetic names. **Real applicant records
  are never used.**
  - Reason: real records are sensitive and hard to access.
  - Synthetic profiles suit controlled rule testing and edge-case coverage.
- **Defence of synthetic data** (needed by REQ-DAT-002):
  - scenarios are *policy-derived* from verified rules and vary one or two factors at a
    time, including boundary conditions;
  - labels are assigned manually against official rules, never invented by an LLM.

## 5. Licensing, access and permissions

### 5.1 Preliminary findings — to verify in Phase 2 (D-024)
- **REQ-LIC-013:** HDB website materials are subject to HDB's published **Terms of Use** and
  copyright.
  - Singapore's **Copyright Act 2021, ss 243–244**, gives a conditional exception for
    *computational data analysis*, covering certain copying and retention, subject to
    lawful-access, purpose and sharing restrictions.
  - This is a *preliminary* reading. The statutory text and the Terms of Use must be checked.
- **REQ-LIC-014:** **robots.txt** compliance [ASM p.2] for every host:
  - `www.hdb.gov.sg`;
  - `file.go.gov.sg`;
  - `www.mynicehome.gov.sg`;
  - (YouTube: links only).

  Status: **not yet checked**.
- **REQ-LIC-012:** **never claim HDB has granted a general redistribution licence.**
- **REQ-LIC-016:** a script may support lawful acquisition. Re-downloading current pages
  can't rebuild a historical frozen snapshot, so hashes and capture dates must be recorded.

### 5.2 Redistribution rules (APPROVED) [APP p.13–14]
- **Git-ignored:**
  - full HDB HTML files;
  - extracted passages containing substantial original text;
  - source-derived indexes containing such text.

  These stay ignored unless redistribution permission is established.
- **May be tracked, subject to content and rights review:**
  - independently authored factual representations;
  - source URLs and metadata;
  - rule definitions and evaluation labels;
  - processing scripts.
- The three-way distinction to document:
  1. A private source snapshot, for local extraction and analysis.
  2. A reviewer-accessible, independently authored policy KB.
  3. A frozen evaluation dataset of fictional scenarios with independently checked labels.
- **REQ-LIC-015:** before submission, review **all tracked data** for copyright, privacy
  and credential exposure.
- **REQ-LIC-017 (D-016):** project-context docs use authored summaries, never substantial
  copyrighted text.

## 6. Privacy — REQ-PRIV-001, REQ-PRIV-010
- **No real personal data:** all profiles are fictional [APP p.16].
- **Deployment limitation [APP p.28]:** free-tier API data-handling terms may not suit
  personal information in a real deployment that ingests applicant data. This feeds the
  model-selection justification (REQ-MOD-001) and the deployment-risk section (REQ-DOC-002).
- **The app never touches transactional services** such as Singpass or the HDB Flat Portal
  (REQ-SRC-006).

## 7. Reproducibility — REQ-DAT-018, REQ-DAT-021, REQ-DAT-022 (APPROVED) [APP p.13–15]
- **Reviewer path:**
  - The repo includes the rights-reviewed `policy_facts.jsonl`, the rules, the source
    metadata and the evaluation datasets.
  - Reviewers build the retrieval index and run the Dockerised app **without downloading HDB
    pages or rebuilding the private corpus**.
- **Developer scripts:** source-capture and extraction scripts are optional and documented.
  They are **not** dependencies of startup or of primary evaluation.
- **Clean-machine test:** a clean-machine Docker test must prove the reviewer-facing
  configuration works (REQ-NFR-001).
- **Live API runs vary,** so each run records:
  - model identifiers;
  - prompt versions;
  - inference settings;
  - corpus versions;
  - **saved predictions**.

  Reproducible offline scoring is reported separately from new live inference.

## 8. README data-section draft (PROPOSED wording, APP p.14–15)

The draft paragraphs in the source cover: data sources, data acquisition (hybrid,
scope-controlled, manual approval, optional browser automation for expandable sections, no
crawling), source provenance (manifest), licensing and access, data handling and
redistribution, reproducibility and limitations.

The draft must be revised before use:
- It says the prototype uses **"four official HDB webpages"**. That is SUPERSEDED by D-007;
  report the final source count after Phase 2.
- It must reflect D-005 (canonical KB) and D-024 (preliminary rights findings).

## 9. Data limitations (APPROVED, for README) [APP p.15, 28]
- Policy content reflects the retrieved versions and may miss later changes.
- No live retrieval. The static KB and rule registry need **manual updates after each policy
  change**, which makes maintenance effort high.
- Synthetic profiles support controlled testing. They **can't establish** how often real
  applicants misunderstand rules, or how the assistant performs on real enquiries.
- The prototype gives informational preparation guidance. It doesn't replace the official
  eligibility assessment.
- **Representativeness (REQ-DAT-003):** state what the data covers and doesn't cover. That
  means the MVP tiers, the household types and the policy period.

requirements (D-001, D-012).

**Source tags:** `[ASM p.N]` = assessment brief, page N; `[APP p.N]` = project-approach
document, page N; `[DEV 2026-10-28]` = developer clarification given on that date.

1. Mandatory assessment requirements.

3. The finalised project scope, architecture, data strategy and evaluation methodology.

- the current approach;
- the alternative;

Configurations A–D are the same pipeline with stages switched off | Review A1; REQ-ARC-003 | The steps are fixed and known, so a linear pipeline is the simplest design that implements BD-04. Typed boundaries make each stage independently testable and scorable (REQ-ARC-007), and bound latency and cost | Exactly the approved capabilities (REQ-ARC-001). Adds no features beyond the MVP | — |
| D-031 | **Retrieval is BM25 only** (`rank-bm25`), over fact `statement` + `aliases`, filtered to gate-approved topics. Facts cited by applicable rules are always added to the evidence. Dense, hybrid or reranking retrieval is proposed **only if** dev retrieval recall@5 < 0.90 *and* error analysis attributes the misses to paraphrase. Facts schema gains an `aliases: list[str]` field | Review A2; REQ-ARC-010; part of Q-22 | ~100 acronym-heavy authored facts suit exact lexical matching, which is explainable, deterministic and dependency-light. Aliases fix BM25's synonym weakness cheaply. Rule-linked facts make required-rule evidence independent of ranking. Embeddings would add torch (≈2 GB image) or another data-sharing API with no demonstrated gain | Retrieval covers only in-scope topics; excluded topics are never searched | "BM25 or lightweight embeddings" open choice [APP p.21] |
| D-032 | **Quote-grounded extraction.** Each extracted field must carry a verbatim quote, and a deterministic guard drops any field whose quote isn't in the input. Missing fields are computed **only for the topics asked about** (plus rules returning `cannot_determine`). Follow-up questions come from static templates | Review A3; REQ-ARC-013, REQ-SCP-013 | Turns LLM extraction into an auditable step and blocks hallucinated applicant facts, the main risk in a consequential domain. Topic scoping avoids interrogating users with irrelevant questions. Templates make follow-ups deterministic and testable | Uses only fields needed by Core/Limited topics. Income/employment fields are limited to HFE documentation (D-013) | — |

# Requirements Register

Stable IDs: `REQ-<AREA>-<NNN>`. IDs are never renumbered or reused. Superseded items keep
their ID and are marked as superseded. Decisions are in [../decisions.md](../decisions.md).

**Status values:** `MANDATORY` (assessment brief) · `APPROVED` · `PROPOSED` · `OPEN` ·
`SUPERSEDED`.
**Source tags:** `[ASM p.N]` assessment brief · `[APP p.N]` project approach · `D-xxx` / `BD-xx`
decisions. Page numbers are physical PDF pages.

**Areas:**

| Code | Area | Code | Area |
|---|---|---|---|
| PRB | problem | ARC | architecture |
| SCP | scope | VER | verifier |
| SRC | sources | EVL | evaluation |
| DAT | data | MOD | model selection |
| LIC | licensing | DOC | documentation |
| PRIV | privacy | SUB | submission |

## 1. Overall task — MANDATORY [ASM p.1]
- Pick a problem relevant to Singapore public-sector stakeholders: an agency, a ministry or

- Build an AI-powered prototype, evaluate it comprehensively, and deliver a **Dockerised

- Classification, detection, retrieval, multimodal and agentic methods are all acceptable.
- **The brief's stated intent:** assess problem identification, scoping and technical
  judgement in using AI tools, especially judging viability and validating outputs
  rigorously.

## 2. Deliverables — MANDATORY [ASM p.2]

| ID | Requirement | Planned evidence |
|---|---|---|
| REQ-SUB-001 | Complete instructions for full deployment and execution | README "Run with Docker" section, tested on a clean machine |
| REQ-PRB-002 | **Significant** AI integration, not just an API call inside a standard web app | Architecture section plus ablation results (A–D) |
| REQ-EVL-001 | Choose and justify a specific evaluation method (e.g. benchmarking, LLM-as-judge, human evaluation, ablation, comparison), with the rationale in the README. Soundness outranks results | README evaluation section; [05](05_evaluation.md) |
| REQ-DAT-001 | Provenance, creation/processing, licensing and privacy for **all** data. Resourcefulness in finding data is assessed | README data section; `data/sources_manifest.json`; [03](03_data_and_licensing.md) |
| REQ-LIC-001 | Comply with source licensing and **robots.txt** | Rights review record (Phase 2) |

| REQ-DOC-001 | **Documentation is the primary artifact:** objectives, rationale, implementation, results, execution instructions, limitations | README |
| REQ-DOC-002 | A **150–250-word** README section: target user and environment; projected inference cost or compute footprint at scale; key post-deployment monitoring metrics; assessment of **one specific** deployment risk. *Only described, not implemented* | README section, word-count check |
| REQ-DOC-003 | A brief development narrative: iterations, discarded strategies, tool-selection rationale, decision justification | README section, drawing on [../decisions.md](../decisions.md) |
| REQ-SUB-003 | A **3–5 minute** demo video of the running application. **Its URL goes in the README** | README link (placeholder until recorded) |

## 3. Submission protocol — MANDATORY [ASM p.2] (details private)

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| REQ-SUB-004 | Deliver via a **private** GitHub repository with the assessor collaborator invited. *Handle kept in private notes* |
| REQ-SUB-005 | **The repository must remain anonymous** about the organisation and role |
| REQ-SUB-006 | The repository must **remain unchanged** throughout the evaluation period |
| REQ-SUB-007 | Submit the URL through the designated channel. *Details kept in private notes* |
| REQ-SUB-008 | **Deadline:** 5 days from receipt. **Estimated effort:** 12–16 hours of focused work. Submission time isn't scored. The receipt date isn't recorded (Q-18) |

## 4. Scoring dimensions — MANDATORY reference [ASM p.3]

| Dimension | Weight | What is assessed (paraphrased) | Main requirement links |
|---|---|---|---|
| Problem framing & creativity | 20% | Worth solving? A non-obvious angle rather than a first idea or low effort? | REQ-PRB-010..015 |
| Technical execution | 25% | Runs from the README on a clean machine; code quality. AI-assisted coding is expected, careless output is not | REQ-NFR-001, REQ-NFR-002 |
| Evaluation & effectiveness | 30% | Sound methodology. Novelty counts only with effectiveness; a proven approach that works beats a novel one that underperforms. Honest limitations | REQ-EVL-* |
| Data thinking | 15% | Provenance, licensing, representativeness, resourceful sourcing, awareness of what the data does and doesn't cover | REQ-DAT-*, REQ-LIC-* |

## 5. Critical non-compliance indicators — MANDATORY [ASM p.4]

| ID | Indicator to avoid |
|---|---|
| REQ-NFR-001 | **Not reproducible:** the solution fails when following the README |
| REQ-DOC-004 | **Code/write-up mismatch:** features, architecture or results described that aren't in the repo |
| REQ-NFR-003 | **Insufficient technical justification:** the developer must be able to explain the rationale behind code and architecture |
| REQ-MOD-001 | **Unsubstantiated model selection:** choices must be justified by operational needs such as privacy, latency or task fit |

  - local inference: Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio;

  - a gallery of past public-sector hackathon projects, as a calibration of feasible scope.
    *The link is kept privately.*

ai_logs/
├── README.md
├── claude_code/

**Draft AI-usage disclosure (PROPOSED, revised per D-009) [APP p.31]:**

## 5. Pydantic contracts (proposed; finalised with the Phase 2 facts schema, Q-22)

Field names are indicative. Enumerations that depend on verified policy (employment
categories, topics) are confirmed in Phase 2.

```python
# ---- shared enums -------------------------------------------------------------
class Tier(StrEnum): CORE="core"; LIMITED="limited"; CONTEXT="context"; EXCLUDED="excluded"

class Topic(StrEnum):
    # in scope (tier fixed by D-008)
    HOUSEHOLD_COMPOSITION="household_composition"          # core
    APPLICATION_REQUIREMENTS="application_requirements"    # core
    HFE_PROCESS="hfe_process"                              # core (prerequisites, timing, validity)
    HFE_DOCUMENTS="hfe_documents"                          # core (incl. income/employment docs, D-013)
    PRIORITY_CONSIDERATIONS="priority_considerations"      # limited
    NON_SELECTION="non_selection"                          # limited
    HFE_GRANT_LOAN_CONTEXT="hfe_grant_loan_context"        # context only
    # excluded (D-008)
    GRANT_LOAN_CALCULATION="grant_loan_calculation"
    FINANCING_AFFORDABILITY="financing_affordability"
    BALLOT_ODDS="ballot_odds"
    POST_PURCHASE="post_purchase"
    ELIGIBILITY_DETERMINATION="eligibility_determination"
    OTHER_HOUSING="other_housing"                          # resale, rental, EC, etc.
    UNRELATED="unrelated"

TOPIC_TIER: dict[Topic, Tier]   # single source of truth for the gate, unit-tested

class ProfileField(StrEnum):    # addressable fields, for missing/conflict reporting
    RELATIONSHIP="relationship"; A1_AGE="applicant_1.age"; A2_AGE="applicant_2.age"
    A1_CITIZENSHIP="applicant_1.citizenship"; A2_CITIZENSHIP="applicant_2.citizenship"
    A1_PRIOR_HOUSING="applicant_1.prior_flat_or_subsidy"; A2_PRIOR_HOUSING="applicant_2.prior_flat_or_subsidy"
    A1_EMPLOYMENT="applicant_1.employment"; A2_EMPLOYMENT="applicant_2.employment"
    HFE_STATUS="hfe_status"; HFE_ISSUE_DATE="hfe_issue_date"
    PRIVATE_PROPERTY="private_property_interest"; HOUSING_LOAN_INTENT="housing_loan_intent"
    CHILDREN="children_or_expecting"

# ---- request / profile ------------------------------------------------------------
class UserRequest(BaseModel):
    request_id: str
    situation_text: str          # free text; fictional profiles only (UI warns)
    question: str

class Person(BaseModel):
    age: int | None = Field(None, ge=0, le=120)
    citizenship: Literal["SC", "SPR", "non_resident"] | None = None
    prior_flat_or_subsidy: bool | None = None      # drives first-timer status
    employment: Literal["employed", "self_employed", "not_working", "other"] | None = None  # Phase 2 aligns with HFE guide

class ApplicantProfile(BaseModel):
    """None = not provided. Never defaulted (REQ-ARC-013)."""
    relationship: Literal["married", "engaged", "other"] | None = None
    applicant_1: Person = Person()
    applicant_2: Person = Person()
    hfe_status: Literal["not_started", "preliminary_done", "applied", "issued"] | None = None
    hfe_issue_date: date | None = None
    private_property_interest: bool | None = None
    housing_loan_intent: Literal["hdb", "financial_institution", "undecided"] | None = None
    children_or_expecting: bool | None = None

class FieldQuote(BaseModel):
    field: ProfileField
    quote: str                    # verbatim span from situation_text

class StatedContradiction(BaseModel):
    field: ProfileField
    quotes: list[str] = Field(min_length=2)

class ProfileExtraction(BaseModel):            # LLM #1 output (schema-constrained)
    profile: ApplicantProfile
    quotes: list[FieldQuote]
    stated_contradictions: list[StatedContradiction]
    question_topics: list[Topic] = Field(min_length=1)

# ---- the four distinct signals -------------------------------------------------------
class MissingProfileField(BaseModel):
    field: ProfileField
    needed_for: list[str]         # topic values and/or rule_ids
    follow_up_question: str       # from a static template map (deterministic)

class ProfileConflict(BaseModel):
    fields: list[ProfileField]
    kind: Literal["stated_contradiction", "logical_inconsistency"]
    detail: str                   # e.g. "engaged, but described as spouse"
    quotes: list[str]
    clarification_question: str

class EvidenceGap(BaseModel):
    topic: Topic | None
    claim_id: str | None = None
    kind: Literal["no_evidence_for_topic", "claim_uncited", "claim_unsupported", "fact_temporally_uncertain"]
    detail: str
    official_source_url: str | None = None      # where to confirm

class OutOfScopeReason(BaseModel):
    code: Literal["excluded_topic", "unsupported_household_type", "unrecognised_question"]
    topic: Topic | None = None
    detail: str
    redirect_url: str | None = None             # official service/page

class ProfileAssessment(BaseModel):
    profile: ApplicantProfile                   # after quote guard
    missing_profile_fields: list[MissingProfileField]
    profile_conflicts: list[ProfileConflict]
    extraction_warnings: list[str]              # dropped unquoted fields, etc.

# ---- gate --------------------------------------------------------------------------
class CoverageDecision(BaseModel):
    status: Literal["in_scope", "partially_in_scope", "out_of_scope"]
    supported_topics: list[Topic]
    out_of_scope_reasons: list[OutOfScopeReason]

# ---- knowledge, rules, evidence --------------------------------------------------------
class PolicyFact(BaseModel):     # per 03 §2.5 (+ aliases, A2); loaded, never LLM-produced
    fact_id: str; statement: str; topic: Topic; scope_tier: Tier
    aliases: list[str] = []
    applies_to: dict[str, str] = {}; exceptions: list[str] = []
    source_id: str; source_url: HttpUrl; section: str
    retrieved_at: date; effective_from: date | None; effective_to: date | None
    validation_status: Literal["verified"]      # loader rejects anything else at runtime
    kb_version: str

class RuleResult(BaseModel):
    rule_id: str; rule_version: str
    status: Literal["applies", "not_applicable", "cannot_determine"]
    preparation_step: str | None                # only when status == "applies"
    source_fact_ids: list[str] = Field(min_length=1)
    missing_fields: list[ProfileField] = []     # required when cannot_determine
    requires_human_review: bool

class Evidence(BaseModel):
    fact_id: str; statement: str; source_url: HttpUrl; section: str
    origin: Literal["rule", "bm25"]
    bm25_score: float | None = None; rank: int | None = None

class EvidenceBundle(BaseModel):
    items: list[Evidence]
    query: str; k: int; kb_version: str
    evidence_gaps: list[EvidenceGap]

# ---- generation and verification ---------------------------------------------------------
class GeneratedClaim(BaseModel):
    claim_id: str
    text: str
    kind: Literal["policy_fact", "preparation_step", "caveat"]   # caveat = not checkable
    cited_fact_ids: list[str]

class GenerationOutput(BaseModel):              # LLM #2 output
    summary: str
    claims: list[GeneratedClaim]
    # Filled by the LLM only in configs A/B (same enums), from upstream in C/D (A6)
    missing_profile_fields: list[MissingProfileField] = []
    profile_conflicts: list[ProfileConflict] = []
    out_of_scope_reasons: list[OutOfScopeReason] = []

class VerificationResult(BaseModel):
    claim_id: str
    outcome: Literal["supported", "contradicted", "insufficient_evidence"]
    method: Literal["deterministic", "llm_judge"]

# Phase 2a — Source Discovery, MVP Mapping, Rights Review and Acquisition Plan

**Status: PROPOSED (2026-10-28). Awaiting developer review.** Nothing in this document has
been fetched, downloaded, captured or extracted. Proposed decisions are D-044 to D-055 in
[decisions.md](decisions.md#proposed-decisions-phase-2a-2026-10-28). They become requirements
only after approval.

**Inputs:**
- the source-discovery matrix in [02 §3](project_context/02_policy_sources.md), re-checked
  against the private project-approach PDF (APP p.4–12) on 2026-10-28;
- the scope in [01 §6](project_context/01_problem_and_scope.md) (D-008, D-013, D-033);
- the data and rights rules in [03](project_context/03_data_and_licensing.md);
- the contracts in [architecture.md §5](architecture.md).

**Why the PDF was reread:** the matrix is the critical input, so its original references had to
be confirmed. The reread found no loss in the Phase 0 extraction. Every row, exception, URL
and media item in 02 §3 matches the PDF. C-14 (Row 4's URL) is present in the original PDF,
so it was not introduced during extraction.

**Provenance tags** (as in [INDEX](project_context/INDEX.md#legend)):
- *matrix* = recorded in the developer's matrix;
- *unverified* = not yet checked against a frozen source;
- *agent knowledge* = from the coding agent's general knowledge. It is unverified and must be
  checked before use; it is never a fact.

**Contents:**
1. [Classification scheme](#1-classification-scheme)
2. [Reconciled source-discovery matrix](#2-reconciled-source-discovery-matrix)
3. [Source relationship and link inventory](#3-source-relationship-and-link-classification-inventory)
4. [Policy dependencies and exceptions](#4-policy-dependencies-and-exceptions)
5. [MVP source coverage matrix](#5-mvp-source-coverage-matrix)
6. [Non-text resources](#6-non-text-resources)
7. [Rights and access assessment](#7-rights-and-access-assessment)
8. [Source manifest schema](#8-source-manifest-schema)
9. [Corpus strategy](#9-corpus-strategy)
10. [Extraction method per approved source](#10-extraction-method-per-approved-source)
11. [Reviewer reproducibility](#11-reviewer-reproducibility-strategy)
12. [Coverage gaps and blockers](#12-source-and-policy-coverage-gaps)
13. [Recommended acquisition scope](#13-recommended-final-acquisition-scope)
14. [Risks, exclusions and approval decisions](#14-unresolved-risks-exclusions-and-approval-decisions)
15. [Requirement traceability](#15-requirement-traceability)

---

## 1. Classification scheme

| Class | Definition used here |
|---|---|
| **Essential** | Needed to implement **and** evaluate a Core area, or the only source for a Limited area that is planned. Without it, a supported rule has no verified source (REQ-SRC-013) |
| **Supporting** | Adds conditions, exceptions or process detail for an in-scope area, or serves a Limited area that has an Essential source elsewhere. Acquire only with item-level approval |
| **Context only** | Used only to explain the HFE ↔ grant/loan relationship, or as a redirect/link target. No facts beyond the relationship; no calculation (REQ-SCP-004) |
| **Outside MVP** | Excluded tier (D-008), out-of-scope household type (D-033) or income determination (D-013). It may still be a **redirect URL** for the coverage gate, but it is **not acquired** |
| **Pending** | The classification depends on content that hasn't been inspected yet, or on an open question. Neither acquired nor dropped until resolved |

**Source IDs:** stable and never reused.
- `S##` is a document: a page, PDF or external page.
- `S##.x` is a section inside a document: an accordion, anchor or note.
- `M##` is a non-text media item.

These IDs become `source_id` in `data/sources_manifest.json` (§8).

### 7.3 Rules carried into the plan

- **robots.txt is not a licence.** A permissive robots.txt only means automated access isn't
  disallowed. It grants no copyright permission.
- **Public is not the same as redistributable.** Nothing acquired is committed, and nothing is
  described as licensed.
- If the Terms of Use **prohibit automated access**, Playwright capture stops. The fallback is
  manual "save page" by the developer in a normal browser, recorded as `manual_rendered_dom`
  (REQ-SRC-006 allows manual extraction). This fallback only changes the access method. It
  does not resolve copyright, so storage and redistribution stay private.
- If robots.txt **disallows** a path, that page is not captured automatically. Manual
  inspection by the developer is a policy decision for the developer to make, recorded in
  decisions.md. It is not assumed.
- Every rights finding is stored in `rights_records` in the manifest (§8.2), with the check
  date and SHA-256 of the robots.txt or terms page.

## 9. Corpus strategy

### 9.1 Layers

| Layer | Content | Path | Git | Who uses it | Rights basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **L0** Raw snapshots | Rendered HTML of approved pages; approved PDFs; private copies of robots.txt and terms pages; capture logs | `data/private_corpus/raw/<source_id>/` | Ignored | Developer: provenance, re-audit | Local analysis only (§7) |
| **L1** Processed passages | Structured blocks: heading path, paragraph/list/table cells, link list, `passage_id`, `source_id`. Any local index built over them | `data/private_corpus/processed/` | Ignored | Developer: completeness audit, fact authoring, verification of facts | Local analysis only. Contains copied text |
| **L2** Authored KB | `policy_facts.jsonl` (paraphrased statements, fact IDs, source pointers by `source_id` and section, **no quotes**); `policy_rules.yaml` citing fact IDs | `data/` | Tracked after rights review | App, BM25, Docker, all evaluation | Own expression of facts |
| **L3** Metadata | `sources_manifest.json`, `source_coverage.csv`, `visual_resources.json`, rights notes | `data/`, `docs/` | Tracked | Reviewers, app (URL resolution, registry links) | URLs, titles, short headings, hashes: not substantial text |

### 9.2 How the reviewer-facing corpus supports the MVP without redistribution

- Every runtime claim cites a **fact ID**. The fact resolves to an **official URL and
  section** through the manifest (D-006), so reviewers check the claim against HDB's live page
  rather than against a redistributed copy.
- The fact records `retrieved_at`, plus `raw_sha256` through its source. That makes clear
  which version the fact describes, even though the snapshot itself isn't shared.
- Coverage is shown in `source_coverage.csv`. This is how the KB demonstrates the
  exceptions it represents, without exposing source text.

### 9.3 Rights review before an authored fact is tracked (proposed in D-054)

1. Paraphrase in independent wording: one condition per statement. Keep only proper names
   (scheme names), numbers, dates and durations, which are facts.
2. **Local overlap check:** a stdlib script in `scripts/` compares each statement with L1
   passages and flags any shared run of 8 or more consecutive words. Flagged statements are
   reworded. The script reads L1 locally and prints only IDs and counts.
3. `rights_review.status = cleared` only after steps 1–2 and a manual read.
4. The anonymity scan and the secret scan run before the commit is suggested.

### 9.4 Who reads L0 and L1

L0 and L1 are processed locally by scripts.

**Open point for approval (D-054):** whether the coding agent may read L1 to help author
facts. Doing so sends source text to the agent's model provider, an external LLM service.
CLAUDE.md requires approval for that. The rights position is **unresolved**, because the
computational data analysis exception limits supplying copies to others.

| Option | Cost |
|---|---|
| **(a) Recommended:** the developer reads L1 and drafts facts. The agent works only on authored drafts, schema, rules and checks | Slower authoring |
| (b) The agent reads L1 under an explicit, recorded approval | Faster. Carries the unresolved rights risk and must be disclosed |

---

## 10. Extraction method per approved source

All capture runs use `scripts/capture_sources.py` (D-042) with a **tracked allowlist**,
`data/capture_allowlist.json`. The allowlist lists approved `source_id` → URL pairs and is
derived from the approved manifest. The script refuses any URL that isn't on the allowlist.

**Common behaviour** (D-053, D-055):
- headless Chromium; one page at a time; a fixed delay between pages (at least 10 s, or the
  robots.txt `Crawl-delay` if larger);
- an honest user-agent string that identifies a research prototype;
- no login and no form submission;
- no link-following;
- `waitUntil: networkidle`, then expand every accordion control inside the main content area,
  recording the controls found and the controls expanded;
- save `page.content()` to L0;
- compute `raw_sha256`;
- serialise structure in-browser with `page.evaluate`: heading path, paragraphs, lists,
  tables (rows, cells, nested tables kept as children) and links (href and text). Output goes
  to L1 as JSONL, with `text_sha256`;
- no screenshots by default;
- no HTML-parsing dependency: the browser DOM does the parsing, so D-036/D-042 stay
  unchanged.

| Source | Method | Specific handling | Validation (REQ-SRC-012 checks) |
|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | Playwright DOM | Expand all category accordions and nested tables. Keep the category heading on every row (REQ-SRC-003). Tag S01.c–e, n3 and i rows as `outside_mvp` in L1; they are kept for the audit and never authored | Accordion count; table row/column spot-check against the rendered page; locate notes n1–n4; find the first-timer definition (G-05) |
| S02 | Playwright DOM | Expand When to apply, How to apply, Validity, Next steps. Record `<img>` src and alt for M00–M02 and the video links. Record outgoing links to S03, S10, S11 and S16 without following them | Check whether the M01 facts (Step-2 window, processing time, validity) appear in the **text** → resolves G-02 |
| S03 | Playwright DOM | Extract supporting-document lists and assessment-period text. Income-calculation passages are tagged `documentation_only` | HTML-equivalence check for S07/S08: does S03 list documents per employment category? |
| S04 | Playwright DOM | Expand all accordions, especially `cancellation`. Search for an "exceptions"/"waiver" heading | Resolves G-03 (S04.b location) |
| S05 | Playwright DOM (if approved) | Expand all. Author only S05.b and S05.c | Accordion count |
| S06 | Playwright DOM (if approved) | BTO section only is authored | — |
| S07, S08 | Direct HTTPS download (if approved after the check) | **No new dependency:** the developer validates the relevant pages manually and records page numbers in L1 by hand (D-052). OCR is not planned | Page and section refs in the manifest |
| S10, S11 | Not captured until Q-08 / G-02 is decided | If approved: Playwright DOM, single page, no sub-link following | — |
| M00–M04, S09, S12–S16 | Link only | Registry or redirect entry with the canonical URL | — |
| S17 | Never accessed | — | — |

**Manual fallback** (if the Terms of Use or robots.txt rule out automation): the developer
saves the rendered page from a normal browser after expanding every accordion by hand. The
same hashing and L1 serialisation then run on the saved file. The method is recorded as
`manual_rendered_dom`.

---

## 11. Reviewer reproducibility strategy

| Reviewer action | Needs | Doesn't need |
|---|---|---|
| `docker build` and `docker run`, or `uv sync` then `streamlit run` | Tracked L2 and L3 files; an LLM key, or committed predictions for offline scoring | L0, L1, Playwright, network access to HDB |
| Rebuild the BM25 index | `policy_facts.jsonl` (index built in memory at startup) | L1 |
| Re-score the evaluation offline | `evaluation/results/<run_id>/` predictions and labels | Any API key |
| Check a cited fact | The fact's `source_url` and section, opened in a browser | L0 |
| Optional: drift check | `--group capture`; the script re-captures the allowlisted pages and compares `text_sha256` with the manifest | — |

**What is and isn't claimed:**
- The app and the evaluation are reproducible from tracked files. A clean-machine test runs
  with `data/private_corpus/` absent (REQ-DAT-012, REQ-NFR-001; architecture §12).
- **Re-capturing pages later doesn't reproduce the frozen corpus.** HDB pages change without
  version identifiers. The drift check *detects* change against recorded hashes but can't
  restore the historical text (REQ-LIC-016).
- The README states the supported policy period as "HDB sources retrieved on <date range>;
  facts may not reflect later changes" (D-021). It never states an effective-date range that
  the sources don't give.

---

**Minimum set: 4 pages (the seeds).** Up to 6 pages with the two Supporting ones. Up to 8
artefacts if the conditional PDFs are needed. The final count is reported after coverage
validation (D-007).

## 1. Classification scheme

| Class | Definition used here |
|---|---|
| **Essential** | Needed to implement **and** evaluate a Core area, or the only source for a Limited area that is planned. Without it, a supported rule has no verified source (REQ-SRC-013) |
| **Supporting** | Adds conditions, exceptions or process detail for an in-scope area, or serves a Limited area that has an Essential source elsewhere. Acquire only with item-level approval |
| **Context only** | Used only to explain the HFE ↔ grant/loan relationship, or as a redirect/link target. No facts beyond the relationship; no calculation (REQ-SCP-004) |
| **Outside MVP** | Excluded tier (D-008), out-of-scope household type (D-033) or income determination (D-013). It may still be a **redirect URL** for the coverage gate, but it is **not acquired** |
| **Pending** | The classification depends on content that hasn't been inspected yet, or on an open question. Neither acquired nor dropped until resolved |

**Source IDs:** stable and never reused.
- `S##` is a document: a page, PDF or external page.
- `S##.x` is a section inside a document: an accordion, anchor or note.

### 7.3 Rules carried into the plan

- **robots.txt is not a licence.** A permissive robots.txt only means automated access isn't
  disallowed. It grants no copyright permission.
- **Public is not the same as redistributable.** Nothing acquired is committed, and nothing is
  described as licensed.
- If the Terms of Use **prohibit automated access**, Playwright capture stops. The fallback is
  manual "save page" by the developer in a normal browser, recorded as `manual_rendered_dom`
  (REQ-SRC-006 allows manual extraction). This fallback only changes the access method. It
  does not resolve copyright, so storage and redistribution stay private.
- If robots.txt **disallows** a path, that page is not captured automatically. Manual
  inspection by the developer is a policy decision for the developer to make, recorded in
  decisions.md. It is not assumed.
- Every rights finding is stored in `rights_records` in the manifest (§8.2), with the check
  date and SHA-256 of the robots.txt or terms page.

## 9. Corpus strategy

### 9.1 Layers

| Layer | Content | Path | Git | Who uses it | Rights basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **L0** Raw snapshots | Rendered HTML of approved pages; approved PDFs; private copies of robots.txt and terms pages; capture logs | `data/private_corpus/raw/<source_id>/` | Ignored | Developer: provenance, re-audit | Local analysis only (§7) |
| **L1** Processed passages | Structured blocks: heading path, paragraph/list/table cells, link list, `passage_id`, `source_id`. Any local index built over them | `data/private_corpus/processed/` | Ignored | Developer: completeness audit, fact authoring, verification of facts | Local analysis only. Contains copied text |
| **L2** Authored KB | `policy_facts.jsonl` (paraphrased statements, fact IDs, source pointers by `source_id` and section, **no quotes**); `policy_rules.yaml` citing fact IDs | `data/` | Tracked after rights review | App, BM25, Docker, all evaluation | Own expression of facts |
| **L3** Metadata | `sources_manifest.json`, `source_coverage.csv`, `visual_resources.json`, rights notes | `data/`, `docs/` | Tracked | Reviewers, app (URL resolution, registry links) | URLs, titles, short headings, hashes: not substantial text |

### 9.2 How the reviewer-facing corpus supports the MVP without redistribution

- Every runtime claim cites a **fact ID**. The fact resolves to an **official URL and
  section** through the manifest (D-006), so reviewers check the claim against HDB's live page
  rather than against a redistributed copy.
- The fact records `retrieved_at`, plus `raw_sha256` through its source. That makes clear
  which version the fact describes, even though the snapshot itself isn't shared.
- Coverage is shown in `source_coverage.csv`. This is how the KB demonstrates the
  exceptions it represents, without exposing source text.

### 9.3 Rights review before an authored fact is tracked (proposed in D-054)

1. Paraphrase in independent wording: one condition per statement. Keep only proper names
   (scheme names), numbers, dates and durations, which are facts.
2. **Local overlap check:** a stdlib script in `scripts/` compares each statement with L1
   passages and flags any shared run of 8 or more consecutive words. Flagged statements are
   reworded. The script reads L1 locally and prints only IDs and counts.
3. `rights_review.status = cleared` only after steps 1–2 and a manual read.
4. The anonymity scan and the secret scan run before the commit is suggested.

### 9.4 Who reads L0 and L1

L0 and L1 are processed locally by scripts.

**Open point for approval (D-054):** whether the coding agent may read L1 to help author
facts. Doing so sends source text to the agent's model provider, an external LLM service.
CLAUDE.md requires approval for that. The rights position is **unresolved**, because the
computational data analysis exception limits supplying copies to others.

| Option | Cost |
|---|---|
| **(a) Recommended:** the developer reads L1 and drafts facts. The agent works only on authored drafts, schema, rules and checks | Slower authoring |
| (b) The agent reads L1 under an explicit, recorded approval | Faster. Carries the unresolved rights risk and must be disclosed |

---

## 10. Extraction method per approved source

All capture runs use `scripts/capture_sources.py` (D-042) with a **tracked allowlist**,
`data/capture_allowlist.json`. The allowlist lists approved `source_id` → URL pairs and is
derived from the approved manifest. The script refuses any URL that isn't on the allowlist.

**Common behaviour** (D-053, D-055):
- headless Chromium; one page at a time; a fixed delay between pages (at least 10 s, or the
  robots.txt `Crawl-delay` if larger);
- an honest user-agent string that identifies a research prototype;
- no login and no form submission;
- no link-following;
- `waitUntil: networkidle`, then expand every accordion control inside the main content area,
  recording the controls found and the controls expanded;
- save `page.content()` to L0;
- compute `raw_sha256`;
- serialise structure in-browser with `page.evaluate`: heading path, paragraphs, lists,
  tables (rows, cells, nested tables kept as children) and links (href and text). Output goes
  to L1 as JSONL, with `text_sha256`;
- no screenshots by default;
- no HTML-parsing dependency: the browser DOM does the parsing, so D-036/D-042 stay
  unchanged.

Tag S01.c–e, n3 and i rows as `outside_mvp` in L1; they are kept for the audit and never authored | Accordion count; table row/column spot-check against the rendered page; locate notes n1–n4; find the first-timer definition (G-05) |
| S02 | Playwright DOM | Expand When to apply, How to apply, Validity, Next steps. Record `<img>` src and alt for M00–M02 and the video links. | S03 | Playwright DOM | Extract supporting-document lists and assessment-period text. Income-calculation passages are tagged `documentation_only` | HTML-equivalence check for S07/S08: does S03 list documents per employment category? |
| S04 | Playwright DOM | Expand all accordions, especially `cancellation`. Search for an "exceptions"/"waiver" heading | Resolves G-03 (S04.b location) |
| S05 | Playwright DOM (if approved) | Expand all. Author only S05.b and S05.c | Accordion count |
| S06 | Playwright DOM (if approved) | BTO section only is authored | — |

**Manual fallback** (if the Terms of Use or robots.txt rule out automation): the developer
saves the rendered page from a normal browser after expanding every accordion by hand. The
same hashing and L1 serialisation then run on the saved file. The method is recorded as
`manual_rendered_dom`.

## 11. Reviewer reproducibility strategy

| Reviewer action | Needs | Doesn't need |
|---|---|---|
| `docker build` and `docker run`, or `uv sync` then `streamlit run` | Tracked L2 and L3 files; an LLM key, or committed predictions for offline scoring | L0, L1, Playwright, network access to HDB |
| Rebuild the BM25 index | `policy_facts.jsonl` (index built in memory at startup) | L1 |
| Re-score the evaluation offline | `evaluation/results/<run_id>/` predictions and labels | Any API key |
| Check a cited fact | The fact's `source_url` and section, opened in a browser | L0 |
| Optional: drift check | `--group capture`; the script re-captures the allowlisted pages and compares `text_sha256` with the manifest | — |

**What is and isn't claimed:**
- The app and the evaluation are reproducible from tracked files. A clean-machine test runs
  with `data/private_corpus/` absent (REQ-DAT-012, REQ-NFR-001; architecture §12).
- **Re-capturing pages later doesn't reproduce the frozen corpus.** HDB pages change without
  version identifiers. The drift check *detects* change against recorded hashes but can't
  restore the historical text (REQ-LIC-016).
- The README states the supported policy period as "HDB sources retrieved on <date range>;

### 7.3 Rules carried into the plan

- **robots.txt is not a licence.** A permissive robots.txt only means automated access isn't
  disallowed. It grants no copyright permission.
- **Public is not the same as redistributable.** Nothing acquired is committed, and nothing is
  described as licensed.
- If the Terms of Use **prohibit automated access**, Playwright capture stops. The fallback is
  manual "save page" by the developer in a normal browser, recorded as `manual_rendered_dom`
  (REQ-SRC-006 allows manual extraction). This fallback only changes the access method. It
  does not resolve copyright, so storage and redistribution stay private.
- If robots.txt **disallows** a path, that page is not captured automatically. Manual
  inspection by the developer is a policy decision for the developer to make, recorded in
  decisions.md. It is not assumed.
- Every rights finding is stored in `rights_records` in the manifest (§8.2), with the check
  date and SHA-256 of the robots.txt or terms page.

## 9. Corpus strategy

### 9.1 Layers

| Layer | Content | Path | Git | Who uses it | Rights basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **L0** Raw snapshots | Rendered HTML of approved pages; approved PDFs; private copies of robots.txt and terms pages; capture logs | `data/private_corpus/raw/<source_id>/` | Ignored | Developer: provenance, re-audit | Local analysis only (§7) |
| **L1** Processed passages | Structured blocks: heading path, paragraph/list/table cells, link list, `passage_id`, `source_id`. Any local index built over them | `data/private_corpus/processed/` | Ignored | Developer: completeness audit, fact authoring, verification of facts | Local analysis only. Contains copied text |
| **L2** Authored KB | `policy_facts.jsonl` (paraphrased statements, fact IDs, source pointers by `source_id` and section, **no quotes**); `policy_rules.yaml` citing fact IDs | `data/` | Tracked after rights review | App, BM25, Docker, all evaluation | Own expression of facts |
| **L3** Metadata | `sources_manifest.json`, `source_coverage.csv`, `visual_resources.json`, rights notes | `data/`, `docs/` | Tracked | Reviewers, app (URL resolution, registry links) | URLs, titles, short headings, hashes: not substantial text |

### 9.2 How the reviewer-facing corpus supports the MVP without redistribution

- Every runtime claim cites a **fact ID**. The fact resolves to an **official URL and
  section** through the manifest (D-006), so reviewers check the claim against HDB's live page
  rather than against a redistributed copy.
- The fact records `retrieved_at`, plus `raw_sha256` through its source. That makes clear
  which version the fact describes, even though the snapshot itself isn't shared.
- Coverage is shown in `source_coverage.csv`. This is how the KB demonstrates the
  exceptions it represents, without exposing source text.

### 9.3 Rights review before an authored fact is tracked (proposed in D-054)

1. Paraphrase in independent wording: one condition per statement. Keep only proper names
   (scheme names), numbers, dates and durations, which are facts.
2. **Local overlap check:** a stdlib script in `scripts/` compares each statement with L1
   passages and flags any shared run of 8 or more consecutive words. Flagged statements are
   reworded. The script reads L1 locally and prints only IDs and counts.
3. `rights_review.status = cleared` only after steps 1–2 and a manual read.
4. The anonymity scan and the secret scan run before the commit is suggested.

### 9.4 Who reads L0 and L1

L0 and L1 are processed locally by scripts.

**Open point for approval (D-054):** whether the coding agent may read L1 to help author
facts. Doing so sends source text to the agent's model provider, an external LLM service.
CLAUDE.md requires approval for that. The rights position is **unresolved**, because the
computational data analysis exception limits supplying copies to others.

| Option | Cost |
|---|---|
| **(a) Recommended:** the developer reads L1 and drafts facts. The agent works only on authored drafts, schema, rules and checks | Slower authoring |
| (b) The agent reads L1 under an explicit, recorded approval | Faster. Carries the unresolved rights risk and must be disclosed |

## 10. Extraction method per approved source

All capture runs use `scripts/capture_sources.py` (D-042) with a **tracked allowlist**,
`data/capture_allowlist.json`. The allowlist lists approved `source_id` → URL pairs and is
derived from the approved manifest. The script refuses any URL that isn't on the allowlist.

**Common behaviour** (D-053, D-055):
- headless Chromium; one page at a time; a fixed delay between pages (at least 10 s, or the
  robots.txt `Crawl-delay` if larger);
- an honest user-agent string that identifies a research prototype;
- no login and no form submission;
- no link-following;
- `waitUntil: networkidle`, then expand every accordion control inside the main content area,
  recording the controls found and the controls expanded;
- save `page.content()` to L0;
- compute `raw_sha256`;
- serialise structure in-browser with `page.evaluate`: heading path, paragraphs, lists,
  tables (rows, cells, nested tables kept as children) and links (href and text). Output goes
  to L1 as JSONL, with `text_sha256`;
- no screenshots by default;
- no HTML-parsing dependency: the browser DOM does the parsing, so D-036/D-042 stay
  unchanged.

| Source | Method | Specific handling | Validation (REQ-SRC-012 checks) |
|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | Playwright DOM | Expand all category accordions and nested tables. Keep the category heading on every row (REQ-SRC-003). Tag S01.c–e, n3 and i rows as `outside_mvp` in L1; they are kept for the audit and never authored | Accordion count; table row/column spot-check against the rendered page; locate notes n1–n4; find the first-timer definition (G-05) |
| S02 | Playwright DOM | Expand When to apply, How to apply, Validity, Next steps. Record `<img>` src and alt for M00–M02 and the video links. Record outgoing links to S03, S10, S11 and S16 without following them | Check whether the M01 facts (Step-2 window, processing time, validity) appear in the **text** → resolves G-02 |
| S03 | Playwright DOM | Extract supporting-document lists and assessment-period text. Income-calculation passages are tagged `documentation_only` | HTML-equivalence check for S07/S08: does S03 list documents per employment category? |
| S04 | Playwright DOM | Expand all accordions, especially `cancellation`. Search for an "exceptions"/"waiver" heading | Resolves G-03 (S04.b location) |
| S05 | Playwright DOM (if approved) | Expand all. Author only S05.b and S05.c | Accordion count |
| S06 | Playwright DOM (if approved) | BTO section only is authored | — |

## 11. Reviewer reproducibility strategy

| Reviewer action | Needs | Doesn't need |
|---|---|---|
| `docker build` and `docker run`, or `uv sync` then `streamlit run` | Tracked L2 and L3 files; an LLM key, or committed predictions for offline scoring | L0, L1, Playwright, network access to HDB |
| Rebuild the BM25 index | `policy_facts.jsonl` (index built in memory at startup) | L1 |
| Re-score the evaluation offline | `evaluation/results/<run_id>/` predictions and labels | Any API key |
| Check a cited fact | The fact's `source_url` and section, opened in a browser | L0 |
| Optional: drift check | `--group capture`; the script re-captures the allowlisted pages and compares `text_sha256` with the manifest | — |

**What is and isn't claimed:**
- The app and the evaluation are reproducible from tracked files. A clean-machine test runs
  with `data/private_corpus/` absent (REQ-DAT-012, REQ-NFR-001; architecture §12).
- **Re-capturing pages later doesn't reproduce the frozen corpus.** HDB pages change without
  version identifiers. The drift check *detects* change against recorded hashes but can't
  restore the historical text (REQ-LIC-016).
- The README states the supported policy period as "HDB sources retrieved on <date range>;
  facts may not reflect later changes" (D-021). It never states an effective-date range that
  the sources don't give.

attachment.content: - anthropic-skills:computer-use: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.

# BTO Buddy — Project Context Index

This is a structured, traceable knowledge base built from the project's two private planning
sources:
- the **assessment brief** (`[ASM p.N]`);
- the **project-approach document** (`[APP p.N]`).

Both PDFs are kept locally and are Git-ignored. This documentation is independently
authored: it paraphrases requirements and policy content rather than reproducing them.

**Status (2026-10-28):** Phase 0 (context) and Phase 1 (setup and architecture) are complete.
**Next:** Phase 2 (policy sources); see the
[development log handoff](../development_log.md#phase-2--policy-sources-handoff).

**What exists:**
- the uv project and lockfile;
- a Streamlit entry-point shell;
- one smoke test;
- the Docker image.

No pipeline modules, data files, model choice or datasets exist yet.

## Files

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [01_problem_and_scope.md](01_problem_and_scope.md) | Final idea, problem statement, research question, problem validation, **MVP scope**, HFE/income boundaries, supported-question draft, missing-information categories, demo archetypes |
| [02_policy_sources.md](02_policy_sources.md) | Seed sources, discovery method, **complete source-discovery matrix**, infographic/video registry candidates, **media-handling decisions**, policy nuances to verify |
| [03_data_and_licensing.md](03_data_and_licensing.md) | Datasets A/B/C, private vs reviewer-facing corpora, manifest, schemas, completeness checks, licensing/robots/copyright, privacy, reproducibility, limitations |
| [04_architecture.md](04_architecture.md) | Pipeline, coverage gate, missing-information contract, representation principles, verifier behaviour, proposed stack, provider comparison, model scorecard |
| [05_evaluation.md](05_evaluation.md) | Configurations A–D, **benchmark structure**, label protocol, proposed split, **metric definitions**, severity rubric, retrieval and verifier evaluation, statistics, failure taxonomy |
| [06_submission_requirements.md](06_submission_requirements.md) | Mandatory deliverables, scoring dimensions, non-compliance indicators, resources, AI-log rules, README requirements |
| [requirements_register.md](requirements_register.md) | **All requirement IDs** with source pages, components and acceptance evidence; contradictions; open questions; completeness audit |
| [../decisions.md](../decisions.md) | Decision log (D-001 onward, BD-00…BD-09) and the instruction priority |
| [../architecture.md](../architecture.md) | **Approved implementation design** (D-030 to D-040): pipeline, contracts, retrieval choice, dependencies, tests |
| [../development_log.md](../development_log.md) | Progress per phase, verified commands, failures, next steps |
| [../../CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md) | Working instructions for coding agents (scope, invariants, Git workflow, commands) |

## Legend

**Status**

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `MANDATORY` | Explicit requirement in the assessment brief |
| `APPROVED` | Final project decision (in the project approach as final, or ratified/added in [decisions.md](../decisions.md)) |
| `PROPOSED` | Technical alternative or implementation detail not yet approved |
| `OPEN` | Cannot be resolved from the sources or decisions; needs a developer answer |
| `HISTORICAL` / `SUPERSEDED` | Earlier idea or decision replaced by an approved one. Kept for traceability, **not** an active requirement |

**Provenance**

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `COPIED-SOURCE` | The project-approach PDF quoted HDB text verbatim at this point. The quotation is **not** reproduced in tracked files |
| `AUTHORED-FACT (unverified)` | Independently paraphrased policy statement. It must be verified against a frozen source before it enters `data/policy_facts.jsonl` |
| `PROJECT-DECISION` | Design choice by the developer (the default for non-policy content) |
| *Author observation* | Point raised while building this knowledge base, not stated in either source |

## Instruction priority (D-001)
1. Mandatory assessment requirements.
2. The developer's latest explicit instructions and approved decisions.
3. Finalised scope, architecture, data strategy and evaluation methodology.
4. The current approved implementation task.
5. Proposed alternatives and open questions.
6. Historical or superseded brainstorming.

## Where to look for a task
| Task | Read |
|---|---|
| Any task | `CLAUDE.md`, then this index |
| Scope questions | 01, plus D-008 / D-013 / D-033 in [decisions](../decisions.md) |
| Source capture, extraction, facts | 02, 03, [architecture §5](../architecture.md) |
| Pipeline code | [architecture.md](../architecture.md) (§3 stages, §5 contracts, §11 modules, §12 tests), 04 |
| Benchmark and evaluation | 05, register (REQ-EVL-*) |
| README and submission | 06, register (REQ-SUB-*, REQ-DOC-*) |
| History and current state | [development_log.md](../development_log.md) |

## Current open items
- **Contradictions open:**
  - C-14 (URL mismatch in the matrix, Q-24);
  - C-15 and C-16 (metric gaps, Q-16 and Q-15);
  - C-17 (privacy missing from the scorecard, Q-13).
- **Questions open:**

  | Needed by | Questions |
  |---|---|
  | Phase 2 | Q-06, Q-07, Q-08, Q-09, Q-11, Q-22, Q-24 |
  | Model selection | Q-13 |
  | Before evaluation | Q-14, Q-15, Q-16, Q-17 |
  | Before dataset creation | Q-20, Q-21 |

- **Resolved:** Q-05, Q-10, Q-12, Q-18, Q-23.
- **Awaiting confirmation:** the `llm.py` addition in D-041.
- **Execution risk:** C-09 / Q-19 (log anonymity vs completeness).

# BTO Buddy — Project Context Index

This is a structured, traceable knowledge base built from the project's two private planning
sources:
- the **assessment brief** (`[ASM p.N]`);
- the **project-approach document** (`[APP p.N]`).

Both PDFs are kept locally and are Git-ignored. This documentation is independently
authored: it paraphrases requirements and policy content rather than reproducing them.

**Status (2026-10-28):** Phase 0 (context) and Phase 1 (setup and architecture) are complete.
Phase 2a (source discovery, MVP mapping, rights review and acquisition plan) is **drafted and
awaiting approval**: [../source_acquisition_plan.md](../source_acquisition_plan.md), with
proposed decisions D-044 to D-055. Nothing has been fetched or captured.

**What exists:**
- the uv project and lockfile;
- a Streamlit entry-point shell;
- one smoke test;
- the Docker image.

No pipeline modules, data files, model choice or datasets exist yet.

## Files

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [01_problem_and_scope.md](01_problem_and_scope.md) | Final idea, problem statement, research question, problem validation, **MVP scope**, HFE/income boundaries, supported-question draft, missing-information categories, demo archetypes |
| [02_policy_sources.md](02_policy_sources.md) | Seed sources, discovery method, **complete source-discovery matrix**, infographic/video registry candidates, **media-handling decisions**, policy nuances to verify |
| [03_data_and_licensing.md](03_data_and_licensing.md) | Datasets A/B/C, private vs reviewer-facing corpora, manifest, schemas, completeness checks, licensing/robots/copyright, privacy, reproducibility, limitations |
| [04_architecture.md](04_architecture.md) | Pipeline, coverage gate, missing-information contract, representation principles, verifier behaviour, proposed stack, provider comparison, model scorecard |
| [05_evaluation.md](05_evaluation.md) | Configurations A–D, **benchmark structure**, label protocol, proposed split, **metric definitions**, severity rubric, retrieval and verifier evaluation, statistics, failure taxonomy |
| [06_submission_requirements.md](06_submission_requirements.md) | Mandatory deliverables, scoring dimensions, non-compliance indicators, resources, AI-log rules, README requirements |
| [requirements_register.md](requirements_register.md) | **All requirement IDs** with source pages, components and acceptance evidence; contradictions; open questions; completeness audit |
| [../decisions.md](../decisions.md) | Decision log (D-001 onward, BD-00…BD-09) and the instruction priority |
| [../architecture.md](../architecture.md) | **Approved implementation design** (D-030 to D-040): pipeline, contracts, retrieval choice, dependencies, tests |
| [../source_acquisition_plan.md](../source_acquisition_plan.md) | **Phase 2a (PROPOSED):** reconciled matrix with source IDs, coverage matrix, link inventory, dependencies, rights assessment, manifest schema, corpus and extraction strategy, gaps, approval gates |
| [../development_log.md](../development_log.md) | Progress per phase, verified commands, failures, next steps |
| [../../CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md) | Working instructions for coding agents (scope, invariants, Git workflow, commands) |

## Legend

**Status**

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `MANDATORY` | Explicit requirement in the assessment brief |
| `APPROVED` | Final project decision (in the project approach as final, or ratified/added in [decisions.md](../decisions.md)) |
| `PROPOSED` | Technical alternative or implementation detail not yet approved |
| `OPEN` | Cannot be resolved from the sources or decisions; needs a developer answer |
| `HISTORICAL` / `SUPERSEDED` | Earlier idea or decision replaced by an approved one. Kept for traceability, **not** an active requirement |

**Provenance**

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `COPIED-SOURCE` | The project-approach PDF quoted HDB text verbatim at this point. The quotation is **not** reproduced in tracked files |
| `AUTHORED-FACT (unverified)` | Independently paraphrased policy statement. It must be verified against a frozen source before it enters `data/policy_facts.jsonl` |
| `PROJECT-DECISION` | Design choice by the developer (the default for non-policy content) |
| *Author observation* | Point raised while building this knowledge base, not stated in either source |

## Instruction priority (D-001)
1. Mandatory assessment requirements.
2. The developer's latest explicit instructions and approved decisions.
3. Finalised scope, architecture, data strategy and evaluation methodology.
4. The current approved implementation task.
5. Proposed alternatives and open questions.
6. Historical or superseded brainstorming.

# Development Log

Chronological record of completed work, decisions, failures and next steps. Decisions
themselves live in [decisions.md](decisions.md). Requirement IDs are in
[project_context/requirements_register.md](project_context/requirements_register.md).

---

## Phase 0 — Context building (2026-10-27 → 2026-10-28) — complete

**Done:**
- Reviewed both private planning PDFs page by page, including all 11 embedded images.
- Built the `docs/project_context/` knowledge base: 150 requirement IDs, a source-discovery
  matrix, the evaluation design, and a completeness audit (register §4).
- The developer resolved contradictions C-01 to C-13 (D-001 to D-025).
- Created `.gitignore` (private PDFs, private corpus, secrets) and private submission notes.
- Commit `c49555f docs: establish project context and requirements`.
- Context-extraction method (for re-audits): text via pdfplumber; every embedded image cropped
  at 300 dpi and read visually; non-default text colours checked to locate verbatim HDB quotes.

**Found:**
- New contradictions C-14 to C-17.
- Open questions Q-05 to Q-24.
- All policy facts quoted in the approach document are **unverified** until Phase 2.

## Phase 1 — Project setup and architecture (2026-10-28) — complete

### Chronology
| Step | Outcome | Decisions | Commit (by developer) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scaffold and agent instructions | `CLAUDE.md`, `pyproject.toml` (src layout), package, smoke test, placeholder README | D-026 (production infra out of scope), D-027 (developer runs all commits/pushes; agent suggests) | `e163bdd chore: initialise project and tooling` |
| Lockfile and tooling | uv with committed `uv.lock`; dev tools in a PEP 735 `dev` group | D-028 | (in `e163bdd`) |
| Docker | Agent install failed (needs `sudo`); developer installed Docker Desktop. Docker 29.9.2 verified | — | — |
| Architecture review | Held draft (D-029) replaced by a full review; A1–A11 approved → [architecture.md](architecture.md) | D-030 to D-040; Q-05, Q-10, Q-12, Q-23 resolved | `0cca98b docs: approve architecture and record design decisions` |
| Schedule | Target 2026-10-29 07:00; effort estimate is reference only; all of A–D planned | D-043 | (in `0cca98b`, as notes) |
| Repository and tooling setup | Developer's structure adopted, simplified; Streamlit entry point, `Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`, `.env.example`, `.streamlit/config.toml` (telemetry off), merged `.gitignore`; Ruff excludes `docs/` (it formats Python blocks inside Markdown) | D-041 | `36531ae chore: add Streamlit entry point, Docker and environment tooling` |
| Capture tooling | Playwright in opt-in `capture` group; Chromium headless shell in user cache; offline launch test only | D-042 | `910eb78 chore: add opt-in Playwright capture dependency group` |

### Final verified state (re-run 2026-10-28, macOS, Python 3.13.2, uv 0.13.6, Docker 29.9.2)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `uv sync` / `uv lock --check` | OK. 54 packages locked (49 in the default env; Playwright only with `--group capture`) |
| `uv run ruff check .` / `uv run ruff format --check .` | All checks passed / 5 files formatted |
| `uv run mypy` (strict) | No issues in 2 source files |
| `uv run pytest` | **1 passed** (`tests/test_smoke.py`: app renders, title, version, disclaimer) |
| `docker build -t bto-buddy .` | OK (image ≈ 820 MB; Streamlit brings numpy, pandas, pyarrow) |
| `docker run -p 8501:8501 --env-file .env.example bto-buddy` | Docker HEALTHCHECK `healthy` in ~8 s; `/_stcore/health` returns `ok` |
| Image contents (checked at setup) | Non-root `app`; `/app` = `.venv`, `.streamlit`, `app.py`; no PDFs, `.env`, `references/`, `private_corpus` |
| Git hygiene | Working tree clean; no private or secret files tracked; `git check-ignore` covers `.env`, private corpus, `references/private/`, caches, `tmp/`, logs, Streamlit secrets; anonymity scan clean |

**What exists in code:** only `src/bto_buddy/__init__.py` and `app.py` (a shell with a disclaimer
and privacy notice; it says the pipeline isn't available yet), plus one smoke test. No pipeline
modules, data files, prompts, model choice or datasets exist yet.

### Unresolved issues carried forward
| Item | Needed by | Where |
|---|---|---|
| D-041: confirm the `llm.py` addition | Before pipeline code | [decisions.md](decisions.md) |
| C-14 / Q-24: the matrix's BTO-process row cites the HFE page URL | Phase 2 | register §2–3; 02 Row 4 |
| Q-06, Q-07: SC+SPR premium and resale-levy tiers | Phase 2 | 02 Row 1 |
| Q-08: HFE FAQ sub-links and the "exceptions and waivers" source | Phase 2 | 02 Rows 2, 5 |
| Q-09: strip `si=` from video URLs (minor) | Phase 2 | 02 Row 2 |
| Q-11: any experiment on the private corpus? (register still says "Phase 1"; carried to Phase 2) | Phase 2 | 03 §2.2 |
| Q-22: `policy_facts` field-level schema | Phase 2 | 03 §2.5; architecture §5 |
| robots.txt and Terms of Use checks; Copyright Act ss 243–244 verification (D-024) | Before any capture | 03 §5.1 |
| Supported policy period (D-021) | After capture | 03 §2.8 |
| Q-13 / C-17: privacy criterion in model scorecard; model and judge-model selection | Model selection | 04 §6.3 |
| Q-14, Q-15/C-16, Q-16/C-15, Q-17: claim annotation guide, "answer coverage", human-review burden, scorer | Before evaluation | 05 §4 |
| Q-20, Q-21: benchmark split (proposed 18/30) and verifier claim set (proposed 60) | Before dataset creation | 05 §3.3, §6.1 |
| Q-19 / C-09: log anonymity vs completeness | Pre-submission | 06 §7 |
| All policy facts in the context docs remain **AUTHORED-FACT (unverified)** | Phase 2 | 02 §5 |

## Phase 2 — Policy sources (handoff)

**Goal (D-007):** determine the **minimum source set** for the MVP and turn verified content
into the reviewer-facing knowledge base. Nothing is included just because it appears in the
matrix.

**Read first:**
1. [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md);
2. [INDEX.md](project_context/INDEX.md);
3. [02_policy_sources.md](project_context/02_policy_sources.md) (matrix, media handling,
   facts to verify);
4. [03_data_and_licensing.md](project_context/03_data_and_licensing.md) (corpora, manifest,
   completeness checks, rights);
5. [architecture.md §5](architecture.md) (contracts, `PolicyFact`).

**Gates the developer must approve, in order:**
1. **Page list for capture.** Seeds plus any linked sources justified by the MVP tiers, with
   C-14 and Q-06 to Q-08 resolved.
2. **Rights check before fetching:** robots.txt and Terms of Use for each host. Never claim a
   redistribution licence.
3. **Capture run:** Playwright (`--group capture`), approved pages only. No crawling,
   link-following or transactional pages. Output goes to `data/private_corpus/raw/`
   (Git-ignored), with SHA-256 and timestamps in `data/sources_manifest.json`.
4. **Extraction and completeness audit:** 8 checks (03 §2.7), output to
   `data/private_corpus/processed/`, plus `data/source_coverage.csv`.
5. **Authoring:** `data/policy_facts.jsonl` (independently authored, verified, rights-reviewed,
   with `aliases`) and `data/policy_rules.yaml` (declarative, D-038). Finalise Q-22.
