I've written the Phase 2a plan in [docs/source_acquisition_plan.md](docs/source_acquisition_plan.md), but the rights assessment is still incomplete. Nothing was fetched, downloaded, captured or extracted, so every permission (robots.txt, Terms of Use, Copyright Act ss 243–244) is marked **UNRESOLVED**. Wherever I relied on my own general knowledge, it's labelled as unverified.

I reread pages 4–12 of the private approach PDF to confirm the matrix's original references. The Phase 0 extraction was complete. The URL mismatch in the BTO-process row (C-14) is in the original PDF too, so it wasn't introduced during extraction.

The plan covers all eight deliverables. It also:
- gives every source a stable ID (S01–S17 for documents, S01.a and similar for sections, M00–M04 for media);
- adds proposed decisions D-044 to D-055 to [decisions.md](docs/decisions.md);
- adds two new open questions, Q-25 and Q-26, to the register;
- updates the INDEX, the matrix pointer in 02 and the development log.

The anonymity and copied-text scans on the changed files came back clean.

**What I found:**
- **Minimum set: the 4 seed pages.** They cover all four Core areas, FT(PMC)/FPPS and cancellation. Priority Schemes (Family Care Scheme sections only) and Modes of Sale (BTO section only) are optional supporting pages. The two HFE guidance PDFs are needed only if the income-guidelines page doesn't list documents by employment type.
- **Non-selection depends on one missing source.** "Exceptions and waivers" has no URL. If it can't be found and verified, I propose cutting that area down to identify-and-link plus a stated evidence gap (D-048).
- **HFE timing may exist only in an infographic.** The 30-day window and processing time may appear only in an image. I recommend treating that as an evidence gap, which also gives a real extraction-gap test case (D-051).
- **First-timer definition not located yet.** It's needed for FT(PMC)/FPPS and the prior-ownership field; I expect it on the Couples and Families page.

**Conflicts I need you to decide:**
1. **PDF tool (D-052).** The approved PDF method (REQ-SRC-009) names PyMuPDF, but the approved dependency list (D-036/D-042) excludes it, and it's AGPL-licensed. I recommend no new dependency: check whether the HTML already carries the content, then validate at most two short PDFs by hand.
2. **Source text and external models (D-054).** If I read the extracted source text to help write facts, that text goes to my model provider. Whether the copyright exception allows that is unresolved. I recommend that you draft the facts from the private passages and I work only on your drafts.

**Your approvals, in order:**
1. **D-044 to D-055.** Most are straightforward:
   - D-045: the BTO-process row's main source is the Application page.
   - D-046: the SC+SPR premium and the resale levy are out of scope, link only.
   - D-047: a non-resident partner is treated as an out-of-scope household.
   - D-049: strip the `si=` tracking parameter from video URLs.
   - D-050: no experiment on the private corpus.
2. **Rights checks (plan §14.3).** Either you read the pages in a browser, or you approve me to fetch three things: `hdb.gov.sg/robots.txt`, HDB's Terms of Use, and ss 243–244 of the Copyright Act. Capture can't start until these are done.
3. **Capturing the 4 seed pages.**

These docs are a coherent unit and would make a good `docs:` commit, either now as a proposal or once you've approved the decisions. No private or secret files are involved.

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

entries.name: WebSearch
entries.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

Web search results for query: "Copyright Act 2021 Singapore section 244 computational data analysis conditions lawful access"

Links: [{"title":"lawpalyer logo","url":"https://lawplayer.com/sg/act/CA2021/244"},{"title":"conventuslaw.com","url":"https://conventuslaw.com/?p=113832"},{"title":"legal500.com","url":"https://legal500.com/developments/?p=38064"},{"title":"text and data mining in singapore","url":"https://www.reedsmith.com/articles/entertainment-and-media-guide-to-ai/text-and-data-mining-in-singapore/"},{"title":"text and data mining in singapore","url":"https://www.reedsmith.com/articles/text-and-data-mining-in-singapore/"},{"title":"“We Don’t Need Permission to Dance”: Key Features of the New Copyright Act 2021","url":"https://lawgazette.com.sg/?p=10621"},{"title":"singapore copyright infringement defence for ai machine learning","url":"https://conventuslaw.com/report/singapore-copyright-infringement-defence-for-ai-machine-learning/"},{"title":"copyright infringement defence for ai machine learning","url":"https://www.mondaq.com/copyright/1432048/copyright-infringement-defence-for-ai-machine-learning"},{"title":"copyright infringement defence for ai machine learning","url":"https://webiis08.mondaq.com/copyright/1432048/copyright-infringement-defence-for-ai-machine-learning"},{"title":"Computational data analysis exception in Singapore’s Copyright Act 2021 a game changer","url":"https://asiaiplaw.com/index.php/sector/it-telecoms/computational-data-analysis-exception-in-singapores-copyright-act-2021-a-game-changer"}]

The search turned up the statutory structure and commentary, but not the full text of the five conditions in section 244(2).

- **Basic rule:** Under section 244(1), making a copy of a work or a protected performance recording is a permitted use if the conditions in subsection (2) are met. 244.—(1) If the conditions in subsection (2) are met, it is a permitted use for a person (X) to make a copy of any of the following material
- **Purpose condition:** The copy must be made for computational data analysis or for preparing the material for it. the copy is made for the purpose of —(i) computational data analysis; or (ii) preparing the work or recording for computational data analysis
- **Use and sharing limits:** The copier may not use the copy for other purposes, and may share it only to verify results or for collaborative research related to the analysis. X does not use the copy for any other purpose
- **Lawful access:** Commentary says section 244(2)(d) covers lawful access and gives examples. Copyright Act 2021 S244(2)(d) provides illustrations of what "lawful access" means. "For example, if certain material can only be accessed through a paid subscription, the user cannot circumvent the paywall to access the material." A second example from the same source is that a user cannot gain access to material that is placed on a database by breaching the terms of use of the database.
- **Definition:** Section 243 defines "computational data analysis" to include using a computer program to identify, extract and analyse information or data from the work, and using the work as an example to improve a program's functioning. "(a) using a computer program to identify, extract and analyze information or data from the work or recording; and (b) using the work or recording as an example of a type of information or data to improve the functioning of a computer program in relation to that type of information or data."
- **Contract override:** One commentary states that neither can it be eliminated from nor modified in a contract.

Caveat: these are secondary sources, not the statute itself. The Reed Smith article is the only one that says section 244(2) sets out five conditions, and none of the results lists all five. Check the official text on Singapore Statutes Online before relying on the exact wording of any condition.

content.content:
Section 244 creates a permitted use allowing a person (X) to copy a work or a recording of a protected performance for computational data analysis (CDA). Under s 244(1), this applies only if the conditions in subsection (2) are met. Under s 244(3), "making a copy" includes storing or retaining it.

**The conditions in s 244(2)**

- **(a) Purpose:** The copy must be made for CDA, or to prepare the work or recording for CDA.
- **(b) No other use:** X must not use the copy for any other purpose.
- **(c) Limited supply:** X must not supply the copy to anyone, by communication or otherwise, except:
  - (i) to verify the results of the CDA X carried out, or
  - (ii) for collaborative research or study related to that CDA.
- **(d) Lawful access:** X must have lawful access to the source copy (the "first copy") from which the copy is made. The illustrations clarify this:
  - Access obtained by circumventing paywalls is not lawful access.
  - Access obtained in breach of a database's terms of use is not lawful access. Terms that are void under s 187 are disregarded.
- **(e) Status of the first copy:** One of three alternatives must apply:
  - (i) the first copy is not an infringing copy;
  - (ii) it is infringing, but X did not know this. If it came from a flagrantly infringing online location (whether or not that location is subject to an access-disabling order under s 325), X also neither knew nor could reasonably have known;
  - (iii) it is infringing, but using infringing copies is necessary for a "prescribed purpose," and X uses the copy only for CDA. The page does not say what the prescribed purposes are, so you would need the regulations.

**Related subsections**

- **Subsection (4):** X may communicate the work or recording to the public if the communication uses a copy made under subsection (1), and the same supply limits as in (2)(c) apply.
- **Subsection (5):** Supplying copies under this section is not treated as publishing the material. Such supply is also disregarded when determining the duration of copyright.

This is a summary of the text on the page, not legal advice. The page notes that later amendments may not be reflected, so check the official text on Singapore Statutes Online.

toolu_01Mj5nD7oZgndjE6ZRbr8zCj.prompt: Summarise section 187 Copyright Act 2021 (Singapore): which permitted uses (list them, especially whether computational data analysis s 244 is included) cannot be excluded or restricted by contract, and the effect (void). Short quotes under 25 words.

content.content:
**Section 187 (Copyright Act 2021)** makes certain contract terms void if they try to take away specified permitted uses.

**Permitted uses covered (s 187(1))**

A contract term is void to the extent it purports, directly or indirectly, to "exclude or restrict" any permitted use under:

- **Division 6 (public collections)**, except s 234, which covers supplying copies of published literary, dramatic or musical works or articles between libraries and archives.
- **Division 7 (computer programs)**.
- **Division 8 (computational data analysis)**. This division comprises ss 243–244, so **s 244 is included**. The page does not reproduce s 244's text, so this answer does not describe what it permits.
- **Division 17 (judicial proceedings and legal advice)**.

Permitted uses under other divisions, such as Division 2 (fair uses) and Division 3 (education), are not listed in this section.

**Specific acts (s 187(2))**

Without limiting subsection (1), a contract term is void to the extent it prevents or restricts these acts, where they constitute a permitted use under the provisions above:

- making a copy of a work or a recording of a protected performance;
- supplying a copy of a work or a recording of a performance, by communication or otherwise;
- performing a work or a recording of a protected performance.

**Timing (s 187(3))**

The section applies to contracts made before, on or after 21 November 2021.

**Effect**

The offending term is void, but only to the extent it excludes or restricts the protected permitted use. The page does not address what happens to the rest of the contract.

   permitted** under this basis. This firms up D-054.
6. **Authored facts** (own expression, no substantial copying) are unaffected.

## 10. Extraction method per approved source

> **Superseded in part by Gate R (§7.2a, revised D-055).** HDB returns 403 to automated
> clients, so **capture is manual**:
> 1. The developer opens each approved page in a normal browser, not logged in.
> 2. Clicks every accordion open.
> 3. In DevTools runs `copy(document.documentElement.outerHTML)` and saves the result as
>    `data/private_corpus/raw/<source_id>/<UTC timestamp>.html`. This takes the live DOM and
>    no image bytes. Chrome's "Save as… Complete" or a single-file save would also save the
>    infographics, so they are avoided.
> 4. Notes the time and how many accordions were opened.
>
> A local **offline** script (`scripts/register_snapshot.py`) then does the rest. It hashes the
> file, writes the manifest entry, counts expanded vs collapsed controls in the saved DOM, and
> serialises structure to L1 with Playwright `set_content` (JavaScript off, no network) or the
> stdlib parser.
>
> The automated-capture description below applies only if HDB later permits automated access.

(e) the first copy isn't infringing (or the stated exceptions apply). **s 187:** contract terms that exclude or restrict the Division 8 (CDA) permitted use are void | Secondary source; confirm against SSO when it's reachable |
+**Consequences:**
+1. **Automated capture is not available.** HDB's bot protection refuses both curl and headless
+   Chromium. Getting around it (spoofed user agent, stealth browser) is rejected: it is an
+   access control, and getting past it would undermine lawful access under s 244(2)(d).
+   Manual capture in a normal browser, which any member of the public can do, is the
+   primary method (revised D-055).
+2. **S10 is disallowed for crawlers.** It won't be acquired by any automated means. The
+   developer may still read it as a normal visitor to decide Q-08. Saving it stays a
+   separate approval.
+3. **Local L0/L1 copies:** s 244 is a plausible basis, given lawful (manual) access and use
+   for analysis only.
+4. **Committing copies to GitHub** is outside s 244(2)(c), so it stays **not permitted**.
+5. **Sending source text to an LLM provider** would be "supplying" a copy to a third party
+   for a purpose other than verifying results or collaborative research. It is **not
+   permitted** under this basis. This firms up D-054.
+6. **Authored facts** (own expression, no substantial copying) are unaffected.
### 7.3 Rules carried into the plan
- **robots.txt is not a licence.** A permissive robots.txt only means automated access isn't

content.text:
## D-047: I recommend reversing it

My first draft was wrong. D-033 puts any **first-timer couple (married or engaged)** in scope and doesn't exclude a couple because of citizenship. Treating an SC with a non-resident spouse or fiancé(e) as out of scope would have quietly cut Core scope. Which citizenship combination a couple has is itself one of the household-composition rules the assistant has to explain.

The revised D-047 (still proposed) says:
- **In scope:** SC + non-resident couples, with facts written only from the couple rows of the "families with non-residents" section of Couples and Families, and only where the conditions are explicit.
- **Fallback:** if those conditions turn out to be discretionary or too detailed to verify, the assistant names the situation, redirects to HDB and states an evidence gap.
- **Still out of scope:** non-resident parent or child households.
- **Unmatched combinations:** any citizenship combination with no matching section gets an evidence gap, never a determination.

It needs no extra capture, because that section is on a seed page.

## Rights check results

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| HDB robots.txt | All 4 seed pages, Priority Schemes, Modes of Sale and the PDF media path are **allowed**. `/hdb-flat-portal` is **disallowed**, which covers the HFE FAQ page, so I won't fetch it by any automated means. There's no crawl delay |
| HDB bot protection | Both curl and headless Chromium got **HTTP 403**, even with an honest user agent. The error pages are saved privately as evidence, with hashes |
| HDB Terms of Use | **Not read, still unresolved.** The page text loads with JavaScript, and the browser attempt got 403. HDB's terms for its separate mynicehome site limit use to personal, non-commercial purposes. That's a different site, so I haven't assumed the same terms apply |
| Copyright Act s 244 | It allows local copies made for computational analysis, on four conditions: no other use; no supply to others except to verify results or for collaborative research; **lawful access**; and a non-infringing source. Accessing in breach of terms of use isn't lawful access, unless s 187 voids the term. I read this from a secondary source because the official statutes site returned 403 |
| Copyright Act s 187 | Contract terms that restrict this exception are void |

What this means for the project:
- **Private corpus:** keeping local copies for analysis is plausible under s 244.
- **GitHub:** committing the copies is not covered by s 244.
- **LLM providers:** sending source text to a provider counts as supplying a copy to a third party, so that's ruled out as well. This firms up D-054.

## Capture: you should capture the seed pages manually

I can't capture them in line with the provenance rules. HDB actively blocks automated clients. The only way around that is to disguise the client, and that is ethically wrong. It would also undermine "lawful access", which is the basis for keeping local copies. A normal visit in your browser is plain public access, and the manual rendered-DOM method was approved from the start (REQ-SRC-006). I've revised D-055 to make it the main method.

For each of the 4 seed pages:
1. Open it in Chrome, not logged in, and click every accordion open.
2. Open DevTools → Console and run `copy(document.documentElement.outerHTML)`. This copies the page as currently shown, with the accordions open, and no images.
3. Paste it into `data/private_corpus/raw/S01/<UTC timestamp>.html`. Use S02 for the HFE page, S03 for Income Guidelines and S04 for Application for a New Flat.
4. Note the time and how many accordions you opened.

Don't use Chrome's "Save as… Complete" or a single-file save. Both would also save the infographic images.

I'll then write `scripts/register_snapshot.py`, which runs offline. For each file it records the hash and timestamp in the manifest, counts open vs closed sections as the completeness check, and splits the text into structured passages, all without network access. It prints only IDs, counts and hashes, so no source text reaches me.

**What I need from you:**
1. Read the HDB Terms of Use in your browser. Save that page and robots.txt the same way into `data/private_corpus/raw/rights/`, so I can summarise the terms and hash both files. Tell me first if the terms forbid copying or automated analysis.
2. Approve D-044 to D-055, including the revised D-047 and D-055.
3. Then do the 4 captures above.

The changes are in [source_acquisition_plan.md](docs/source_acquisition_plan.md) (§7.2a, §10, S01.e), [decisions.md](docs/decisions.md) and the [development log](docs/development_log.md). The private files are git-ignored, and the anonymity scan is clean.

Sources:
- [HDB robots.txt](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/robots.txt)
- [MyNiceHome Terms of Use](https://www.mynicehome.gov.sg/terms-of-use)
- [Copyright Act 2021 s 244 (lawplayer)](https://lawplayer.com/sg/act/CA2021/244)
- [Copyright Act 2021 s 187 (lawplayer)](https://lawplayer.com/sg/act/CA2021/187)
- [Reed Smith: Text and data mining in Singapore](https://www.reedsmith.com/articles/text-and-data-mining-in-singapore/)

content.text:
Your output shows the Couples and Families page is in good shape:

- **Rows 4–8 are the five applicant-category accordions.** Each panel is already in the page with 11.6k–12.8k characters, even when collapsed. Closing a section only hides it, so the exclusive behaviour doesn't affect capture.
- **Rows 0–3 are site navigation.** These are the Login button and menus. The page has no `<main>` element, so the script scanned the whole page. Ignore them.
- **The page also embeds about 144k characters of page data** (`__NEXT_DATA__`), which is probably the full page content. A single copy includes it, so it can serve as a second check.

There's one thing to verify. The source-discovery matrix lists FT(PMC) and FPPS as expandable sections on this page, but they aren't among the five controls the script found. They may be nested inside the category panels, or built with a widget that doesn't use the attribute the script looked for. If their content is in the page, a copy captures it anyway. The real risk is content that only loads when you click, and the procedure below tests for exactly that.

## Procedure for each of the 4 pages

**A. Default copy.** Load the page fresh, not logged in, and wait until it finishes loading. Run the step 1 script and paste the table to me. Then run:
```js
copy(document.documentElement.outerHTML)
```
Save it as `data/private_corpus/raw/S0n/<UTC timestamp>_default.html`.

**B. Expanded copy.** In the same tab, open everything you can see that expands, including nested sections like FT(PMC) and FPPS and any "read more" links. Order doesn't matter, and it's fine that they close each other. Scroll to the bottom, run the same `copy(...)` and save it as `S0n/<UTC timestamp>_expanded.html`.

**C. Note anything shown on the page about when it was last updated or reviewed.** That's the only date evidence we'll have for D-021.

Folder names:

| Folder | Page |
|---|---|
| S01 | Couples and Families |
| S02 | HFE letter |
| S03 | Income Guidelines and Documents |
| S04 | Application for a New Flat (make sure "Cancellation of flat application" is opened) |

## How completeness gets proven

Once the files are saved, my offline script compares each page's two copies. Text that appears only in the expanded copy would mean some content loads only on click. In that case, we use the step 2 collector for that page only. If there's no such text, the default copy is complete and both files are kept, with hashes.

The script also checks, for each page:
- the visible page text against the embedded page data, to catch content that's only in the data;
- that each section on the expected list is present, such as FT(PMC), FPPS, the under-21 fiancé(e) note, the HFE validity section and the cancellation section.

It prints only yes/no results, counts and hashes, so no source text reaches me.

Two copies per page is a few extra minutes, and it turns "we think we captured everything" into a measured result for the accordion-coverage check (REQ-SRC-012).

If you want, I'll write `scripts/register_snapshot.py` (offline, standard library only) while you capture, so it's ready when the files land.

# Development Log

Chronological record of completed work, decisions, failures and next steps. Decisions
themselves live in [decisions.md](decisions.md). Requirement IDs are in
[project_context/requirements_register.md](project_context/requirements_register.md).

---

## Phase 0 — Context building (2026-10-27 → 2026-10-28) — complete

**Done:**
- Reviewed both private planning PDFs page by page, including all 11 embedded images.
- Built the `docs/project_context/` knowledge base: 150 requirement IDs, a source-discovery
  matrix, the evaluation design, and a completeness audit (register §4).
- The developer resolved contradictions C-01 to C-13 (D-001 to D-025).
- Created `.gitignore` (private PDFs, private corpus, secrets) and private submission notes.
- Commit `c49555f docs: establish project context and requirements`.
- Context-extraction method (for re-audits): text via pdfplumber; every embedded image cropped
  at 300 dpi and read visually; non-default text colours checked to locate verbatim HDB quotes.

**Found:**
- New contradictions C-14 to C-17.
- Open questions Q-05 to Q-24.
- All policy facts quoted in the approach document are **unverified** until Phase 2.

| Lockfile and tooling | uv with committed `uv.lock`; dev tools in a PEP 735 `dev` group | D-028 | (in `e163bdd`) |
| Docker | Agent install failed (needs `sudo`); developer installed Docker Desktop. Docker 29.9.2 verified | — | — |
| Architecture review | Held draft (D-029) replaced by a full review; A1–A11 approved → [architecture.md](architecture.md) | D-030 to D-040; Q-05, Q-10, Q-12, Q-23 resolved | `0cca98b docs: approve architecture and record design decisions` |
| Schedule | Target 2026-10-29 07:00; effort estimate is reference only; all of A–D planned | D-043 | (in `0cca98b`, as notes) |
| Repository and tooling setup | Developer's structure adopted, simplified; Streamlit entry point, `Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`, `.env.example`, `.streamlit/config.toml` (telemetry off), merged `.gitignore`; Ruff excludes `docs/` (it formats Python blocks inside Markdown) | D-041 | `36531ae chore: add Streamlit entry point, Docker and environment tooling` |
| Capture tooling | Playwright in opt-in `capture` group; Chromium headless shell in user cache; offline launch test only | D-042 | `910eb78 chore: add opt-in Playwright capture dependency group` |

### Final verified state (re-run 2026-10-28, macOS, Python 3.13.2, uv 0.13.6, Docker 29.9.2)

and privacy notice; it says the pipeline isn't available yet), plus one smoke test. No pipeline

## Phase 2 — Policy sources (handoff)

**Goal (D-007):** determine the **minimum source set** for the MVP and turn verified content
into the reviewer-facing knowledge base. Nothing is included just because it appears in the
matrix.

**Read first:**
1. [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md);
2. [INDEX.md](project_context/INDEX.md);
3. [02_policy_sources.md](project_context/02_policy_sources.md) (matrix, media handling,
   facts to verify);
4. [03_data_and_licensing.md](project_context/03_data_and_licensing.md) (corpora, manifest,
   completeness checks, rights);
5. [architecture.md §5](architecture.md) (contracts, `PolicyFact`).

**Gates the developer must approve, in order:**
1. **Page list for capture.** Seeds plus any linked sources justified by the MVP tiers, with
   C-14 and Q-06 to Q-08 resolved.
2. **Rights check before fetching:** robots.txt and Terms of Use for each host. Never claim a
   redistribution licence.
3. **Capture run:** Playwright (`--group capture`), approved pages only. No crawling,
   link-following or transactional pages. Output goes to `data/private_corpus/raw/`
   (Git-ignored), with SHA-256 and timestamps in `data/sources_manifest.json`.
4. **Extraction and completeness audit:** 8 checks (03 §2.7), output to
   `data/private_corpus/processed/`, plus `data/source_coverage.csv`.
5. **Authoring:** `data/policy_facts.jsonl` (independently authored, verified, rights-reviewed,
   with `aliases`) and `data/policy_rules.yaml` (declarative, D-038). Finalise Q-22.

**Can proceed in parallel, with no dependence on real facts:**
- `schemas.py` and `policy.py` (loaders, rule interpreter, gate, profile assessment), with
  unit tests against a clearly fictional fixture KB in `tests/fixtures/`.

## Phase 2a — Source discovery, MVP mapping and rights review (2026-10-28) — awaiting approval

**Done:**
- Reconciled every matrix row and linked resource against the approved scope. The result is
  [source_acquisition_plan.md](source_acquisition_plan.md):
  - stable IDs: 17 documents (S01–S17), about 30 sections, 5 media items;
  - a five-way classification with reasons;
  - a relationship tree and link-type inventory;
  - a policy-dependency table;
  - an MVP coverage matrix;
  - a rights table per host;
  - the manifest schema;
  - the corpus layers L0–L3;
  - an extraction method per source;
  - a reviewer-reproducibility strategy;
  - gaps G-01 to G-14 and gates R, C and P.
- Reread APP p.4–12 of the private approach PDF (text and link annotations only) to confirm
  the matrix's original references. The Phase 0 extraction was complete. C-14 is present in

  to processed source text) to the register.

  - Copyright Act ss 244 and 187 were read from a secondary source (SSO returned 403).

Capturing it doesn't expand scope, because it supplies evidence for an area that's already approved. "Relevant first-timer and priority considerations" is an approved Limited-tier area under D-008. The audit showed FT(PMC) and FPPS are no longer on Couples and Families, so the Priority Schemes page is now the only source for that area. It was also already in your source-discovery matrix as S05, with this same URL.

I'd call it an **approved Essential source** rather than a **seed**. "Seed" refers to the four starting pages recorded in REQ-SRC-001 and D-007, and relabelling it would blur that record. I've moved S05 into the first capture group in both the plan and the proposed D-044.

The scope limits stay as they are:
- **Write facts only** from the FT(PMC), FPPS and Family Care Scheme sections. The other schemes (Third Child, Senior and Tenants' Priority) are captured with the page but are outside the MVP.
- **Limited tier means** identifying the considerations and linking to them, with conditions stated only where they're explicit and verified. It never predicts allocation or ballot outcomes.

To capture it, use the same method as before:
1. Run the step 1 check.
2. Copy the page with `copy(document.documentElement.outerHTML)`.
3. Save it as `data/private_corpus/raw/S05/<UTC timestamp>_priority_schemes_default.html`.

If you save it without the timestamp, I'll add it from the file's creation time as before.

## 2. Put the PDFs in the raw folder, one folder per source

def audit_pdf(path: Path, source_id: str) -> None:
    """Byte-level PDF facts only: no parser dependency (D-052) and no text output (D-054).

    Counts and Info-dictionary dates are read with regexes over the raw bytes. They are
    indicative: compressed object streams can hide them, in which case 'not found' is shown.
    """
    data = path.read_bytes()
    print(f"\n=== {source_id}: {path.name}")
    print(f"bytes={len(data)} sha256={hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()}")
    print(f"pdf header: {data[:8].decode('latin-1', 'replace')!r}")
    pages = len(re.findall(rb"/Type\s*/Page(?!s)", data))
    print(f"page objects (indicative): {pages or 'not found (object streams)'}")
    for key in (b"CreationDate", b"ModDate"):
        m = re.search(rb"/" + key + rb"\s*\(D:(\d{8,14})", data)
        print(f"{key.decode()}: {m.group(1).decode() if m else 'not found'}")
    print(f"font resources present (text layer likely): {bool(re.search(rb'/Font', data))}")

"""Fill acquisition provenance in data/sources_manifest.json from private raw captures.

For each `data/private_corpus/raw/<source_id>/<UTC>_<name>.(html|pdf)` it records:
- retrieved_at, parsed from the UTC prefix, which is the file's creation time at save;
- raw_sha256, byte_size and private_path;
- text_sha256 for HTML (normalised DOM text, via audit_snapshots). This hash detects real
  content drift on a later re-capture without storing any text.

Only metadata is written. The manifest is tracked; the raw files stay Git-ignored (D-005).
If a source has several captures, the newest one is registered (REQ-LIC-016). Earlier hashes
stay in Git history.

Usage: python -I scripts/register_snapshots.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import re
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path

from audit_snapshots import Snapshot, norm

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
RAW = ROOT / "data" / "private_corpus" / "raw"
MANIFEST = ROOT / "data" / "sources_manifest.json"
STAMP = re.compile(r"^(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T\d{6}Z)_")


def text_hash(html: bytes) -> str:
    snap = Snapshot()
    snap.feed(html.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
    return hashlib.sha256(norm(" ".join(snap.text)).encode()).hexdigest()


def main() -> None:
    manifest = json.loads(MANIFEST.read_text())
    by_id = {s["source_id"]: s for s in manifest["sources"]}
    for folder in sorted(p for p in RAW.glob("S*") if p.is_dir()):
        files = sorted(f for f in folder.iterdir() if STAMP.match(f.name))
        if not files or folder.name not in by_id:
            print(f"skip {folder.name}: no stamped file or no manifest entry")
            continue
        f = files[-1]
        data = f.read_bytes()
        stamp = STAMP.match(f.name).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]
        retrieved = datetime.strptime(stamp, "%Y-%m-%dT%H%M%SZ").replace(tzinfo=UTC)
        acq = by_id[folder.name]["acquisition"]
        acq.update(
            {
                "retrieved_at": retrieved.isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z"),
                "retrieved_at_basis": "file creation time at save (UTC filename prefix)",
                "raw_sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),
                "text_sha256": text_hash(data) if f.suffix == ".html" else None,
                "byte_size": len(data),
                "private_path": str(f.relative_to(ROOT)),
            }
        )
        print(f"{folder.name}: {acq['retrieved_at']} sha256={acq['raw_sha256'][:12]} ({f.name})")
    MANIFEST.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        stamp = STAMP.match(f.name).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]
        retrieved = datetime.strptime(stamp, "%Y-%m-%dT%H%M%SZ").replace(tzinfo=UTC)
        acq = by_id[folder.name]["acquisition"]
        acq.update(
            {
                "retrieved_at": retrieved.isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z"),
                "retrieved_at_basis": "file creation time at save (UTC filename prefix)",
                "raw_sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),
                "text_sha256": text_hash(data) if f.suffix == ".html" else None,
                "byte_size": len(data),
                "private_path": str(f.relative_to(ROOT)),
            }
        )
        print(f"{folder.name}: {acq['retrieved_at']} sha256={acq['raw_sha256'][:12]} ({f.name})")
    MANIFEST.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

# BTO Buddy — Project Context Index

This is a structured, traceable knowledge base built from the project's two private planning
sources:
- the **assessment brief** (`[ASM p.N]`);
- the **project-approach document** (`[APP p.N]`).

Both PDFs are kept locally and are Git-ignored. This documentation is independently
authored: it paraphrases requirements and policy content rather than reproducing them.

**Status (2026-10-28):** Phase 0 (context) and Phase 1 (setup and architecture) are complete.
Phase 2a (source discovery, MVP mapping, rights review and acquisition plan) is **drafted and
awaiting approval**: [../source_acquisition_plan.md](../source_acquisition_plan.md), with
proposed decisions D-044 to D-055. Nothing has been fetched or captured.

**What exists:**
- the uv project and lockfile;
- a Streamlit entry-point shell;
- one smoke test;
- the Docker image.

No pipeline modules, data files, model choice or datasets exist yet.

## Files

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [01_problem_and_scope.md](01_problem_and_scope.md) | Final idea, problem statement, research question, problem validation, **MVP scope**, HFE/income boundaries, supported-question draft, missing-information categories, demo archetypes |
| [02_policy_sources.md](02_policy_sources.md) | Seed sources, discovery method, **complete source-discovery matrix**, infographic/video registry candidates, **media-handling decisions**, policy nuances to verify |
| [03_data_and_licensing.md](03_data_and_licensing.md) | Datasets A/B/C, private vs reviewer-facing corpora, manifest, schemas, completeness checks, licensing/robots/copyright, privacy, reproducibility, limitations |
| [04_architecture.md](04_architecture.md) | Pipeline, coverage gate, missing-information contract, representation principles, verifier behaviour, proposed stack, provider comparison, model scorecard |
| [05_evaluation.md](05_evaluation.md) | Configurations A–D, **benchmark structure**, label protocol, proposed split, **metric definitions**, severity rubric, retrieval and verifier evaluation, statistics, failure taxonomy |
| [06_submission_requirements.md](06_submission_requirements.md) | Mandatory deliverables, scoring dimensions, non-compliance indicators, resources, AI-log rules, README requirements |
| [requirements_register.md](requirements_register.md) | **All requirement IDs** with source pages, components and acceptance evidence; contradictions; open questions; completeness audit |
| [../decisions.md](../decisions.md) | Decision log (D-001 onward, BD-00…BD-09) and the instruction priority |
| [../architecture.md](../architecture.md) | **Approved implementation design** (D-030 to D-040): pipeline, contracts, retrieval choice, dependencies, tests |
| [../source_acquisition_plan.md](../source_acquisition_plan.md) | **Phase 2a (PROPOSED):** reconciled matrix with source IDs, coverage matrix, link inventory, dependencies, rights assessment, manifest schema, corpus and extraction strategy, gaps, approval gates |
| [../development_log.md](../development_log.md) | Progress per phase, verified commands, failures, next steps |
| [../../CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md) | Working instructions for coding agents (scope, invariants, Git workflow, commands) |

## Legend

**Status**

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `MANDATORY` | Explicit requirement in the assessment brief |
| `APPROVED` | Final project decision (in the project approach as final, or ratified/added in [decisions.md](../decisions.md)) |
| `PROPOSED` | Technical alternative or implementation detail not yet approved |
| `OPEN` | Cannot be resolved from the sources or decisions; needs a developer answer |
| `HISTORICAL` / `SUPERSEDED` | Earlier idea or decision replaced by an approved one. Kept for traceability, **not** an active requirement |

**Provenance**

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `COPIED-SOURCE` | The project-approach PDF quoted HDB text verbatim at this point. The quotation is **not** reproduced in tracked files |
| `AUTHORED-FACT (unverified)` | Independently paraphrased policy statement. It must be verified against a frozen source before it enters `data/policy_facts.jsonl` |
| `PROJECT-DECISION` | Design choice by the developer (the default for non-policy content) |
| *Author observation* | Point raised while building this knowledge base, not stated in either source |

## Instruction priority (D-001)
1. Mandatory assessment requirements.
2. The developer's latest explicit instructions and approved decisions.
3. Finalised scope, architecture, data strategy and evaluation methodology.
4. The current approved implementation task.
5. Proposed alternatives and open questions.
6. Historical or superseded brainstorming.

## Where to look for a task
| Task | Read |
|---|---|
| Any task | `CLAUDE.md`, then this index |
| Scope questions | 01, plus D-008 / D-013 / D-033 in [decisions](../decisions.md) |
| Source capture, extraction, facts | [source_acquisition_plan](../source_acquisition_plan.md) first, then 02, 03, [architecture §5](../architecture.md) |
| Pipeline code | [architecture.md](../architecture.md) (§3 stages, §5 contracts, §11 modules, §12 tests), 04 |
| Benchmark and evaluation | 05, register (REQ-EVL-*) |
| README and submission | 06, register (REQ-SUB-*, REQ-DOC-*) |
| History and current state | [development_log.md](../development_log.md) |

## Current open items
- **Contradictions open:**
  - C-14 (URL mismatch in the matrix, Q-24);
  - C-15 and C-16 (metric gaps, Q-16 and Q-15);
  - C-17 (privacy missing from the scorecard, Q-13).
- **Questions open:**

  | Needed by | Questions |
  |---|---|
  | Phase 2 | Q-06, Q-07, Q-08, Q-09, Q-11, Q-22, Q-24 |
  | Model selection | Q-13 |
  | Before evaluation | Q-14, Q-15, Q-16, Q-17 |
  | Before dataset creation | Q-20, Q-21 |
  | Pre-submission | Q-19 |

- **Resolved:** Q-05, Q-10, Q-12, Q-18, Q-23.
- **Awaiting confirmation:** the `llm.py` addition in D-041.
- **Execution risk:** C-09 / Q-19 (log anonymity vs completeness).

Details are in [requirements_register.md §2–3](requirements_register.md#2-contradictions). The
consolidated list with owners and deadlines is in the
[development log](../development_log.md#unresolved-issues-carried-forward).

Then the web-fetch tool → file served | One `User-agent: *` group; about 150 `Disallow` entries, mostly transactional and account paths; no `Crawl-delay`; sitemap listed. **No rule matches** S01–S06 or `/-/media/`. **`Disallow: /hdb-flat-portal` matches S10** (HFE FAQs). No wildcard rule matches `?anchor=` URLs | Checked. Raw copy **not** held (only the tool's reading), so the developer should save robots.txt from a browser to get a hash |
309	| R4 HDB Terms of Use (`www.hdb.gov.sg/terms-of-use`) | Web-fetch → heading only (body is rendered by JavaScript). Headless Chromium with an honest UA → **HTTP 403** (saved privately, sha256 `df0a74…c9d6`) | **Clauses not read.** For reference only: HDB's terms for its other site (mynicehome.gov.sg) limit use to personal, non-commercial purposes and assert IP ownership ([source](https://www.mynicehome.gov.sg/terms-of-use)). That is a different site and must not be assumed to apply | **UNRESOLVED.** The developer reads it in a browser |
310	| R6 Copyright Act 2021 ss 243–244, 187 | Singapore Statutes Online → 403. Secondary text on lawplayer.com ([s 244](https://lawplayer.com/sg/act/CA2021/244), [s 187](https://lawplayer.com/sg/act/CA2021/187)) | **s 244(2):** (a) copy made for computational data analysis or preparing for it; (b) no other use; (c) **no supply to others except to verify results or for collaborative research**; (d) **lawful access** to the first copy. The illustrations say circumventing a paywall, or breaching a database's terms of use, isn't lawful access, but terms void under s 187 are disregarded. (e) the first copy isn't infringing (or the stated exceptions apply). **s 187:** contract terms that exclude or restrict the Division 8 (CDA) permitted use are void | Secondary source; confirm against SSO when it's reachable |
311	
312	**Consequences:**
313	1. **Automated capture is not available.** HDB's bot protection refuses both curl and headless
314	   Chromium. Getting around it (spoofed user agent, stealth browser) is rejected: it is an
315	   access control, and getting past it would undermine lawful access under s 244(2)(d).
316	   Manual capture in a normal browser, which any member of the public can do, is the
317	   primary method (revised D-055).
318	2. **S10 is disallowed for crawlers.** It won't be acquired by any automated means. The
319	   developer may still read it as a normal visitor to decide Q-08. Saving it stays a
320	   separate approval.
321	3. **Local L0/L1 copies:** s 244 is a plausible basis, given lawful (manual) access and use
322	   for analysis only.
323	4. **Committing copies to GitHub** is outside s 244(2)(c), so it stays **not permitted**.
324	5. **Sending source text to an LLM provider** would be "supplying" a copy to a third party
325	   for a purpose other than verifying results or collaborative research. It is **not
326	   permitted** under this basis. This firms up D-054.
327	6. **Authored facts** (own expression, no substantial copying) are unaffected.
328	
329	### 7.3 Rules carried into the plan
330	
331	- **robots.txt is not a licence.** A permissive robots.txt only means automated access isn't
332	  disallowed. It grants no copyright permission.
333	- **Public is not the same as redistributable.** Nothing acquired is committed, and nothing is
334	  described as licensed.
335	- If the Terms of Use **prohibit automated access**, Playwright capture stops. The fallback is
336	  manual "save page" by the developer in a normal browser, recorded as `manual_rendered_dom`
337	  (REQ-SRC-006 allows manual extraction). This fallback only changes the access method. It
338	  does not resolve copyright, so storage and redistribution stay private.
339	- If robots.txt **disallows** a path, that page is not captured automatically. Manual
340	  inspection by the developer is a policy decision for the developer to make, recorded in
341	  decisions.md. It is not assumed.
342	- Every rights finding is stored in `rights_records` in the manifest (§8.2), with the check
343	  date and SHA-256 of the robots.txt or terms page.
344	
345	---
346	
347	## 8. Source manifest schema
348	
349	File: `data/sources_manifest.json` (tracked, D-022). It holds metadata only and **never source
350	text**. Typed with Pydantic in `policy.py` when first needed. Proposed as **D-053**.
351	
352	### 8.1 Top level
353	
354	```json
355	{
356	  "manifest_version": "2026-10-28.1",
357	  "generated_at": "2026-10-28T00:00:00+08:00",
358	  "rights_records": [ /* §8.2 */ ],

362	
363	### 8.2 `rights_records[]` (one per host or terms regime)

374	| `robots_checked_at` | datetime or null | |
375	| `robots_sha256` | str or null | |
376	| `robots_relevant_rules` | list[str] | Directives affecting the planned paths, e.g. `"User-agent: * / Disallow: /x"`. Short directives are not substantial text |
377	| `robots_permits_planned_paths` | `yes` / `no` / `partial` / `unchecked` | |
378	| `legal_basis` | `cda_s243_244` / `terms_permission` / `link_only` / `unresolved` | Basis for local copying |
379	| `redistribution` | `not_permitted` / `unresolved` / `permitted` | For copies and copied text |
380	| `llm_transmission` | `not_permitted` / `unresolved` / `permitted` | For source text |
381	| `notes` | str | |

383	### 8.3 `sources[]` (one per document, section or media item)
384	
385	| Field | Type | Meaning / allowed values |
386	|---|---|---|
387	| `source_id` | str | `S01`, `S01.a`, `M01` (§1). Stable and never reused |
388	| `record_kind` | `document` / `section` / `media` | |

391	| `canonical_url` | str | Normalised: https, lower-case host, no tracking or cache query (`si`, `sc_lang`, `hash`), no anchor. YouTube becomes `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<id>` |

401	| `matrix_refs` | list[str] | e.g. `["Row 1, APP p.6"]` |
402	| `policy_areas` | list of `Topic` | architecture §5 enum, e.g. `hfe_process` |
403	| `applicant_categories` | list of enum | `first_timer_couple_married` · `first_timer_couple_engaged` · `out_of_scope_household` · `all` |
404	| `mvp_class` | enum | `essential` · `supporting` · `context_only` · `outside_mvp` · `pending` |
405	| `mvp_class_reason` | str | One line, as in §2 |
406	| `effective_date` | date or null | Only if the source states it |
407	| `effective_date_status` | enum | `stated` · `page_last_updated_only` · `unknown` |
408	| `page_last_updated` | date or null | If the page displays one |

411	| `acquisition.approved_by` | str or null | Decision ID approving this item's capture, e.g. `D-044` |
412	| `acquisition.retrieved_at` | datetime (+08:00) or null | Capture time |
413	| `acquisition.http_status` | int or null | |
414	| `acquisition.raw_sha256` | str or null | SHA-256 of the saved raw artefact (HTML or PDF) |
415	| `acquisition.text_sha256` | str or null | SHA-256 of the normalised extracted text. This separates real content change from page noise (scripts, tokens) on later drift checks |
416	| `acquisition.byte_size` | int or null | |

420	| `extraction.headings_visible` / `headings_extracted` | int or null | Section-coverage check |
421	| `extraction.links` | list of `{url, text, decision: included/excluded/pending, reason}` | Link-coverage check |
422	| `extraction.status` | enum | `not_started` · `extracted` · `validated` · `failed` |

428	### 8.4 Example: planned entry before capture

436	  "canonical_url": "https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/application-for-an-hdb-flat-eligibility-hfe-letter",
437	  "host": "www.hdb.gov.sg",

439	  "discovered_from": [{"source_id": "S02", "link_text": "How to apply"}],

455	                  "http_status": null, "raw_sha256": null, "text_sha256": null,

463	
464	Sections inherit the acquisition record of their parent document, because one snapshot covers
465	all sections. Their own `acquisition` fields stay null except `method`.
466	
467	### 8.5 `data/source_coverage.csv` columns (format for the 03 §1 asset)
468	
469	`area_tier, sub_area, rule_or_fact_ids, essential_source_ids, supporting_source_ids,
470	exceptions_required, exceptions_verified (y/n), coverage_status
471	(covered/partial/gap/excluded), evidence_gap_kind (05 §8 taxonomy), notes`
472	
473	---
474	
475	## 9. Corpus strategy
476	
477	### 9.1 Layers
478	
479	| Layer | Content | Path | Git | Who uses it | Rights basis |
480	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
481	| **L0** Raw snapshots | Rendered HTML of approved pages; approved PDFs; private copies of robots.txt and terms pages; capture logs | `data/private_corpus/raw/<source_id>/` | Ignored | Developer: provenance, re-audit | Local analysis only (§7) |
482	| **L1** Processed passages | Structured blocks: heading path, paragraph/list/table cells, link list, `passage_id`, `source_id`. Any local index built over them | `data/private_corpus/processed/` | Ignored | Developer: completeness audit, fact authoring, verification of facts | Local analysis only. Contains copied text |
483	| **L2** Authored KB | `policy_facts.jsonl` (paraphrased statements, fact IDs, source pointers by `source_id` and section, **no quotes**); `policy_rules.yaml` citing fact IDs | `data/` | Tracked after rights review | App, BM25, Docker, all evaluation | Own expression of facts |
484	| **L3** Metadata | `sources_manifest.json`, `source_coverage.csv`, `visual_resources.json`, rights notes | `data/`, `docs/` | Tracked | Reviewers, app (URL resolution, registry links) | URLs, titles, short headings, hashes: not substantial text |
485	
486	### 9.2 How the reviewer-facing corpus supports the MVP without redistribution
487	
488	- Every runtime claim cites a **fact ID**. The fact resolves to an **official URL and
489	  section** through the manifest (D-006), so reviewers check the claim against HDB's live page
490	  rather than against a redistributed copy.
491	- The fact records `retrieved_at`, plus `raw_sha256` through its source. That makes clear
492	  which version the fact describes, even though the snapshot itself isn't shared.
493	- Coverage is shown in `source_coverage.csv`. This is how the KB demonstrates the
494	  exceptions it represents, without exposing source text.
495	
496	### 9.3 Rights review before an authored fact is tracked (proposed in D-054)
497	
498	1. Paraphrase in independent wording: one condition per statement. Keep only proper names
499	   (scheme names), numbers, dates and durations, which are facts.
500	2. **Local overlap check:** a stdlib script in `scripts/` compares each statement with L1
501	   passages and flags any shared run of 8 or more consecutive words. Flagged statements are
502	   reworded. The script reads L1 locally and prints only IDs and counts.
503	3. `rights_review.status = cleared` only after steps 1–2 and a manual read.
504	4. The anonymity scan and the secret scan run before the commit is suggested.
505	
506	### 9.4 Who reads L0 and L1
507	
508	L0 and L1 are processed locally by scripts.
509	
510	**Open point for approval (D-054):** whether the coding agent may read L1 to help author
511	facts. Doing so sends source text to the agent's model provider, an external LLM service.
512	CLAUDE.md requires approval for that. The rights position is **unresolved**, because the
513	computational data analysis exception limits supplying copies to others.
514	
515	| Option | Cost |
516	|---|---|
517	| **(a) Recommended:** the developer reads L1 and drafts facts. The agent works only on authored drafts, schema, rules and checks | Slower authoring |
518	| (b) The agent reads L1 under an explicit, recorded approval | Faster. Carries the unresolved rights risk and must be disclosed |
519	
520	---
521	
522	## 10. Extraction method per approved source
523	
524	> **Superseded in part by Gate R (§7.2a, revised D-055).** HDB returns 403 to automated
525	> clients, so **capture is manual**:
526	> 1. The developer opens each approved page in a normal browser, not logged in.
527	> 2. Clicks every accordion open.
528	> 3. In DevTools runs `copy(document.documentElement.outerHTML)` and saves the result as
529	>    `data/private_corpus/raw/<source_id>/<UTC timestamp>.html`. This takes the live DOM and
530	>    no image bytes. Chrome's "Save as… Complete" or a single-file save would also save the
531	>    infographics, so they are avoided.
532	> 4. Notes the time and how many accordions were opened.
533	>
534	> A local **offline** script (`scripts/register_snapshot.py`) then does the rest. It hashes the
535	> file, writes the manifest entry, counts expanded vs collapsed controls in the saved DOM, and
536	> serialises structure to L1 with Playwright `set_content` (JavaScript off, no network) or the
537	> stdlib parser.
538	>
539	> **Exclusive accordions** (opening one closes another; observed by the developer 2026-10-28):
540	> 1. First run a read-only console check. It counts accordion controls and measures whether
541	>    each collapsed panel's content is already in the DOM. It also checks for the embedded
542	>    page-data JSON (`__NEXT_DATA__`; the site is Next.js on a Sitecore media path).
543	> 2. If every panel is in the DOM, a single `outerHTML` copy is complete.
544	> 3. If panels are unmounted when closed, a console-assisted collector opens each section in
545	>    turn in the developer's own session, at about 1 s per click. It saves each section's
546	>    heading and panel HTML with the full page into one JSON bundle per page.
547	> 4. Recorded as `manual_rendered_dom` with `expansion: console_assisted_sequential`.
548	> 5. Completeness check: the section count in the bundle equals the control count from the
549	>    check, and no panel is empty.
550	>
551	> The automated-capture description below applies only if HDB later permits automated access.
552	
553	All capture runs use `scripts/capture_sources.py` (D-042) with a **tracked allowlist**,
554	`data/capture_allowlist.json`. The allowlist lists approved `source_id` → URL pairs and is
555	derived from the approved manifest. The script refuses any URL that isn't on the allowlist.
556	
557	**Common behaviour** (D-053, D-055):
558	- headless Chromium; one page at a time; a fixed delay between pages (at least 10 s, or the
559	  robots.txt `Crawl-delay` if larger);
560	- an honest user-agent string that identifies a research prototype;
561	- no login and no form submission;
562	- no link-following;
563	- `waitUntil: networkidle`, then expand every accordion control inside the main content area,
564	  recording the controls found and the controls expanded;
565	- save `page.content()` to L0;
566	- compute `raw_sha256`;
567	- serialise structure in-browser with `page.evaluate`: heading path, paragraphs, lists,
568	  tables (rows, cells, nested tables kept as children) and links (href and text). Output goes
569	  to L1 as JSONL, with `text_sha256`;
570	- no screenshots by default;
571	- no HTML-parsing dependency: the browser DOM does the parsing, so D-036/D-042 stay
572	  unchanged.
573	
574	| Source | Method | Specific handling | Validation (REQ-SRC-012 checks) |
575	|---|---|---|---|
576	| S01 | Playwright DOM | Expand all category accordions and nested tables. Keep the category heading on every row (REQ-SRC-003). Tag S01.c–e, n3 and i rows as `outside_mvp` in L1; they are kept for the audit and never authored | Accordion count; table row/column spot-check against the rendered page; locate notes n1–n4; find the first-timer definition (G-05) |
577	| S02 | Playwright DOM | Expand When to apply, How to apply, Validity, Next steps. Record `<img>` src and alt for M00–M02 and the video links. Record outgoing links to S03, S10, S11 and S16 without following them | Check whether the M01 facts (Step-2 window, processing time, validity) appear in the **text** → resolves G-02 |
578	| S03 | Playwright DOM | Extract supporting-document lists and assessment-period text. Income-calculation passages are tagged `documentation_only` | HTML-equivalence check for S07/S08: does S03 list documents per employment category? |
579	| S04 | Playwright DOM | Expand all accordions, especially `cancellation`. Search for an "exceptions"/"waiver" heading | Resolves G-03 (S04.b location) |
580	| S05 | Playwright DOM (if approved) | Expand all. Author only S05.b and S05.c | Accordion count |
581	| S06 | Playwright DOM (if approved) | BTO section only is authored | — |
582	| S07, S08 | Direct HTTPS download (if approved after the check) | **No new dependency:** the developer validates the relevant pages manually and records page numbers in L1 by hand (D-052). OCR is not planned | Page and section refs in the manifest |
583	| S10, S11 | Not captured until Q-08 / G-02 is decided | If approved: Playwright DOM, single page, no sub-link following | — |

# Phase 2a — Source Discovery, MVP Mapping, Rights Review and Acquisition Plan

**Status: PROPOSED (2026-10-28). Awaiting developer review.** Nothing in this document has
been fetched, downloaded, captured or extracted. Proposed decisions are D-044 to D-055 in
[decisions.md](decisions.md#proposed-decisions-phase-2a-2026-10-28). They become requirements
only after approval.

**Inputs:**
- the source-discovery matrix in [02 §3](project_context/02_policy_sources.md), re-checked
  against the private project-approach PDF (APP p.4–12) on 2026-10-28;
- the scope in [01 §6](project_context/01_problem_and_scope.md) (D-008, D-013, D-033);
- the data and rights rules in [03](project_context/03_data_and_licensing.md);
- the contracts in [architecture.md §5](architecture.md).

**Why the PDF was reread:** the matrix is the critical input, so its original references had to
be confirmed. The reread found no loss in the Phase 0 extraction. Every row, exception, URL
and media item in 02 §3 matches the PDF. C-14 (Row 4's URL) is present in the original PDF,
so it was not introduced during extraction.

**Provenance tags** (as in [INDEX](project_context/INDEX.md#legend)):
- *matrix* = recorded in the developer's matrix;
- *unverified* = not yet checked against a frozen source;
- *agent knowledge* = from the coding agent's general knowledge. It is unverified and must be
  checked before use; it is never a fact.

**Contents:**
1. [Classification scheme](#1-classification-scheme)
2. [Reconciled source-discovery matrix](#2-reconciled-source-discovery-matrix)
3. [Source relationship and link inventory](#3-source-relationship-and-link-classification-inventory)
4. [Policy dependencies and exceptions](#4-policy-dependencies-and-exceptions)
5. [MVP source coverage matrix](#5-mvp-source-coverage-matrix)
6. [Non-text resources](#6-non-text-resources)
7. [Rights and access assessment](#7-rights-and-access-assessment)
8. [Source manifest schema](#8-source-manifest-schema)
9. [Corpus strategy](#9-corpus-strategy)
10. [Extraction method per approved source](#10-extraction-method-per-approved-source)
11. [Reviewer reproducibility](#11-reviewer-reproducibility-strategy)
12. [Coverage gaps and blockers](#12-source-and-policy-coverage-gaps)
13. [Recommended acquisition scope](#13-recommended-final-acquisition-scope)
14. [Risks, exclusions and approval decisions](#14-unresolved-risks-exclusions-and-approval-decisions)
15. [Requirement traceability](#15-requirement-traceability)

---

## 1. Classification scheme

| Class | Definition used here |
|---|---|
| **Essential** | Needed to implement **and** evaluate a Core area, or the only source for a Limited area that is planned. Without it, a supported rule has no verified source (REQ-SRC-013) |
| **Supporting** | Adds conditions, exceptions or process detail for an in-scope area, or serves a Limited area that has an Essential source elsewhere. Acquire only with item-level approval |
| **Context only** | Used only to explain the HFE ↔ grant/loan relationship, or as a redirect/link target. No facts beyond the relationship; no calculation (REQ-SCP-004) |
| **Outside MVP** | Excluded tier (D-008), out-of-scope household type (D-033) or income determination (D-013). It may still be a **redirect URL** for the coverage gate, but it is **not acquired** |
| **Pending** | The classification depends on content that hasn't been inspected yet, or on an open question. Neither acquired nor dropped until resolved |

**Source IDs:** stable and never reused.
- `S##` is a document: a page, PDF or external page.
- `S##.x` is a section inside a document: an accordion, anchor or note.
- `M##` is a non-text media item.

These IDs become `source_id` in `data/sources_manifest.json` (§8).

---

## 2. Reconciled source-discovery matrix

The table covers every row and every linked resource in the matrix. The **Matrix ref** column
keeps the original location in the approach document.

### 2.1 Documents

| ID | Title (as recorded) | Original URL (as recorded) | Matrix ref | Class | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**Consequences:**
1. **Automated capture is not available.** HDB's bot protection refuses both curl and headless
   Chromium. Getting around it (spoofed user agent, stealth browser) is rejected: it is an
   access control, and getting past it would undermine lawful access under s 244(2)(d).
   Manual capture in a normal browser, which any member of the public can do, is the
   primary method (revised D-055).
2. **S10 is disallowed for crawlers.** It won't be acquired by any automated means. The
   developer may still read it as a normal visitor to decide Q-08. Saving it stays a
   separate approval.
3. **Local L0/L1 copies:** s 244 is a plausible basis, given lawful (manual) access and use
   for analysis only.
4. **Committing copies to GitHub** is outside s 244(2)(c), so it stays **not permitted**.
5. **Sending source text to an LLM provider** would be "supplying" a copy to a third party
   for a purpose other than verifying results or collaborative research. It is **not
   permitted** under this basis. This firms up D-054.
6. **Authored facts** (own expression, no substantial copying) are unaffected.

### 7.3 Rules carried into the plan

- **robots.txt is not a licence.** A permissive robots.txt only means automated access isn't
  disallowed. It grants no copyright permission.
- **Public is not the same as redistributable.** Nothing acquired is committed, and nothing is
  described as licensed.
- If the Terms of Use **prohibit automated access**, Playwright capture stops. The fallback is
  manual "save page" by the developer in a normal browser, recorded as `manual_rendered_dom`
  (REQ-SRC-006 allows manual extraction). This fallback only changes the access method. It
  does not resolve copyright, so storage and redistribution stay private.
- If robots.txt **disallows** a path, that page is not captured automatically. Manual
  inspection by the developer is a policy decision for the developer to make, recorded in
  decisions.md. It is not assumed.
- Every rights finding is stored in `rights_records` in the manifest (§8.2), with the check
  date and SHA-256 of the robots.txt or terms page.

## 9. Corpus strategy

### 9.1 Layers

| Layer | Content | Path | Git | Who uses it | Rights basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **L0** Raw snapshots | Rendered HTML of approved pages; approved PDFs; private copies of robots.txt and terms pages; capture logs | `data/private_corpus/raw/<source_id>/` | Ignored | Developer: provenance, re-audit | Local analysis only (§7) |
| **L1** Processed passages | Structured blocks: heading path, paragraph/list/table cells, link list, `passage_id`, `source_id`. Any local index built over them | `data/private_corpus/processed/` | Ignored | Developer: completeness audit, fact authoring, verification of facts | Local analysis only. Contains copied text |
| **L2** Authored KB | `policy_facts.jsonl` (paraphrased statements, fact IDs, source pointers by `source_id` and section, **no quotes**); `policy_rules.yaml` citing fact IDs | `data/` | Tracked after rights review | App, BM25, Docker, all evaluation | Own expression of facts |
| **L3** Metadata | `sources_manifest.json`, `source_coverage.csv`, `visual_resources.json`, rights notes | `data/`, `docs/` | Tracked | Reviewers, app (URL resolution, registry links) | URLs, titles, short headings, hashes: not substantial text |

### 9.2 How the reviewer-facing corpus supports the MVP without redistribution

- Every runtime claim cites a **fact ID**. The fact resolves to an **official URL and
  section** through the manifest (D-006), so reviewers check the claim against HDB's live page
  rather than against a redistributed copy.
- The fact records `retrieved_at`, plus `raw_sha256` through its source. That makes clear
  which version the fact describes, even though the snapshot itself isn't shared.
- Coverage is shown in `source_coverage.csv`. This is how the KB demonstrates the
  exceptions it represents, without exposing source text.

### 9.3 Rights review before an authored fact is tracked (proposed in D-054)

1. Paraphrase in independent wording: one condition per statement. Keep only proper names
   (scheme names), numbers, dates and durations, which are facts.
2. **Local overlap check:** a stdlib script in `scripts/` compares each statement with L1
   passages and flags any shared run of 8 or more consecutive words. Flagged statements are
   reworded. The script reads L1 locally and prints only IDs and counts.
3. `rights_review.status = cleared` only after steps 1–2 and a manual read.
4. The anonymity scan and the secret scan run before the commit is suggested.

### 9.4 Who reads L0 and L1

L0 and L1 are processed locally by scripts.

**Open point for approval (D-054):** whether the coding agent may read L1 to help author
facts. Doing so sends source text to the agent's model provider, an external LLM service.
CLAUDE.md requires approval for that. The rights position is **unresolved**, because the
computational data analysis exception limits supplying copies to others.

| Option | Cost |
|---|---|
| **(a) Recommended:** the developer reads L1 and drafts facts. The agent works only on authored drafts, schema, rules and checks | Slower authoring |
| (b) The agent reads L1 under an explicit, recorded approval | Faster. Carries the unresolved rights risk and must be disclosed |

## 10. Extraction method per approved source

> **Superseded in part by Gate R (§7.2a, revised D-055).** HDB returns 403 to automated
> clients, so **capture is manual**:
> 1. The developer opens each approved page in a normal browser, not logged in.
> 2. Clicks every accordion open.
> 3. In DevTools runs `copy(document.documentElement.outerHTML)` and saves the result as
>    `data/private_corpus/raw/<source_id>/<UTC timestamp>.html`. This takes the live DOM and
>    no image bytes. Chrome's "Save as… Complete" or a single-file save would also save the
>    infographics, so they are avoided.
> 4. Notes the time and how many accordions were opened.
>
> A local **offline** script (`scripts/register_snapshot.py`) then does the rest. It hashes the
> file, writes the manifest entry, counts expanded vs collapsed controls in the saved DOM, and
> serialises structure to L1 with Playwright `set_content` (JavaScript off, no network) or the
> stdlib parser.
>
> **Exclusive accordions** (opening one closes another; observed by the developer 2026-10-28):
> 1. First run a read-only console check. It counts accordion controls and measures whether
>    each collapsed panel's content is already in the DOM. It also checks for the embedded
>    page-data JSON (`__NEXT_DATA__`; the site is Next.js on a Sitecore media path).
> 2. If every panel is in the DOM, a single `outerHTML` copy is complete.
> 3. If panels are unmounted when closed, a console-assisted collector opens each section in
>    turn in the developer's own session, at about 1 s per click. It saves each section's
>    heading and panel HTML with the full page into one JSON bundle per page.
> 4. Recorded as `manual_rendered_dom` with `expansion: console_assisted_sequential`.
> 5. Completeness check: the section count in the bundle equals the control count from the
>    check, and no panel is empty.
>
> The automated-capture description below applies only if HDB later permits automated access.

All capture runs use `scripts/capture_sources.py` (D-042) with a **tracked allowlist**,
`data/capture_allowlist.json`. The allowlist lists approved `source_id` → URL pairs and is
derived from the approved manifest. The script refuses any URL that isn't on the allowlist.

**Common behaviour** (D-053, D-055):
- headless Chromium; one page at a time; a fixed delay between pages (at least 10 s, or the
  robots.txt `Crawl-delay` if larger);
- an honest user-agent string that identifies a research prototype;
- no login and no form submission;
- no link-following;
- `waitUntil: networkidle`, then expand every accordion control inside the main content area,
  recording the controls found and the controls expanded;
- save `page.content()` to L0;
- compute `raw_sha256`;
- serialise structure in-browser with `page.evaluate`: heading path, paragraphs, lists,
  tables (rows, cells, nested tables kept as children) and links (href and text). Output goes
  to L1 as JSONL, with `text_sha256`;
- no screenshots by default;
- no HTML-parsing dependency: the browser DOM does the parsing, so D-036/D-042 stay
  unchanged.

| **Outside MVP** | Excluded tier, out-of-scope household (D-033) or income determination (D-013). It may be a redirect URL, but its content is never authored |
| **Pending** | Depends on an open question |

- `S##` is a document;
- `S##.x` is a section inside a document;
- `M##` is a media item.

### 6.2 Consequences

## 7. Acquisition method and completeness

**Capture method (D-055):**
1. The developer opens each page in a normal browser, not logged in.
2. Runs a read-only console check of the accordions.
3. Copies `document.documentElement.outerHTML`. This takes the live DOM, not the image files.
   "Save as complete" is avoided because it would also save the infographics.
4. Saves the copy to `data/private_corpus/raw/<source_id>/<UTC>_<name>.html`.

PDFs are downloaded in the browser, never re-saved. Their final URLs come from the
download record. The UTC prefix is the file's creation time; for the PDFs it matches
Chrome's download timestamp to within 2 s.

Accordions open exclusively, but every panel is present in the DOM in the default state
(console check, confirmed by the offline audit). So **one default-state copy per page is
complete**.

**Offline tooling:** stdlib only. Output is structure only, never source text.

## 8. Corpus design

### 8.1 Layers

| Layer | Content | Path | Git |
|---|---|---|---|
| L0 raw | HTML and PDF snapshots; rights-check evidence | `data/private_corpus/raw/` | Ignored |
| L1 processed | Structured passages (heading path, text, tables, links) and any local index | `data/private_corpus/processed/` | Ignored |
| L2 authored KB | `policy_facts.jsonl` (paraphrased, fact IDs, source pointers, **no quotes**); `policy_rules.yaml` | `data/` | Tracked after rights review |
| L3 metadata | `sources_manifest.json`, `source_coverage.csv`, `visual_resources.json` | `data/` | Tracked |

The app, BM25 index, Docker image and evaluation use **only L2 and L3** (D-005,
REQ-DAT-011/012). Each claim cites a fact ID. The fact resolves to an official URL and section
through the manifest (D-006), so reviewers check it against HDB's live page, not a copy.

### 8.2 Rights review before a fact is tracked (D-054)

1. **Write independently worded statements**, one condition each. Only proper names, numbers,
   dates and durations are kept as-is.
2. **Run a local overlap check:** flag any 8+ consecutive words shared with L1, and reword.
3. **Read it manually,** then set `rights_review: cleared`.
4. **Run the anonymity and secret scans** before suggesting a commit.

The developer drafts facts from L1, and the coding agent works only on the drafts (D-054
option (a), recommended).

### 8.3 Manifest schema (D-053, PROPOSED)

Top level: `manifest_version`, `rights_records[]`, `sources[]`.

| `rights_records[]` fields | `sources[]` fields |
|---|---|
| `rights_id`, `host`, `terms_url`, `terms_checked_at`, `terms_sha256`, `terms_summary` (authored), `robots_url`, `robots_checked_at`, `robots_sha256`, `robots_relevant_rules`, `robots_permits_planned_paths`, `legal_basis`, `redistribution`, `llm_transmission`, `notes` | `source_id`, `record_kind`, `title`, `original_url`, `canonical_url`, `host`, `parent_source_id`, `link_relation`, `content_format`, `matrix_refs`, `policy_areas` (architecture §5 `Topic`), `mvp_class`, `mvp_class_reason`, `page_last_updated`, `effective_date`, `effective_date_status` (`stated` / `page_last_updated_only` / `pdf_metadata_date_only` / `unknown`), `acquisition` {`method`, `requested_url`, `final_url`, `retrieved_at`, `retrieved_at_basis`, `raw_sha256`, `text_sha256`, `byte_size`, `private_path`}, `rights_id`, `permission_status`, `review` |

- **`text_sha256`** hashes the normalised page text. A future re-capture can then tell real
  content change apart from page noise.
- **Section-level records** (`S01.a`, …) and **extraction counts** are added when L1 is
  built.
- **`data/source_coverage.csv` columns:** `area_tier, sub_area, rule_or_fact_ids,
  essential_source_ids, supporting_source_ids, exceptions_required, exceptions_verified,
  coverage_status, evidence_gap_kind, notes`.

---

## 9. Reviewer reproducibility

| Reviewer action | Needs | Doesn't need |
|---|---|---|
| Run the app (Docker or `uv`) | Tracked L2/L3; an LLM key for live answers | L0/L1, network access to HDB |
| Re-score the evaluation | Saved predictions and labels | API key |
| Check a cited fact | The fact's URL and section in a browser | L0 |

**Not claimed:**
- Re-capturing pages later does **not** reproduce this corpus. HDB pages change without
  versions. Re-running `snapshots.py register` on a new capture only *detects* drift against
  the recorded hashes (REQ-LIC-016).
- The README states the policy period as "HDB sources retrieved 28 Oct 2026" (D-021). It
  never claims effective dates the sources don't give.
