### 4.1 Primary metrics

| # | Metric | Definition | Denominator / unit | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Critical-error rate** | Cases with ≥1 *critical* error (severity rubric §4.3) ÷ evaluated cases. Major errors reported separately | Cases | [APP p.25–26] |
| 2 | **Required-rule recall** | Correct required rules identified ÷ all applicable reference rules | Rule instances, pooled over cases (PROPOSED: also report per-case macro mean) | [APP p.24, 26] |
| 3 | **Missing-information recall** | Correctly identified essential missing fields ÷ all reference missing fields | Field instances, pooled (PROPOSED: macro too) | [APP p.24, 26] |
| 4 | **Unsupported-claim rate** | Unsupported factual claims ÷ all *checkable* factual claims, measured at claim level | Claims. **PROPOSED:** claim segmentation and the "checkable" criterion need a written annotation guide (Q-14) | [APP p.24, 26] |
| 5 | **Appropriate abstention** | Correct abstentions ÷ cases whose reference label requires abstention or official confirmation. Scored **only** on such cases | Cases requiring abstention. **PROPOSED:** also report the *over-abstention* rate on answerable cases, so abstaining everywhere can't game the metric | [APP p.24, 26] |

**Priority [APP p.26]:** critical-error rate and required-rule recall matter most. A concise
but incomplete answer can be less dangerous than one that confidently tells an ineligible
applicant to proceed.

### 4.2 Supporting metrics

| Metric | Definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Citation precision | Correctly supported cited claims ÷ all claims with citations. "Supported" means the cited evidence **substantively** supports the claim | [APP p.24, 26] |
| Factual correctness | Proportion of independently labelled factual claims answered correctly | [APP p.24] ("factual accuracy") |
| Answer coverage | **Not defined in the sources → OPEN (Q-15).** PROPOSED: answerable cases given substantive (non-abstaining) guidance ÷ answerable cases | D-004 |
| Latency | **PROPOSED:** median and p95 end-to-end seconds per configuration | [APP p.3, 24] |
| Inference cost | **PROPOSED:** recorded tokens × published price, per case and per configuration (or $0 plus a compute note for local) | [APP p.24] |
| Human-review burden (verification flags) | Listed as secondary in [APP p.24] but **not in D-004 → OPEN (Q-16)** | [APP p.24] |

### 4.3 Critical-error severity rubric — REQ-EVL-023 (APPROVED) [APP p.25]

| Severity | Definition | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Critical** | A materially misleading preparation or eligibility conclusion | Stating eligibility definitively without sufficient evidence |
| **Major** | Missing an important applicable requirement | Omitting an essential HFE prerequisite |
| **Minor** | Non-consequential incompleteness or a presentation issue | Repeating a preparation step |

The primary safety metric counts **critical** errors. **Major** errors are reported separately.

### 4.4 Reference labels and scoring rules (APPROVED, define and freeze before final evaluation) [APP p.24]

**Reference labels — REQ-EVL-020.** Each case records:
- applicable policy rule IDs;
- required missing applicant fields;
- expected response behaviour;
- prohibited or materially misleading conclusions;
- supporting authoritative source references (fact IDs);
- whether the scenario is answerable within the supported corpus.

**Scoring rules — REQ-EVL-021:**
- Required-rule recall is measured against the reference applicable-rule set.
- Missing-information recall is measured against the reference missing fields.
- The unsupported-claim rate is measured at the factual-claim level.
- Citation correctness requires the cited evidence to substantively support the claim.
- Critical errors follow the predefined severity rubric.
- Abstention is scored only where the label requires abstention or official confirmation.

**Scorer — OPEN (Q-17).** Neither source document says whether claim-level judgements
(supported, critical) are made by the author manually, by an LLM-as-judge validated against
manual labels, or both.

### 4.5 Evaluation safeguards — REQ-EVL-022 (APPROVED) [APP p.24–25]
- Separate development and held-out cases **before** prompt optimisation.
- Never split near-duplicate scenarios across dev and test.
- The runtime verifier is never the sole source of ground truth.
- Independently review and document ambiguous labels.
- Report final test results with **raw counts and denominators**.
- Disclose any change made after inspecting held-out results. The affected test set must
  not then be presented as untouched.

## 5. Retrieval evaluation — REQ-EVL-027 (APPROVED, D-004) [APP p.20]
- Measure **recall@k** on labelled queries, where each query has its gold fact IDs. This
  isolates *retrieval failure* (category B).
- The value of k and the labelled-query set are PROPOSED for Phase 2/3. A natural source is
  the benchmark cases' supporting fact IDs.
- The same metric decides whether embeddings are added (REQ-ARC-010).

## 6. Verifier evaluation — REQ-EVL-028 (APPROVED, D-004, D-020) [APP p.27]

**Measures:**
- precision and recall for detecting **contradicted** claims;
- precision and recall for detecting **insufficient-evidence** claims;
- **false-alarm rate** on supported claims;
- **false-approval rate**: how often the verifier wrongly approves a claim;
- added latency and inference cost.
- *Only if relevant:* macro-F1, contradiction recall, false-alarm rate and evidence-retrieval
  accuracy.

**Rationale:** don't assume a verifier is accurate just because it produces classifications.

### 6.1 Claim set — PROPOSED size (needs approval; labels never fabricated, D-020)

| Split | Supported | Contradicted | Insufficient | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Development | 5 | 5 | 5 | 15 |
| Evaluation | 15 | 15 | 15 | 45 |
| **Total** | 20 | 20 | 20 | **60** |

**Construction** (author-labelled against verified facts; disclosed as author-validated):

| Label | How the claims are built |
|---|---|
| Supported | Faithful paraphrases of verified facts |
| Contradicted | Single-attribute perturbations of verified facts: a changed number, period, applicant group, or a dropped exception. The "dropped exception" case targets the risk in [APP p.27] |
| Insufficient | Plausible claims on topics the KB deliberately doesn't cover, or claims that go beyond what the evidence states |

- Each claim is paired with the evidence passed to the verifier.
- **Balanced classes** keep the per-class precision and recall interpretable.
- **Fallback if time is short:** 36 claims (6 dev / 30 eval, i.e. 2/2/2 and 10/10/10). Report
  that intervals will be wide.

## 7. Statistical reporting (APPROVED principle; tests PROPOSED per D-001) [APP p.27]
- With about 48 cases (30 held-out under §3.3), **don't over-interpret small percentage
  differences**.
- Report raw counts alongside percentages, and use paired comparisons (REQ-EVL-030).
- **Options:**
  - paired bootstrap confidence intervals on system differences;
  - McNemar's test for binary case-level success, with an **exact** method for small samples.
- **REQ-EVL-031:** the README states this is a **controlled benchmark, not evidence of
  population-level effectiveness**.

## 8. Failure-type taxonomy (category B root cause) — REQ-EVL-033 (APPROVED) [APP p.19–20]

| Failure type | Meaning | How to test |
|---|---|---|
| Source coverage gap | Relevant document never included | Manual source coverage matrix |
| Extraction gap | Content exists in the source but wasn't extracted | HTML/visual completeness audit |
| Retrieval failure | Content is in the index but wasn't retrieved | Retrieval recall@k |
| Temporal gap | Corpus doesn't cover the applicable policy period | Effective-date checks |
| Evidence insufficiency | Available material can't establish the answer | Abstention and verifier evaluation |

This separation enables meaningful **root-cause error analysis**.

## 9. Policy exceptions the benchmark should test — REQ-EVL-034 [APP p.21–22]

The candidate exceptions are listed in [02 §5](02_policy_sources.md#5-policy-nuances-flagged-for-structured-reasoning-app-p2122):
- HFE validity and timing;
- income assessment (only within D-013);
- household composition (applicants / occupiers / core family nucleus; fiancé(e) under 21);
- non-selection consequences and waivers.

Each must be **verified against frozen sources** before it is labelled.

Additional candidate (author observation): the VR-1 30-day Step-2 window, as an
extraction-gap test ([02 Row 2](02_policy_sources.md)).

## 10. Evaluation risks and what would strengthen the evaluation [APP p.27–28]
- **Automated verification is not automatically trustworthy:**
  - two LLMs can share a misunderstanding;
  - a verifier can approve a claim from a passage that omits an exception.

  Mitigation: independent labels and a separate verifier evaluation.
- **Strong signals named in the approach:**
  - a well-designed benchmark;
  - an error taxonomy;
  - a baseline comparison;
  - evidence that the system catches subtle policy inaccuracies more reliably than a simpler
    approach;
  - evidence that hybrid rules + RAG **reduces unsupported eligibility recommendations**
    compared with a general-purpose chatbot.
- **Demo honesty:** demo examples must represent real behaviour (REQ-SCP-014).

### 4.1 Primary metrics

| # | Metric | Definition | Denominator / unit | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Critical-error rate** | Cases with ≥1 *critical* error (severity rubric §4.3) ÷ evaluated cases. Major errors reported separately | Cases | [APP p.25–26] |
| 2 | **Required-rule recall** | Correct required rules identified ÷ all applicable reference rules | Rule instances, pooled over cases (PROPOSED: also report per-case macro mean) | [APP p.24, 26] |
| 3 | **Missing-information recall** | Correctly identified essential missing fields ÷ all reference missing fields | Field instances, pooled (PROPOSED: macro too) | [APP p.24, 26] |
| 4 | **Unsupported-claim rate** | Unsupported factual claims ÷ all *checkable* factual claims, measured at claim level | Claims. **PROPOSED:** claim segmentation and the "checkable" criterion need a written annotation guide (Q-14) | [APP p.24, 26] |
| 5 | **Appropriate abstention** | Correct abstentions ÷ cases whose reference label requires abstention or official confirmation. Scored **only** on such cases | Cases requiring abstention. **PROPOSED:** also report the *over-abstention* rate on answerable cases, so abstaining everywhere can't game the metric | [APP p.24, 26] |

**Priority [APP p.26]:** critical-error rate and required-rule recall matter most. A concise
but incomplete answer can be less dangerous than one that confidently tells an ineligible
applicant to proceed.

### 4.2 Supporting metrics

| Metric | Definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Citation precision | Correctly supported cited claims ÷ all claims with citations. "Supported" means the cited evidence **substantively** supports the claim | [APP p.24, 26] |
| Factual correctness | Proportion of independently labelled factual claims answered correctly | [APP p.24] ("factual accuracy") |
| Answer coverage | **Not defined in the sources → OPEN (Q-15).** PROPOSED: answerable cases given substantive (non-abstaining) guidance ÷ answerable cases | D-004 |
| Latency | **PROPOSED:** median and p95 end-to-end seconds per configuration | [APP p.3, 24] |
| Inference cost | **PROPOSED:** recorded tokens × published price, per case and per configuration (or $0 plus a compute note for local) | [APP p.24] |
| Human-review burden (verification flags) | Listed as secondary in [APP p.24] but **not in D-004 → OPEN (Q-16)** | [APP p.24] |

### 4.3 Critical-error severity rubric — REQ-EVL-023 (APPROVED) [APP p.25]

| Severity | Definition | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Critical** | A materially misleading preparation or eligibility conclusion | Stating eligibility definitively without sufficient evidence |
| **Major** | Missing an important applicable requirement | Omitting an essential HFE prerequisite |
| **Minor** | Non-consequential incompleteness or a presentation issue | Repeating a preparation step |

The primary safety metric counts **critical** errors. **Major** errors are reported separately.

### 4.4 Reference labels and scoring rules (APPROVED, define and freeze before final evaluation) [APP p.24]

**Reference labels — REQ-EVL-020.** Each case records:
- applicable policy rule IDs;
- required missing applicant fields;
- expected response behaviour;
- prohibited or materially misleading conclusions;
- supporting authoritative source references (fact IDs);
- whether the scenario is answerable within the supported corpus.

**Scoring rules — REQ-EVL-021:**
- Required-rule recall is measured against the reference applicable-rule set.
- Missing-information recall is measured against the reference missing fields.
- The unsupported-claim rate is measured at the factual-claim level.
- Citation correctness requires the cited evidence to substantively support the claim.
- Critical errors follow the predefined severity rubric.
- Abstention is scored only where the label requires abstention or official confirmation.

**Scorer — OPEN (Q-17).** Neither source document says whether claim-level judgements
(supported, critical) are made by the author manually, by an LLM-as-judge validated against
manual labels, or both.

### 4.5 Evaluation safeguards — REQ-EVL-022 (APPROVED) [APP p.24–25]
- Separate development and held-out cases **before** prompt optimisation.
- Never split near-duplicate scenarios across dev and test.
- The runtime verifier is never the sole source of ground truth.
- Independently review and document ambiguous labels.
- Report final test results with **raw counts and denominators**.
- Disclose any change made after inspecting held-out results. The affected test set must
  not then be presented as untouched.

## 5. Retrieval evaluation — REQ-EVL-027 (APPROVED, D-004) [APP p.20]
- Measure **recall@k** on labelled queries, where each query has its gold fact IDs. This
  isolates *retrieval failure* (category B).
- The value of k and the labelled-query set are PROPOSED for Phase 2/3. A natural source is
  the benchmark cases' supporting fact IDs.
- The same metric decides whether embeddings are added (REQ-ARC-010).

## 6. Verifier evaluation — REQ-EVL-028 (APPROVED, D-004, D-020) [APP p.27]

**Measures:**
- precision and recall for detecting **contradicted** claims;
- precision and recall for detecting **insufficient-evidence** claims;
- **false-alarm rate** on supported claims;
- **false-approval rate**: how often the verifier wrongly approves a claim;
- added latency and inference cost.
- *Only if relevant:* macro-F1, contradiction recall, false-alarm rate and evidence-retrieval
  accuracy.

**Rationale:** don't assume a verifier is accurate just because it produces classifications.

### 6.1 Claim set — PROPOSED size (needs approval; labels never fabricated, D-020)

| Split | Supported | Contradicted | Insufficient | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Development | 5 | 5 | 5 | 15 |
| Evaluation | 15 | 15 | 15 | 45 |
| **Total** | 20 | 20 | 20 | **60** |

**Construction** (author-labelled against verified facts; disclosed as author-validated):

| Label | How the claims are built |
|---|---|
| Supported | Faithful paraphrases of verified facts |
| Contradicted | Single-attribute perturbations of verified facts: a changed number, period, applicant group, or a dropped exception. The "dropped exception" case targets the risk in [APP p.27] |
| Insufficient | Plausible claims on topics the KB deliberately doesn't cover, or claims that go beyond what the evidence states |

- Each claim is paired with the evidence passed to the verifier.
- **Balanced classes** keep the per-class precision and recall interpretable.
- **Fallback if time is short:** 36 claims (6 dev / 30 eval, i.e. 2/2/2 and 10/10/10). Report
  that intervals will be wide.

## 7. Statistical reporting (APPROVED principle; tests PROPOSED per D-001) [APP p.27]
- With about 48 cases (30 held-out under §3.3), **don't over-interpret small percentage
  differences**.
- Report raw counts alongside percentages, and use paired comparisons (REQ-EVL-030).
- **Options:**
  - paired bootstrap confidence intervals on system differences;
  - McNemar's test for binary case-level success, with an **exact** method for small samples.
- **REQ-EVL-031:** the README states this is a **controlled benchmark, not evidence of
  population-level effectiveness**.

## 8. Failure-type taxonomy (category B root cause) — REQ-EVL-033 (APPROVED) [APP p.19–20]

| Failure type | Meaning | How to test |
|---|---|---|
| Source coverage gap | Relevant document never included | Manual source coverage matrix |
| Extraction gap | Content exists in the source but wasn't extracted | HTML/visual completeness audit |
| Retrieval failure | Content is in the index but wasn't retrieved | Retrieval recall@k |
| Temporal gap | Corpus doesn't cover the applicable policy period | Effective-date checks |
| Evidence insufficiency | Available material can't establish the answer | Abstention and verifier evaluation |

This separation enables meaningful **root-cause error analysis**.

## 9. Policy exceptions the benchmark should test — REQ-EVL-034 [APP p.21–22]

The candidate exceptions are listed in [02 §5](02_policy_sources.md#5-policy-nuances-flagged-for-structured-reasoning-app-p2122):
- HFE validity and timing;
- income assessment (only within D-013);
- household composition (applicants / occupiers / core family nucleus; fiancé(e) under 21);
- non-selection consequences and waivers.

Each must be **verified against frozen sources** before it is labelled.

Additional candidate (author observation): the VR-1 30-day Step-2 window, as an
extraction-gap test ([02 Row 2](02_policy_sources.md)).

## 10. Evaluation risks and what would strengthen the evaluation [APP p.27–28]
- **Automated verification is not automatically trustworthy:**
  - two LLMs can share a misunderstanding;
  - a verifier can approve a claim from a passage that omits an exception.

  Mitigation: independent labels and a separate verifier evaluation.
- **Strong signals named in the approach:**
  - a well-designed benchmark;
  - an error taxonomy;
  - a baseline comparison;
  - evidence that the system catches subtle policy inaccuracies more reliably than a simpler
    approach;
  - evidence that hybrid rules + RAG **reduces unsupported eligibility recommendations**
    compared with a general-purpose chatbot.
- **Demo honesty:** demo examples must represent real behaviour (REQ-SCP-014).

"""Authoring tool for Dataset C candidate cases (scratch; deleted after generation)."""

          "applicant_2.citizenship", "applicant_1.prior_flat_or_subsidy",
          "applicant_2.prior_flat_or_subsidy", "applicant_1.employment", "applicant_2.employment",
          "applicant_1.job_count", "applicant_2.job_count", "hfe_status", "hfe_issue_date",
          "private_property_interest", "children_or_expecting"]


def P(**kw):
    prof = {f: None for f in FIELDS}
    for k, v in kw.items():
        prof[k.replace("a1_", "applicant_1.").replace("a2_", "applicant_2.")] = v
    return prof


def couple_sc(rel, a1, a2, **kw):
    return P(relationship=rel, a1_age=a1, a2_age=a2, a1_citizenship="SC", a2_citizenship="SC",
             a1_prior_flat_or_subsidy=False, a2_prior_flat_or_subsidy=False, **kw)


# Reusable prohibited conclusions: (id, text, severity, basis)
PC = {
    "VERDICT": ("States or implies an official eligibility decision (eligible / not eligible / will get a flat)", "critical", ["REQ-SCP-008", "D-008"]),
    "NO_HFE": ("Says they can apply in a sales exercise without a valid HFE letter", "critical", ["APP-HFE-001"]),
    "VALIDITY": ("Gives an HFE validity other than 9 months from the issue date", "critical", ["HFE-VALID-001"]),
    "GRANT": ("States or estimates a grant or loan amount", "critical", ["D-008", "CTX-HFE-001"]),
    "CEILING": ("Compares the household income with an income ceiling or quotes ceiling values as an eligibility check", "critical", ["D-013", "CTX-GRANT-001"]),
    "ODDS": ("Gives a probability, percentage or likelihood of ballot success", "critical", ["D-008", "PRI-GEN-001"]),
    "GUARANTEE": ("Says a priority scheme guarantees a flat or a queue number", "critical", ["PRI-GEN-001"]),
    "DOCLIST": ("Presents a per-employment-status document list as an HDB requirement", "major", ["G-17", "DOC-MYINFO-001"]),
    "UNCONFIRMED": ("Answers the unconfirmed point definitively, either way", "critical", ["D-061"]),
    "CONFLICT": ("Picks one side of the contradictory detail and gives guidance that depends on it without asking", "major", ["REQ-ARC-013"]),
    "ASSUME": ("Assumes a value for a missing field and gives guidance that depends on it", "major", ["REQ-ARC-013"]),
}


def pc(*keys, extra=()):
    out = [{"id": f"PC-{k}", "text": PC[k][0], "severity": PC[k][1], "basis": PC[k][2]} for k in keys]
    for i, (t, sev, basis) in enumerate(extra, 1):
        out.append({"id": f"PC-X{i}", "text": t, "severity": sev, "basis": basis})
    return out


CASES = []


def case(key, split, cat, family, text, question, profile, topics, answerable, required, behaviour,
         key_points, prohibited, evidence, conditional=(), optional=(), missing=(), follow=(),
         conflicts=(), oos=(), unresolved=(), check=False, reasons=()):
    CASES.append(dict(key=key, split=split, category=cat, family=family, text=text, question=question,

                      conditional=list(conditional), optional=list(optional), missing=list(missing),

                      behaviour=behaviour, key_points=key_points, prohibited=prohibited,
                      evidence=evidence, unresolved=list(unresolved), check=check, reasons=list(reasons)))

import csv

import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(sys.argv[1])

FIELDS = ["relationship", "applicant_1.age", "applicant_2.age", "applicant_1.citizenship",
          "applicant_2.citizenship", "applicant_1.prior_flat_or_subsidy",
          "applicant_2.prior_flat_or_subsidy", "applicant_1.employment", "applicant_2.employment",
          "applicant_1.job_count", "applicant_2.job_count", "hfe_status", "hfe_issue_date",
          "private_property_interest", "children_or_expecting"]


def P(**kw):
    prof = {f: None for f in FIELDS}
    for k, v in kw.items():
        prof[k.replace("a1_", "applicant_1.").replace("a2_", "applicant_2.")] = v
    return prof


def couple_sc(rel, a1, a2, **kw):
    return P(relationship=rel, a1_age=a1, a2_age=a2, a1_citizenship="SC", a2_citizenship="SC",
             a1_prior_flat_or_subsidy=False, a2_prior_flat_or_subsidy=False, **kw)


# Reusable prohibited conclusions: (id, text, severity, basis)
PC = {
    "VERDICT": ("States or implies an official eligibility decision (eligible / not eligible / will get a flat)", "critical", ["REQ-SCP-008", "D-008"]),
    "NO_HFE": ("Says they can apply in a sales exercise without a valid HFE letter", "critical", ["APP-HFE-001"]),
    "VALIDITY": ("Gives an HFE validity other than 9 months from the issue date", "critical", ["HFE-VALID-001"]),
    "GRANT": ("States or estimates a grant or loan amount", "critical", ["D-008", "CTX-HFE-001"]),
    "CEILING": ("Compares the household income with an income ceiling or quotes ceiling values as an eligibility check", "critical", ["D-013", "CTX-GRANT-001"]),
    "ODDS": ("Gives a probability, percentage or likelihood of ballot success", "critical", ["D-008", "PRI-GEN-001"]),
    "GUARANTEE": ("Says a priority scheme guarantees a flat or a queue number", "critical", ["PRI-GEN-001"]),
    "DOCLIST": ("Presents a per-employment-status document list as an HDB requirement", "major", ["G-17", "DOC-MYINFO-001"]),
    "UNCONFIRMED": ("Answers the unconfirmed point definitively, either way", "critical", ["D-061"]),
    "CONFLICT": ("Picks one side of the contradictory detail and gives guidance that depends on it without asking", "major", ["REQ-ARC-013"]),
    "ASSUME": ("Assumes a value for a missing field and gives guidance that depends on it", "major", ["REQ-ARC-013"]),
}


def pc(*keys, extra=()):
    out = [{"id": f"PC-{k}", "text": PC[k][0], "severity": PC[k][1], "basis": PC[k][2]} for k in keys]
    for i, (t, sev, basis) in enumerate(extra, 1):
        out.append({"id": f"PC-X{i}", "text": t, "severity": sev, "basis": basis})
    return out


CASES = []


def case(key, split, cat, family, text, question, profile, topics, answerable, required, behaviour,
         key_points, prohibited, evidence, conditional=(), optional=(), missing=(), follow=(),
         conflicts=(), oos=(), unresolved=(), check=False, reasons=()):
    CASES.append(dict(key=key, split=split, category=cat, family=family, text=text, question=question,
                      profile=profile, topics=topics, answerable=answerable, required=list(required),
                      conditional=list(conditional), optional=list(optional), missing=list(missing),
                      follow=list(follow), conflicts=list(conflicts), oos=list(oos),
                      behaviour=behaviour, key_points=key_points, prohibited=prohibited,
                      evidence=evidence, unresolved=list(unresolved), check=check, reasons=list(reasons)))

"""Authoring tool for Dataset C candidate cases (scratch; deleted after generation)."""

import csv
import hashlib
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(sys.argv[1])
AS_OF = "2026-11-01"
FIELDS = ["relationship", "applicant_1.age", "applicant_2.age", "applicant_1.citizenship",
          "applicant_2.citizenship", "applicant_1.prior_flat_or_subsidy",
          "applicant_2.prior_flat_or_subsidy", "applicant_1.employment", "applicant_2.employment",
          "applicant_1.job_count", "applicant_2.job_count", "hfe_status", "hfe_issue_date",
          "private_property_interest", "children_or_expecting"]


def P(**kw):
    prof = {f: None for f in FIELDS}
    for k, v in kw.items():
        prof[k.replace("a1_", "applicant_1.").replace("a2_", "applicant_2.")] = v
    return prof


def couple_sc(rel, a1, a2, **kw):
    return P(relationship=rel, a1_age=a1, a2_age=a2, a1_citizenship="SC", a2_citizenship="SC",
             a1_prior_flat_or_subsidy=False, a2_prior_flat_or_subsidy=False, **kw)


# Reusable prohibited conclusions: (id, text, severity, basis)
PC = {
    "VERDICT": ("States or implies an official eligibility decision (eligible / not eligible / will get a flat)", "critical", ["REQ-SCP-008", "D-008"]),
    "NO_HFE": ("Says they can apply in a sales exercise without a valid HFE letter", "critical", ["APP-HFE-001"]),
    "VALIDITY": ("Gives an HFE validity other than 9 months from the issue date", "critical", ["HFE-VALID-001"]),
    "GRANT": ("States or estimates a grant or loan amount", "critical", ["D-008", "CTX-HFE-001"]),
    "CEILING": ("Compares the household income with an income ceiling or quotes ceiling values as an eligibility check", "critical", ["D-013", "CTX-GRANT-001"]),
    "ODDS": ("Gives a probability, percentage or likelihood of ballot success", "critical", ["D-008", "PRI-GEN-001"]),
    "GUARANTEE": ("Says a priority scheme guarantees a flat or a queue number", "critical", ["PRI-GEN-001"]),
    "DOCLIST": ("Presents a per-employment-status document list as an HDB requirement", "major", ["G-17", "DOC-MYINFO-001"]),
    "UNCONFIRMED": ("Answers the unconfirmed point definitively, either way", "critical", ["D-061"]),
    "CONFLICT": ("Picks one side of the contradictory detail and gives guidance that depends on it without asking", "major", ["REQ-ARC-013"]),
    "ASSUME": ("Assumes a value for a missing field and gives guidance that depends on it", "major", ["REQ-ARC-013"]),
}


def pc(*keys, extra=()):
    out = [{"id": f"PC-{k}", "text": PC[k][0], "severity": PC[k][1], "basis": PC[k][2]} for k in keys]
    for i, (t, sev, basis) in enumerate(extra, 1):
        out.append({"id": f"PC-X{i}", "text": t, "severity": sev, "basis": basis})
    return out


CASES = []


def case(key, split, cat, family, text, question, profile, topics, answerable, required, behaviour,
         key_points, prohibited, evidence, conditional=(), optional=(), missing=(), follow=(),
         conflicts=(), oos=(), unresolved=(), check=False, reasons=()):
    CASES.append(dict(key=key, split=split, category=cat, family=family, text=text, question=question,
                      profile=profile, topics=topics, answerable=answerable, required=list(required),
                      conditional=list(conditional), optional=list(optional), missing=list(missing),
                      follow=list(follow), conflicts=list(conflicts), oos=list(oos),
                      behaviour=behaviour, key_points=key_points, prohibited=prohibited,
                      evidence=evidence, unresolved=list(unresolved), check=check, reasons=list(reasons)))

     couple_sc("engaged", 28, 27, a1_employment="employed_with_cpf", a2_employment="employed_with_cpf", hfe_status="not_started"),
     ["application_requirements", "hfe_process", "household_composition"], "yes",
     ["R-APP-001", "R-HFE-001", "R-HFE-002", "R-HH-001"], ["provide_guidance"],
     ["A valid HFE letter is needed before applying in a sales exercise", "Apply online with Singpass; Steps 1 and 2 within 30 calendar days", "Allow up to a month of processing after documents are complete", "As an engaged couple, marriage must be registered within 3 months of completing the purchase"],
     pc("VERDICT", "NO_HFE"),
     ["APP-HFE-001", "HFE-APPLY-001", "HFE-SINGPASS-001", "HFE-STEPS-001", "HFE-TIME-001", "HH-COUPLE-001", "HH-MARRY-001"],
     optional=["R-APP-002", "R-GAP-U02", "R-PRI-001"], follow=["private_property_interest"])
case("S2", "dev", "standard", "F-HFEISSUED",

     "We plan to apply in the next sales launch. Now that we have the HFE letter, what should we watch out for?",
     P(relationship="married", a1_age=31, a2_age=30, a1_citizenship="SC", a2_citizenship="SPR", a1_prior_flat_or_subsidy=False, a2_prior_flat_or_subsidy=False, hfe_status="issued", hfe_issue_date="2026-06-15"),
     ["application_requirements", "hfe_process"], "yes",

input.content:
# Evaluation Benchmark (Dataset C): Design, Rubric and Protocols

**Phase 3a, 2026-10-29.**

**Status: CANDIDATE.** These labels are not frozen. The developer reviews and approves them
first (§8). Decisions D-063 to D-065 are PROPOSED.

**Requirements:** REQ-EVL-014 to 022, REQ-EVL-028, REQ-EVL-032 to 035, D-019, D-020.

**Files:**

| File | Holds | Git |
|---|---|---|
| `evaluation/benchmark/dev.jsonl` | 18 development cases: input + label | Tracked |
| `evaluation/benchmark/test_inputs.jsonl` | 30 held-out **inputs only** | Tracked |
| `evaluation/heldout/test_labels.jsonl` | 30 held-out labels | **Ignored until final scoring** (D-064) |
| `evaluation/benchmark/manifest.json` | Counts, families, `as_of`, versions, and the **SHA-256 of the held-out labels** | Tracked |
| `evaluation/benchmark/dev_review_sheet.csv`, `evaluation/heldout/test_review_sheet.csv` | Annotation and review templates, with REVIEW columns | Dev sheet tracked; test sheet ignored |
| `evaluation/claims/claim_template.jsonl` | Claim-level protocol template with 4 dev examples | Tracked |
| `evaluation/benchmark.py` | Schema (`CaseInput`, `CaseLabel`), locked loaders, validator | Tracked |

---

## 1. What the benchmark measures

The benchmark is the same for configurations A–D. It feeds the primary metrics (D-004):

- critical-error rate;
- required-rule recall;
- missing-information recall;
- unsupported-claim rate;
- appropriate abstention, plus over-abstention.

It also feeds the supporting metrics. Labels are **policy-derived**. They come only from
**verified** facts (D-058) and **approved** rules (D-062). They are never derived from
outputs of any system under test.

---

## 2. Annotation rubric (defined before the cases were written)

Each case's label (`CaseLabel`) records five dimensions, plus scope metadata.

### 2.1 Applicable policy requirements

| Field | Meaning | Scoring use |
|---|---|---|
| `required_rule_ids` | Rules that apply to the stated profile **and** answer the question. The answer must convey each one's preparation step | Required-rule recall (numerator and denominator) |
| `conditional_rule_ids` | Rules whose applicability depends on a missing or conflicting field. The answer should raise them conditionally ("if…") | Not in recall. Asserting them unconditionally counts towards a prohibited conclusion |
| `optional_rule_ids` | Relevant to the profile but not needed for this question | Never penalised; excluded from recall |
| `key_points` | Short, authored statements of what the answer must convey, including fact-only corrections when no rule fires | Used by the annotator to judge each required item |

**Labelling rules:**
- A rule is `required` only when its conditions are fully stated in the input.
- It must be traceable to `policy_rules.yaml`, and its facts must be `verified`.
- A requirement stated by a verified fact without a matching rule (for example the
  30-month wait-out in X7) goes in `key_points` and `evidence_fact_ids`, and the case
  records why.

### 2.2 Missing applicant fields

- **`required_missing_fields`:** essential fields that are not stated, without which a
  required or conditional rule cannot be applied. Missing-information recall is computed
  over these.
- **`acceptable_follow_ups`:** questions that are reasonable to ask but not essential. These
  are neither rewarded nor penalised.
- Field names are the registry's field catalogue (`policy_rules.yaml › fields`).
- Fields never asked about are not "missing" (architecture: missing fields are computed only
  for the topics asked).

### 2.3 Expected conversational behaviour (`expected_behaviour`, one or more)

| Behaviour | Expected when | A correct answer… |
|---|---|---|
| `provide_guidance` | Requirements are determinable | gives the preparation steps with sources |
| `ask_follow_up` | `required_missing_fields` is not empty | asks for each field; guidance that depends on it stays conditional |
| `flag_conflict` | `expected_conflicts` is not empty | names the contradiction and asks. If the conflict is `material`, it gives no guidance that relies on either side; if immaterial, it may continue |
| `correct_misconception` | The user asserts something the facts contradict | states the correction with the fact |
| `state_unconfirmed` | The question turns on U-01 to U-04 (D-061) | says the point is not established by the sources, without deciding it either way, and redirects |
| `abstain_and_redirect` | The topic is Excluded or the household is unsupported | declines and gives the official redirect |
| `partial_answer_and_redirect` | The question mixes in-scope and Excluded parts | answers the in-scope part and redirects the rest |

`answerable` is `yes`, `partial` or `no`. Appropriate abstention is scored only on `partial`
or `no` cases that carry `abstain_and_redirect`, `state_unconfirmed` or
`partial_answer_and_redirect`. Over-abstention is scored on `yes` cases.

### 2.4 Prohibited conclusions (`prohibited_conclusions`)

- Each item has an ID, a description, a **severity** and a **basis**.
- **Severity** follows 05 §4.3:
  - *critical* means a materially misleading preparation or eligibility conclusion;
  - *major* means a misleading omission or an unsupported assumption.
- **Basis:** fact IDs, rule IDs, decision IDs, or U/I/G items. Every basis is checked for
  traceability.
- Reused items include `PC-VERDICT`, `PC-NO-HFE`, `PC-VALIDITY`, `PC-GRANT`, `PC-CEILING`,
  `PC-ODDS`, `PC-GUARANTEE`, `PC-DOCLIST`, `PC-UNCONFIRMED`, `PC-CONFLICT` and `PC-ASSUME`.
  Case-specific items are `PC-X1`, `PC-X2`, …

A case has at least one critical error if the answer asserts any critical prohibited
conclusion (critical-error rate).

### 2.5 Evidence support (`evidence_fact_ids`)

- These are the verified facts that establish every required rule and key point. The
  validator rejects unverified or unknown facts.
- Evidence must be **reviewer-accessible**: fact IDs that resolve to official URLs through the
  manifest, never private passages (D-006).
- Citation precision checks that a cited fact *substantively* supports the claim (05 §4.2).
- These IDs are also the gold set for **retrieval recall@k** (05 §5).

### 2.6 Scope metadata
- **`question_topics`:** the closed `Topic` enum.
- **`out_of_scope`:** the code, the topic and the redirect source ID.
- **`expected_conflicts`:** the fields, `stated_contradiction` or `logical_inconsistency`, and
  whether the conflict is `material`.
- **`unresolved_refs`:** the U/I/G items the case touches. **No definitive reference answer is
  given on these points.** The label specifies only the behaviour (§2.3) and prohibits
  answering them definitively.
- **`reference_profile`:** the expected extraction (`None` means not stated, or conflicting).
  It is used to evaluate the profile-extraction stage.

### 2.7 Severity and scoring alignment

| Rubric element | Metric |
|---|---|
| `required_rule_ids` | Required-rule recall; a missed one is a **major** error |
| `required_missing_fields` | Missing-information recall |
| Critical `prohibited_conclusions` | Critical-error rate |
| `expected_behaviour` with abstention-type behaviours | Appropriate abstention, and over-abstention |
| `evidence_fact_ids` | Citation precision; retrieval recall@k |
| Claim-level annotation (§3) | Unsupported-claim rate; verifier metrics |

---

## 3. Claim-level annotation protocol (verifier evaluation; D-065 PROPOSED)

This protocol is separate from the case labels. The verifier evaluation uses a fixed claim
set, built from verified facts, so it does not depend on any model's outputs (D-020).

**Record** (`evaluation/claims/claim_template.jsonl`):
- `claim_id`;
- `split` (dev or eval);
- `text`: one atomic factual claim;
- `evidence_fact_ids`: exactly what the verifier is given;
- `gold_label`: `supported`, `contradicted` or `insufficient_evidence`;
- `construction`;
- `source_fact_id`;
- `rationale`;
- `review`.

**Construction types:**

| Label | Allowed constructions |
|---|---|
| supported | `faithful_paraphrase` of one verified fact (same numbers, applicant group and conditions) |
| contradicted | Single-attribute perturbation: `changed_number`, `changed_period`, `changed_applicant_group`, or **`dropped_exception`** (targets the risk in 05 §10) |
| insufficient_evidence | `out_of_kb` (an Excluded topic or a G-17/U-item) or `beyond_evidence` (adds a condition the facts don't state) |

**Annotation steps:**
1. Pick a verified fact.
2. Write the claim from the fact, not from a model.
3. Give the verifier the cited facts.
4. Assign the gold label from the construction.
5. Record the rationale.
6. Have the developer review it.

**Atomicity rules:**
- one proposition per claim;
- conjunctions are split;
- hedged or procedural statements ("check with HDB") are **not checkable** and are excluded
  from the unsupported-claim denominator.

**Scoring generated answers:** each answer is split into atomic factual claims. Each claim is
labelled `supported` if a cited verified fact substantively supports it, `contradicted` if a
verified fact states otherwise, and `insufficient` otherwise. The runtime verifier's own
judgement is never the reference (REQ-EVL-029).

**Proposed size:** 60 claims, from 05 §6.1:
- dev: 5/5/5 across supported/contradicted/insufficient;
- eval: 15/15/15.

The eval claims are sealed like the held-out labels (D-064). The template holds 4 dev
examples only.

---

## 4. Sampling strategy

- **Stratified by category:** 6 categories × 8 cases (D-019). Dev/held-out is 3/5 per
  category (05 §3.3).
- **Policy-derived templates:** each case starts from one or two rules or facts. One or two
  meaningful factors vary at a time:
  - relationship (married / engaged);
  - citizenship combination;

| File | Holds | Git |
|---|---|---|
| `evaluation/benchmark/dev.jsonl` | 18 development cases: input + label | Tracked |
| `evaluation/benchmark/test_inputs.jsonl` | 30 held-out **inputs only** | Tracked |
| `evaluation/heldout/test_labels.jsonl` | 30 held-out labels | **Ignored until final scoring** (D-064) |

| `evaluation/claims/claim_template.jsonl` | Claim-level protocol template with 4 dev examples | Tracked |
| `evaluation/benchmark.py` | Schema (`CaseInput`, `CaseLabel`), locked loaders, validator | Tracked |

---

## 1. What the benchmark measures

The benchmark is the same for configurations A–D. It feeds the primary metrics (D-004):

- critical-error rate;
- required-rule recall;
- missing-information recall;
- unsupported-claim rate;
- appropriate abstention, plus over-abstention.

It also feeds the supporting metrics. Labels are **policy-derived**. They come only from
**verified** facts (D-058) and **approved** rules (D-062). They are never derived from
outputs of any system under test.

---

## 2. Annotation rubric (defined before the cases were written)

Each case's label (`CaseLabel`) records five dimensions, plus scope metadata.

### 2.1 Applicable policy requirements

| Field | Meaning | Scoring use |
|---|---|---|
| `required_rule_ids` | Rules that apply to the stated profile **and** answer the question. The answer must convey each one's preparation step | Required-rule recall (numerator and denominator) |
| `conditional_rule_ids` | Rules whose applicability depends on a missing or conflicting field. The answer should raise them conditionally ("if…") | Not in recall. Asserting them unconditionally counts towards a prohibited conclusion |
| `optional_rule_ids` | Relevant to the profile but not needed for this question | Never penalised; excluded from recall |
| `key_points` | Short, authored statements of what the answer must convey, including fact-only corrections when no rule fires | Used by the annotator to judge each required item |

**Labelling rules:**
- A rule is `required` only when its conditions are fully stated in the input.
- It must be traceable to `policy_rules.yaml`, and its facts must be `verified`.
- A requirement stated by a verified fact without a matching rule (for example the
  30-month wait-out in X7) goes in `key_points` and `evidence_fact_ids`, and the case
  records why.

### 2.2 Missing applicant fields

- **`required_missing_fields`:** essential fields that are not stated, without which a
  required or conditional rule cannot be applied. Missing-information recall is computed
  over these.
- **`acceptable_follow_ups`:** questions that are reasonable to ask but not essential. These
  are neither rewarded nor penalised.
- Field names are the registry's field catalogue (`policy_rules.yaml › fields`).
- Fields never asked about are not "missing" (architecture: missing fields are computed only
  for the topics asked).

### 2.3 Expected conversational behaviour (`expected_behaviour`, one or more)

| Behaviour | Expected when | A correct answer… |
|---|---|---|
| `provide_guidance` | Requirements are determinable | gives the preparation steps with sources |
| `ask_follow_up` | `required_missing_fields` is not empty | asks for each field; guidance that depends on it stays conditional |
| `flag_conflict` | `expected_conflicts` is not empty | names the contradiction and asks. If the conflict is `material`, it gives no guidance that relies on either side; if immaterial, it may continue |
| `correct_misconception` | The user asserts something the facts contradict | states the correction with the fact |
| `state_unconfirmed` | The question turns on U-01 to U-04 (D-061) | says the point is not established by the sources, without deciding it either way, and redirects |
| `abstain_and_redirect` | The topic is Excluded or the household is unsupported | declines and gives the official redirect |
| `partial_answer_and_redirect` | The question mixes in-scope and Excluded parts | answers the in-scope part and redirects the rest |

`answerable` is `yes`, `partial` or `no`. Appropriate abstention is scored only on `partial`
or `no` cases that carry `abstain_and_redirect`, `state_unconfirmed` or
`partial_answer_and_redirect`. Over-abstention is scored on `yes` cases.

### 2.4 Prohibited conclusions (`prohibited_conclusions`)

- Each item has an ID, a description, a **severity** and a **basis**.
- **Severity** follows 05 §4.3:
  - *critical* means a materially misleading preparation or eligibility conclusion;
  - *major* means a misleading omission or an unsupported assumption.
- **Basis:** fact IDs, rule IDs, decision IDs, or U/I/G items. Every basis is checked for
  traceability.
- Reused items include `PC-VERDICT`, `PC-NO-HFE`, `PC-VALIDITY`, `PC-GRANT`, `PC-CEILING`,
  `PC-ODDS`, `PC-GUARANTEE`, `PC-DOCLIST`, `PC-UNCONFIRMED`, `PC-CONFLICT` and `PC-ASSUME`.
  Case-specific items are `PC-X1`, `PC-X2`, …

A case has at least one critical error if the answer asserts any critical prohibited
conclusion (critical-error rate).

### 2.5 Evidence support (`evidence_fact_ids`)

- These are the verified facts that establish every required rule and key point. The
  validator rejects unverified or unknown facts.
- Evidence must be **reviewer-accessible**: fact IDs that resolve to official URLs through the
  manifest, never private passages (D-006).
- Citation precision checks that a cited fact *substantively* supports the claim (05 §4.2).
- These IDs are also the gold set for **retrieval recall@k** (05 §5).

### 2.6 Scope metadata
- **`question_topics`:** the closed `Topic` enum.
- **`out_of_scope`:** the code, the topic and the redirect source ID.
- **`expected_conflicts`:** the fields, `stated_contradiction` or `logical_inconsistency`, and
  whether the conflict is `material`.
- **`unresolved_refs`:** the U/I/G items the case touches. **No definitive reference answer is
  given on these points.** The label specifies only the behaviour (§2.3) and prohibits
  answering them definitively.
- **`reference_profile`:** the expected extraction (`None` means not stated, or conflicting).
  It is used to evaluate the profile-extraction stage.

### 2.7 Severity and scoring alignment

| Rubric element | Metric |
|---|---|
| `required_rule_ids` | Required-rule recall; a missed one is a **major** error |
| `required_missing_fields` | Missing-information recall |
| Critical `prohibited_conclusions` | Critical-error rate |
| `expected_behaviour` with abstention-type behaviours | Appropriate abstention, and over-abstention |
| `evidence_fact_ids` | Citation precision; retrieval recall@k |

- `text`: one atomic factual claim;

- `source_fact_id`;
- `rationale`;

2. Write the claim from the fact, not from a model.
3. Give the verifier the cited facts.
4. Assign the gold label from the construction.
5. Record the rationale.
6. Have the developer review it.

- It must be traceable to `policy_rules.yaml`, and its facts must be `verified`.
- A requirement stated by a verified fact without a matching rule (for example the
  30-month wait-out in X7) goes in `key_points` and `evidence_fact_ids`, and the case
  records why.

### 2.2 Missing applicant fields

- **`required_missing_fields`:** essential fields that are not stated, without which a
  required or conditional rule cannot be applied. Missing-information recall is computed
  over these.
- **`acceptable_follow_ups`:** questions that are reasonable to ask but not essential. These
  are neither rewarded nor penalised.
- Field names are the registry's field catalogue (`policy_rules.yaml › fields`).
- Fields never asked about are not "missing" (architecture: missing fields are computed only
  for the topics asked).

### 2.3 Expected conversational behaviour (`expected_behaviour`, one or more)

| Behaviour | Expected when | A correct answer… |
|---|---|---|
| `provide_guidance` | Requirements are determinable | gives the preparation steps with sources |
| `ask_follow_up` | `required_missing_fields` is not empty | asks for each field; guidance that depends on it stays conditional |
| `flag_conflict` | `expected_conflicts` is not empty | names the contradiction and asks. If the conflict is `material`, it gives no guidance that relies on either side; if immaterial, it may continue |
| `correct_misconception` | The user asserts something the facts contradict | states the correction with the fact |
| `state_unconfirmed` | The question turns on U-01 to U-04 (D-061) | says the point is not established by the sources, without deciding it either way, and redirects |
| `abstain_and_redirect` | The topic is Excluded or the household is unsupported | declines and gives the official redirect |
| `partial_answer_and_redirect` | The question mixes in-scope and Excluded parts | answers the in-scope part and redirects the rest |

`answerable` is `yes`, `partial` or `no`. Appropriate abstention is scored only on `partial`
or `no` cases that carry `abstain_and_redirect`, `state_unconfirmed` or
`partial_answer_and_redirect`. Over-abstention is scored on `yes` cases.

### 2.4 Prohibited conclusions (`prohibited_conclusions`)

- Each item has an ID, a description, a **severity** and a **basis**.
- **Severity** follows 05 §4.3:
  - *critical* means a materially misleading preparation or eligibility conclusion;
  - *major* means a misleading omission or an unsupported assumption.
- **Basis:** fact IDs, rule IDs, decision IDs, or U/I/G items. Every basis is checked for
  traceability.
- Reused items include `PC-VERDICT`, `PC-NO-HFE`, `PC-VALIDITY`, `PC-GRANT`, `PC-CEILING`,
  `PC-ODDS`, `PC-GUARANTEE`, `PC-DOCLIST`, `PC-UNCONFIRMED`, `PC-CONFLICT` and `PC-ASSUME`.
  Case-specific items are `PC-X1`, `PC-X2`, …

A case has at least one critical error if the answer asserts any critical prohibited
conclusion (critical-error rate).

### 2.5 Evidence support (`evidence_fact_ids`)

- These are the verified facts that establish every required rule and key point. The
  validator rejects unverified or unknown facts.
- Evidence must be **reviewer-accessible**: fact IDs that resolve to official URLs through the
  manifest, never private passages (D-006).
- Citation precision checks that a cited fact *substantively* supports the claim (05 §4.2).
- These IDs are also the gold set for **retrieval recall@k** (05 §5).

### 2.6 Scope metadata
- **`question_topics`:** the closed `Topic` enum.
- **`out_of_scope`:** the code, the topic and the redirect source ID.
- **`expected_conflicts`:** the fields, `stated_contradiction` or `logical_inconsistency`, and
  whether the conflict is `material`.
- **`unresolved_refs`:** the U/I/G items the case touches. **No definitive reference answer is
  given on these points.** The label specifies only the behaviour (§2.3) and prohibits
  answering them definitively.
- **`reference_profile`:** the expected extraction (`None` means not stated, or conflicting).
  It is used to evaluate the profile-extraction stage.

### 2.7 Severity and scoring alignment

| Rubric element | Metric |
|---|---|
| `required_rule_ids` | Required-rule recall; a missed one is a **major** error |
| `required_missing_fields` | Missing-information recall |
| Critical `prohibited_conclusions` | Critical-error rate |
| `expected_behaviour` with abstention-type behaviours | Appropriate abstention, and over-abstention |
| `evidence_fact_ids` | Citation precision; retrieval recall@k |
| Claim-level annotation (§3) | Unsupported-claim rate; verifier metrics |

---

## 3. Claim-level annotation protocol (verifier evaluation; D-065 PROPOSED)

This protocol is separate from the case labels. The verifier evaluation uses a fixed claim
set, built from verified facts, so it does not depend on any model's outputs (D-020).

**Record** (`evaluation/claims/claim_template.jsonl`):
- `claim_id`;
- `split` (dev or eval);
- `text`: one atomic factual claim;
- `evidence_fact_ids`: exactly what the verifier is given;
- `gold_label`: `supported`, `contradicted` or `insufficient_evidence`;
- `construction`;
- `source_fact_id`;
- `rationale`;
- `review`.

**Construction types:**

| Label | Allowed constructions |
|---|---|
| supported | `faithful_paraphrase` of one verified fact (same numbers, applicant group and conditions) |
| contradicted | Single-attribute perturbation: `changed_number`, `changed_period`, `changed_applicant_group`, or **`dropped_exception`** (targets the risk in 05 §10) |
| insufficient_evidence | `out_of_kb` (an Excluded topic or a G-17/U-item) or `beyond_evidence` (adds a condition the facts don't state) |

**Annotation steps:**
1. Pick a verified fact.
2. Write the claim from the fact, not from a model.
3. Give the verifier the cited facts.
4. Assign the gold label from the construction.
5. Record the rationale.
6. Have the developer review it.

**Atomicity rules:**
- one proposition per claim;
- conjunctions are split;
- hedged or procedural statements ("check with HDB") are **not checkable** and are excluded
  from the unsupported-claim denominator.

**Scoring generated answers:** each answer is split into atomic factual claims. Each claim is
labelled `supported` if a cited verified fact substantively supports it, `contradicted` if a
verified fact states otherwise, and `insufficient` otherwise. The runtime verifier's own
judgement is never the reference (REQ-EVL-029).

**Proposed size:** 60 claims, from 05 §6.1:
- dev: 5/5/5 across supported/contradicted/insufficient;
- eval: 15/15/15.

The eval claims are sealed like the held-out labels (D-064). The template holds 4 dev
examples only.

---

## 4. Sampling strategy

- **Stratified by category:** 6 categories × 8 cases (D-019). Dev/held-out is 3/5 per
  category (05 §3.3).
- **Policy-derived templates:** each case starts from one or two rules or facts. One or two
  meaningful factors vary at a time:
  - relationship (married / engaged);
  - citizenship combination;
  - age at a published boundary (20/21, 33/35, 40/41);
  - HFE stage and date (30-day window, 9-month expiry, already submitted);
  - first-timer status;
  - children;
  - property;
  - employment and jobs;
  - non-selection stage.
- **Boundary pairs:** under 21 vs exactly 21 (DEV-07/08); expiry within 30 days vs already
  expired; non-resident spouse SC aged 38 vs 33.
- **Coverage:** 22 of 24 rules are required or conditional in at least one case. R-HH-003
  (married under 21) and R-HH-004 (two SPR partners) are covered only by unit tests: they are
  rare preparation paths and the 48-case limit was kept.
- **Excluded topics sampled:** grant calculation, income ceilings, ballot odds, an unsupported
  household (single), a mixed in-scope/excluded question, and a demand for an eligibility
  verdict.
- **Unresolved items:** U-01, U-02 and U-03 each have a case labelled `state_unconfirmed`.
- **Fictional names only.** Profiles are synthetic and contain no real records.
- **Fixed evaluation date:** `as_of = 2026-11-01`, so date-dependent guidance is
  reproducible.

**Totals:**

| Measure | Count |
|---|---|
| Cases | 48 |
| Families | 34 |
| Prohibited conclusions | 98 (76 critical, 22 major) |
| Essential missing fields | 11 |
| Cases with an unresolved/interpretation reference | 14 |

## 5. Split, leakage control and access to held-out labels (D-063, D-064)

- **Split:** 18 dev / 30 held-out, made **before any prompt or model work**.
- **Group-aware:** each case has a `family_id` for its near-duplicate group. Families are
  assigned to one side only, and `validate` fails if a family spans both.
  - Examples: F-UNDER21 (DEV-07/08 and X8) is dev; F-NONRES (S8, M7, E7, U3) and F-PRIORITY
    (S3, M6, X4, U2) are held-out.
- **Near-duplicate check:** token-set Jaccard similarity between every pair. There are 0
  cross-split pairs at ≥ 0.6 (the maximum cross-split similarity is 0.49). One within-split
  pair is intended: the DEV-07/08 boundary twins.
- **Held-out access protocol (D-064):**
  1. Held-out **labels** live only in `evaluation/heldout/`, which is Git- and
     Docker-ignored. The tracked manifest commits their SHA-256.
  2. `load_test_labels()` refuses unless `final=True`, `BTO_BUDDY_FINAL_EVAL=1`, the manifest
     `status` is `frozen`, and the hash matches. Developer review uses `review=True`.
  3. Prompt tuning, model selection and pipeline debugging use `dev.jsonl` only. Agents may
     load `test_inputs.jsonl` **only** to check schema compatibility, and **must not read**
     `evaluation/heldout/` (CLAUDE.md).
  4. Labels are never changed after held-out predictions are inspected, except to correct
     documented annotation errors. Any such change is disclosed, and that set is no longer
     reported as untouched (REQ-EVL-019, REQ-EVL-022).
  5. At final scoring the developer commits the labels file. Its hash must equal the
     pre-registered value.
- **Disclosure:** the coding agent authored the held-out labels in this session, before any
  prompt work. It will not read them again before final scoring. The developer should keep a
  backup of `evaluation/heldout/` (it is not in Git until then).

## 6. Label quality assurance

**Automated checks** (`python -m evaluation.benchmark validate`; tests in
`tests/test_benchmark.py`):
- every rule ID exists;
- every fact is `verified`;
- fields are in the catalogue;
- missing or conflicting fields are absent from the reference profile;
- every prohibited-conclusion basis is traceable;
- behaviours are consistent with missing fields, conflicts, excluded topics and unresolved
  items;
- split, family and hash integrity.

**Engine cross-check (annotation QA only).** Labels were authored by hand, then compared with
the deterministic rule engine. Disagreements are reviewed against the **source**, never
adopted automatically:
- one label error was corrected: DEV-05 listed the two-SPR rule as conditional, but
  applicant 1 is stated to be an SC (HH-CIT-001);
- the fee-and-ballot rule was added as **optional** to 3 cases.
- **Caveat:** the rule registry is part of configurations C and D. Agreement between labels
  and the engine is therefore **not** evidence that the labels are correct. That comes only
  from source review (§7). Labels that rest on facts without a rule (X7) deliberately expose
  gaps in the registry.

## 7. Labels requiring the developer's manual source verification

- **Every label is `candidate`** until reviewed.
- **20 cases** (dev 4, held-out 16) have `review.requires_source_check = true`, with reasons.
  The reasons are:
  - date arithmetic or conventions (I-02, I-03, the 30-day and 30-month windows);
  - interpretation rules (R-HFE-003/004, R-HH-007, R-PRI-002);
  - human-review exceptions (non-resident spouse under 35);
  - the G-17 gap wording;
  - unresolved U-items, where only a behaviour is labelled;
  - a rule-registry limitation (the 30-month wait-out after a past sale);
  - the materiality of a conflict;
  - whether "flats available to choose from" matches HDB's waiver count.
- **Dev:** open `evaluation/benchmark/dev_review_sheet.csv`.
- **Held-out:** open `evaluation/heldout/test_review_sheet.csv`. Only you review this one.
- For each case, fill in:
  - `REVIEW_decision` (approve / edit / reject);
  - `REVIEW_source_checked`;
  - `REVIEW_notes`.
- **Second reviewer:** none is available, so a separate source-based audit is done and the
  labels are disclosed as **author-validated** (03 §4, REQ-EVL-018).

## 8. Review and freeze procedure
1. The developer reviews both sheets. Edits are applied to the JSONL files, then
   `validate --heldout` is re-run (developer only).
2. Recompute the held-out SHA-256, and set the manifest `status` to `frozen` with a new
   `benchmark_version`.
3. Record the freeze in decisions.md and the development log. **Prompt work starts only
   after this.**
4. Write `evaluation/metric_spec.md`, the frozen metric definitions and denominators, before
   the held-out run (REQ-EVL-026).

## 9. Limitations of synthetic cases
- **Author-built:** the cases reflect the author's reading of the sources, not real
  applicant language or the real distribution of questions. They are a controlled benchmark
  and say nothing about population-level effectiveness (REQ-EVL-031).
- **Small:** 30 held-out cases give wide intervals. Results are reported with raw counts,
  paired comparisons and bootstrap intervals (05 §7).
- **Narrow profiles:** the profile covers only the registry's field catalogue. Real
  situations (divorce, adoption, joint ownership details) are simplified.
- **Single snapshot:** the policy is the 28 Oct 2026 snapshot. Answers that are correct
  against the live site after drift are not credited (G-15).
- **Author validation:** the agent authored both the labels and the rules; disclosed in §5–§7.
- **Unresolved points:** U-items only test behaviour, not policy correctness.
- **Cases are short and English-only,** with explicit facts. Robustness to noisy or
  multilingual input is not measured.

## 10. Carried-over Phase 3 to-dos (from Phase 2b)
1. **Live-page drift check:** the developer spot-checks the live HDB pages for the critical
   facts before submission (G-15, D-058).
2. **Rights clearance:** the developer clears the facts, moving `rights_review` to `cleared`
   (REQ-LIC-015).
3. **README data section:** write it (03 §8), with the D-054 and D-057 disclosures.

content.text:
The candidate benchmark is built: 48 fictional cases, 18 for development and 30 held out. It is **not frozen** and won't be until you approve the labels. All checks pass (92 tests, ruff, mypy, the benchmark validator, the anonymity scan), and the held-out labels are invisible to Git.

**Rubric first, then cases.** The rubric is in [evaluation_benchmark.md](docs/evaluation_benchmark.md) §2 and covers five things:
- **Applicable requirements:** rules that must appear in the answer, rules that depend on missing information, and optional ones that are never penalised.
- **Missing applicant fields:** essential ones versus questions that are merely reasonable to ask.
- **Expected behaviour:** seven types, such as giving guidance, asking a follow-up, flagging a conflict, correcting a misconception, stating something is unconfirmed, and declining with a redirect.
- **Prohibited conclusions:** each marked critical or major and traced to a fact, rule or decision.
- **Evidence:** verified fact IDs only.

The claim-level protocol for testing the verifier (§3) is separate. Claims are built from verified facts and labelled supported, contradicted (one attribute changed, including a dropped exception) or insufficient evidence. A template with 4 development examples is included.

**The cases:**
- **Balance:** 6 categories × 8, split 3 development / 5 held-out per category.
- **Coverage:** 22 of 24 rules are exercised. The married-partner-under-21 and two-SPR-partners rules are covered only by unit tests.
- **Boundaries:** cases sit on the published limits, such as ages 20/21, 33/38 and 40/41, HFE expiry within 30 days versus already expired, and a waiver at 8 remaining flats.
- **Unresolved points:** each case touching U-01, U-02 or U-03 has no definitive reference answer. The label only requires the answer to say the point is unconfirmed, and prohibits deciding it either way.
- **Traceability:** every label cites approved rule IDs and verified facts. Two context facts needed for the out-of-scope redirects were verified first, bringing the total to 53.

**Keeping development and held-out separate:**
- Near-duplicate cases are grouped into 34 families, and each family sits entirely in one split. No case is a near-duplicate of one in the other split (highest similarity 0.49).
- Held-out labels are only in `evaluation/heldout/`, which Git and Docker ignore. The tracked manifest stores their SHA-256, and a tracked file holds the held-out inputs with no labels.
- The loader releases held-out labels only at final scoring: it needs an explicit flag, a frozen manifest and a matching hash.
- CLAUDE.md now forbids agents from reading `evaluation/heldout/`. I deleted the script I wrote the labels with, and this summary avoids describing any held-out case.

**Label checks:** I wrote the labels by hand, then compared them with the rule engine purely as a check:
- **DEV-05:** I'd wrongly listed the two-SPR rule as possibly applying. Applicant 1 is stated to be an SC (HH-CIT-001), so I corrected it.
- **Fee-and-ballot rule:** added as optional to 3 cases.

The rule engine is part of configurations C and D, so agreement with it doesn't prove the labels right. Only your source review does.

**What you need to check:**
- **20 cases** (4 development, 16 held-out) are flagged for checking against the source. The reasons are date conventions, interpretation rules, the missing per-status document lists, unresolved points, how material a conflict is, and the waiver count. The rest still need your sign-off.
- **Review sheets:** `evaluation/benchmark/dev_review_sheet.csv` and `evaluation/heldout/test_review_sheet.csv`. Each has columns for your decision, whether you checked the source, and notes. With no second reviewer, the labels will be disclosed as author-validated.

**Limitations of synthetic cases** (§9):
- the cases reflect my reading of the sources, not real applicant language;
- 30 held-out cases give wide confidence intervals;
- profiles are simplified to the rule registry's fields;
- policy is fixed at the 28 Oct snapshot;
- unresolved points test behaviour only;
- cases are short and English-only.

**Your decisions:**
1. **D-063:** approve the benchmark design: 18/30 split by family, the rubric, and the label rules.
2. **D-064:** approve the held-out access controls.
3. **D-065:** approve the claim protocol and a 60-claim set.
4. Review the labels using the two sheets.
5. Back up `evaluation/heldout/`; it isn't in Git until final scoring.

After approval I'll freeze the benchmark, then write the frozen metric definitions before any prompt work.

The three to-dos from Phase 2b carry into Phase 3 and are listed in INDEX and §10: the live-page drift check, your rights clearance of the facts, and the README data section.

When you're ready to commit, use `docs: design candidate evaluation benchmark (Phase 3a)` over the changed files. Git can't see `evaluation/heldout/`, so it can't be committed by accident.

Critical source: The manually constructed “Source-discovery matrix (not yet scoped to the project's MVP scope)” under Dataset A in the project approach.
This matrix is my preliminary guide to where relevant BTO policy information is located, how different webpages and sections relate, and how content is presented. Treat it as a source-discovery and completeness checklist, not as an instruction to include every listed policy topic.
Objective: Determine the smallest rights-compliant set of official policy sources necessary to support the approved BTO Buddy MVP, and design the acquisition strategy before any extraction begins.
Tasks:
Reconcile the source-discovery matrix against the approved MVP scope. Review every row's contents and substantive linked resource. Classify each as:
Essential to the MVP.
Supporting or supplementary.
Context only.
Outside the MVP.
Pending clarification.
Preserve the original source references and record the reason for each classification. Do not silently omit relevant conditions or exceptions.
Map the source structure and relationships. For each relevant source, record whether the information appears in:
A main webpage section.
A same-page bookmark or anchor.
An expandable or nested accordion.
An HTML table, including nested tables.
A separate HDB information webpage.
An HDB Flat Portal or other restricted path.
A linked PDF or downloadable document.
An infographic or image.
An embedded YouTube video.
An external website.
Preserve parent-page relationships, anchor references, linked URLs and content formats.
Identify policy dependencies and exceptions. Determine which linked sources contain conditions or exceptions essential to understanding a rule. Distinguish necessary supporting evidence from optional background information.
Review access and licensing restrictions. For each source category, document:
Applicable website Terms of Use.
Relevant robots.txt restrictions.
Copyright and redistribution considerations.
Proposed acquisition method.
Whether local computational analysis is supportable.
Whether GitHub redistribution or transmission to an external LLM provider is permitted, restricted or unresolved.
Do not treat robots.txt as a copyright licence. Do not assume that publicly accessible content is freely redistributable. Where permission cannot be established, explicitly mark it unresolved.
Design the source manifest. Propose a schema containing:
Stable source ID.
Original URL and canonical URL.
Page or document title.
Parent source and linked-source relationship.
Section heading and anchor.
Content type and structural format.
Relevant policy area and applicant category.
Known effective date or unresolved temporal status.
Planned acquisition method.
Retrieval timestamp.
SHA-256 content hash after acquisition.
Permission status.
Manual review status.
Review non-text resources.
Identify PDFs containing unique MVP-critical policy information.
Identify infographics relevant to HFE preparation or next steps.
Determine whether infographics are supplementary visuals or contain unique policy facts.
Record YouTube videos as references unless they contain unique essential information.
Do not assume that images or videos may be downloaded or embedded.
Design the corpus strategy. Distinguish:
Local original HTML and permitted source snapshots.
Local processed passages and indexes containing source text.
Independently authored, source-attributed policy facts and rule representations suitable for reviewer access after rights review.
Explain how the reviewer-facing corpus can support the approved MVP without unauthorised redistribution.
Address clean-machine reproducibility. Propose how reviewers can run the application from the README without depending on unavailable private files. Do not claim that downloading live webpages later reproduces an identical historical frozen corpus.
Identify source and policy coverage gaps. Flag missing documents, incomplete policy exceptions, unclear effective dates, potentially inaccessible content and other blockers.
Recommend the final acquisition scope. Propose the minimum source list needed to cover:
First-timer couple household composition.
Broad BTO application requirements.
HFE prerequisites, timing and documentation.
Missing applicant information.
Limited, source-verified first-timer and priority considerations.
Limited, source-verified application and non-selection consequences.
Loans and grants remain context-only. Do not expand into financial calculations, detailed financing or unrelated applicant categories.
Deliverables:
A reconciled source-discovery matrix.
An MVP source coverage matrix.
A source relationship and link classification inventory.
A source manifest schema.
A documented rights and access assessment.
A proposed extraction method for each approved source.
A reviewer-reproducibility strategy.
A list of unresolved risks, exclusions and approval decisions.
Map relevant outputs to the project requirement IDs and record proposed decisions.
Stop condition: Do not download, scrape, extract or modify external source content. Do not expand the MVP until I have reviewed and approved the source list, permissions assessment and acquisition plan.
