522	## 10. Extraction method per approved source
523	
524	> **Superseded in part by Gate R (§7.2a, revised D-055).** HDB returns 403 to automated
525	> clients, so **capture is manual**:
526	> 1. The developer opens each approved page in a normal browser, not logged in.
527	> 2. Clicks every accordion open.
528	> 3. In DevTools runs `copy(document.documentElement.outerHTML)` and saves the result as
529	>    `data/private_corpus/raw/<source_id>/<UTC timestamp>.html`. This takes the live DOM and
530	>    no image bytes. Chrome's "Save as… Complete" or a single-file save would also save the
531	>    infographics, so they are avoided.
532	> 4. Notes the time and how many accordions were opened.
533	>
534	> A local **offline** script (`scripts/register_snapshot.py`) then does the rest. It hashes the
535	> file, writes the manifest entry, counts expanded vs collapsed controls in the saved DOM, and
536	> serialises structure to L1 with Playwright `set_content` (JavaScript off, no network) or the
537	> stdlib parser.
538	>
539	> **Exclusive accordions** (opening one closes another; observed by the developer 2026-10-28):
540	> 1. First run a read-only console check. It counts accordion controls and measures whether
541	>    each collapsed panel's content is already in the DOM. It also checks for the embedded
542	>    page-data JSON (`__NEXT_DATA__`; the site is Next.js on a Sitecore media path).
543	> 2. If every panel is in the DOM, a single `outerHTML` copy is complete.
544	> 3. If panels are unmounted when closed, a console-assisted collector opens each section in
545	>    turn in the developer's own session, at about 1 s per click. It saves each section's
546	>    heading and panel HTML with the full page into one JSON bundle per page.
547	> 4. Recorded as `manual_rendered_dom` with `expansion: console_assisted_sequential`.
548	> 5. Completeness check: the section count in the bundle equals the control count from the
549	>    check, and no panel is empty.
550	>
551	> The automated-capture description below applies only if HDB later permits automated access.
552	
553	All capture runs use `scripts/capture_sources.py` (D-042) with a **tracked allowlist**,
554	`data/capture_allowlist.json`. The allowlist lists approved `source_id` → URL pairs and is
555	derived from the approved manifest. The script refuses any URL that isn't on the allowlist.
556	
557	**Common behaviour** (D-053, D-055):
558	- headless Chromium; one page at a time; a fixed delay between pages (at least 10 s, or the
559	  robots.txt `Crawl-delay` if larger);
560	- an honest user-agent string that identifies a research prototype;
561	- no login and no form submission;
562	- no link-following;
563	- `waitUntil: networkidle`, then expand every accordion control inside the main content area,
564	  recording the controls found and the controls expanded;
565	- save `page.content()` to L0;
566	- compute `raw_sha256`;
567	- serialise structure in-browser with `page.evaluate`: heading path, paragraphs, lists,
568	  tables (rows, cells, nested tables kept as children) and links (href and text). Output goes
569	  to L1 as JSONL, with `text_sha256`;
570	- no screenshots by default;
571	- no HTML-parsing dependency: the browser DOM does the parsing, so D-036/D-042 stay
572	  unchanged.

  [`data/sources_manifest.json`](../data/sources_manifest.json).

- **Chronology:** [development_log.md](development_log.md).

  and against the live site at capture.

**Status:** 7 sources acquired manually and held privately: S01–S05 (HTML) and S07–S08
(PDF). Fact authoring hasn't started.

**Provenance tags:**

## 1. Classification and IDs

| Class | Meaning |

| **Pending** | Depends on an open question |

IDs are stable and never reused:
- `S##` is a document;
- `S##.x` is a section inside a document;

## 6. Rights and access

### 6.1 Checks (2026-10-28)

| Check | Result |

| `www.hdb.gov.sg/robots.txt` | Read via a web-fetch tool; curl got HTTP 403. No rule matches S01–S06 or `/-/media/`. **`Disallow: /hdb-flat-portal`** matches S10. No crawl delay. No raw copy is held |

### 6.2 Consequences

| Use | Position |
|---|---|

## 7. Acquisition method and completeness

**Capture method (D-055):**
1. The developer opens each page in a normal browser, not logged in.
2. Runs a read-only console check of the accordions.
3. Copies `document.documentElement.outerHTML`. This takes the live DOM, not the image files.
   "Save as complete" is avoided because it would also save the infographics.
4. Saves the copy to `data/private_corpus/raw/<source_id>/<UTC>_<name>.html`.

PDFs are downloaded in the browser, never re-saved. Their final URLs come from the
download record. The UTC prefix is the file's creation time; for the PDFs it matches
Chrome's download timestamp to within 2 s.

Accordions open exclusively, but every panel is present in the DOM in the default state
(console check, confirmed by the offline audit). So **one default-state copy per page is
complete**.

**Offline tooling:** stdlib only. Output is structure only, never source text.

Every page-data item missing from the DOM is metadata: page or meta descriptions, and the
descriptions of link cards to other pages. No policy content is unrendered.

S02 was updated on capture day, and its HFE infographic file is dated 27 Oct 2026. Facts come
from these snapshots, never from the matrix's earlier paraphrases.

---

## 8. Corpus design

### 8.1 Layers

| Layer | Content | Path | Git |
|---|---|---|---|
| L0 raw | HTML and PDF snapshots; rights-check evidence | `data/private_corpus/raw/` | Ignored |
| L1 processed | Structured passages (heading path, text, tables, links) and any local index | `data/private_corpus/processed/` | Ignored |
| L2 authored KB | `policy_facts.jsonl` (paraphrased, fact IDs, source pointers, **no quotes**); `policy_rules.yaml` | `data/` | Tracked after rights review |
| L3 metadata | `sources_manifest.json`, `source_coverage.csv`, `visual_resources.json` | `data/` | Tracked |

The app, BM25 index, Docker image and evaluation use **only L2 and L3** (D-005,
REQ-DAT-011/012). Each claim cites a fact ID. The fact resolves to an official URL and section
through the manifest (D-006), so reviewers check it against HDB's live page, not a copy.

### 8.2 Rights review before a fact is tracked (D-054)

1. **Write independently worded statements**, one condition each. Only proper names, numbers,
   dates and durations are kept as-is.
2. **Run a local overlap check:** flag any 8+ consecutive words shared with L1, and reword.
3. **Read it manually,** then set `rights_review: cleared`.
4. **Run the anonymity and secret scans** before suggesting a commit.

The developer drafts facts from L1, and the coding agent works only on the drafts (D-054
option (a), recommended).

### 8.3 Manifest schema (D-053, PROPOSED)

Top level: `manifest_version`, `rights_records[]`, `sources[]`.

| `rights_records[]` fields | `sources[]` fields |
|---|---|
| `rights_id`, `host`, `terms_url`, `terms_checked_at`, `terms_sha256`, `terms_summary` (authored), `robots_url`, `robots_checked_at`, `robots_sha256`, `robots_relevant_rules`, `robots_permits_planned_paths`, `legal_basis`, `redistribution`, `llm_transmission`, `notes` | `source_id`, `record_kind`, `title`, `original_url`, `canonical_url`, `host`, `parent_source_id`, `link_relation`, `content_format`, `matrix_refs`, `policy_areas` (architecture §5 `Topic`), `mvp_class`, `mvp_class_reason`, `page_last_updated`, `effective_date`, `effective_date_status` (`stated` / `page_last_updated_only` / `pdf_metadata_date_only` / `unknown`), `acquisition` {`method`, `requested_url`, `final_url`, `retrieved_at`, `retrieved_at_basis`, `raw_sha256`, `text_sha256`, `byte_size`, `private_path`}, `rights_id`, `permission_status`, `review` |

- **`text_sha256`** hashes the normalised page text. A future re-capture can then tell real
  content change apart from page noise.
- **Section-level records** (`S01.a`, …) and **extraction counts** are added when L1 is
  built.
- **`data/source_coverage.csv` columns:** `area_tier, sub_area, rule_or_fact_ids,
  essential_source_ids, supporting_source_ids, exceptions_required, exceptions_verified,
  coverage_status, evidence_gap_kind, notes`.

---

| Run the app (Docker or `uv`) | Tracked L2/L3; an LLM key for live answers | L0/L1, network access to HDB |
| Re-score the evaluation | Saved predictions and labels | API key |
| Check a cited fact | The fact's URL and section in a browser | L0 |

**Not claimed:**
- Re-capturing pages later does **not** reproduce this corpus. HDB pages change without

  the recorded hashes (REQ-LIC-016).
- The README states the policy period as "HDB sources retrieved 28 Oct 2026" (D-021). It

+    drift from page noise without storing text (REQ-LIC-016). Only metadata is written.
+    manifest = json.loads(MANIFEST.read_text())
+    by_id = {s["source_id"]: s for s in manifest["sources"]}
+    for folder in sorted(p for p in RAW.glob("S*") if p.is_dir()):
+        files = sorted(f for f in folder.iterdir() if STAMP.match(f.name))
+        if not files or folder.name not in by_id:
+            print(f"skip {folder.name}: no stamped file or no manifest entry")
+            continue
+        f = files[-1]
+        data = f.read_bytes()
+        stamp = STAMP.match(f.name).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]
+        retrieved = datetime.strptime(stamp, "%Y-%m-%dT%H%M%SZ").replace(tzinfo=UTC)
+        text_sha = None
+        if f.suffix == ".html":
+            snap = Snapshot()
+            snap.feed(data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
+            text_sha = hashlib.sha256(norm(" ".join(snap.text)).encode()).hexdigest()
+        acq = by_id[folder.name]["acquisition"]
+        acq.update(
+                "retrieved_at": retrieved.isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z"),
+                "retrieved_at_basis": "file creation time at save (UTC filename prefix)",
+                "raw_sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),
+                "text_sha256": text_sha,
+                "byte_size": len(data),
+                "private_path": str(f.relative_to(ROOT)),
+        print(f"{folder.name}: {acq['retrieved_at']} sha256={acq['raw_sha256'][:12]} ({f.name})")
+    MANIFEST.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
+def main() -> None:
+    command = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else ""
+    if command == "audit":
+        run_audit()
+    elif command == "register":
+        run_register()
+    else:
+        sys.exit("usage: python -I scripts/snapshots.py {audit|register}")
if __name__ == "__main__":
main()

content.text:
The repo is cleaned up, and it now holds only files that are needed or are submission evidence. Ruff, mypy, pytest and the lockfile check all pass, there are no broken doc links, and the anonymity scan is clean.

## What changed
| Item | Action | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/source_acquisition_plan.md` (800 lines) | **Replaced** by [docs/data_sources.md](docs/data_sources.md) (about 350 lines) | The old file was a pre-capture plan, with speculation, superseded automated-capture steps and a copy of the decision list. The new doc describes the current state of the sources only. |
| `scripts/audit_snapshots.py` + `register_snapshots.py` | **Merged** into [scripts/snapshots.py](scripts/snapshots.py) with `audit` and `register` commands | One tool instead of two. It regenerates the manifest byte-for-byte identically, so the recorded hashes stay reproducible. |
| `.DS_Store`, `src/bto_buddy.egg-info`, tool caches, `__pycache__` | **Deleted** | Local leftovers, all git-ignored and regenerated automatically. |
| References in CLAUDE.md, INDEX, 02, 03, decisions and the development log | **Repointed** | No links to the deleted files remain. The development log keeps the history and adds a cleanup entry. |

## What I kept, and why
- **`data_sources.md` as its own doc.** The submission plan explicitly allows separate files for policy-source manifests (REQ-DOC-012). Merging it into decisions.md or the development log would mix reference material with decisions and history, and would bloat both files.
- **`data/sources_manifest.json`.** It's the required provenance record (REQ-SRC-002).
- **`scripts/snapshots.py`.** Without it, the hashes in the manifest couldn't be re-checked.
- **`docs/project_context/` 01–06 and `architecture.md`.** They're the approved requirements and design that every decision cites. Merging them now would break traceability for little gain.
- **`README.md`.** It's still a placeholder, and it becomes the main deliverable later.

Private captures, the rights-check evidence, `references/private/` and `.venv` are all git-ignored. I didn't touch any of them.

## Needs your approval: D-056
The Playwright `capture` dependency group is now unused, because HDB blocks automated access and capture is manual. I've proposed removing it from `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`, and removing the planned `capture_sources.py` from the architecture doc. I haven't done it, because it reverses your approved decision D-042. Tell me if I should go ahead.

This is a good point to commit:
- **Files:** `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/`, `data/sources_manifest.json` and `scripts/snapshots.py`. Nothing private is included.
- **Suggested message:** `data: add source manifest, data-sources doc and snapshot tooling`.
- **Push:** fine to the private remote after the secret scan.

given my latest data capture approach, is playwright still necessary for any subsequent/current steps? if it is not, then proceed with removing the dependency and update all relevant docs with the latest data acquisition approach and alignment to data provenance and licensing regulations

For current and future steps, Playwright isn't needed:

| Step | Needs Playwright? |
|---|---|
| Capture | No. It's manual in your browser, because HDB blocks automated clients |
| Audit and manifest | No. `snapshots.py` uses only the standard library |
| Building structured passages (next step) | No. The standard library HTML parser already reads the saved pages, and every accordion panel is in the saved DOM |
| PDFs | No. Checked by hand under D-052 |
| Drift check before submission | No. It's a manual re-capture plus `snapshots.py register` |
| App, Docker, evaluation | No. It was never part of them |

So I'll go ahead with D-056. First, every place that mentions it:

**Why it isn't needed:**
- **Capture** is manual in your browser, because HDB blocks automated clients.
- **The audit, the manifest register and the next step** (turning saved pages into structured passages) all read the saved files with Python's standard library.
- **The two PDFs** are checked by hand.
- **The drift check before submission** is a manual re-capture followed by `snapshots.py register`.
- **The app, Docker and evaluation** never used it.

**Dependency removal:**
- Ran `uv remove --group capture playwright` and removed the leftover empty `capture` group from `pyproject.toml`.
- `uv.lock` went from 54 to 51 packages; Playwright's two supporting packages went with it.

**Docs updated to the manual capture approach:**
- **[decisions.md](docs/decisions.md):** D-056 is approved and done, and D-042 is marked superseded. D-052 no longer refers to a capture group that doesn't exist, and D-053 drops the capture allowlist.
- **[architecture.md](docs/architecture.md):** the dependency table marks Playwright as removed. The scripts listing now shows `snapshots.py` instead of the planned capture script.

  - approved pages only (REQ-SRC-006);
  - robots.txt (REQ-LIC-014);
  - each Copyright Act s 244 condition: lawful access with no bypassing of the bot protection, analysis-only use, no copies supplied to others (private corpus is git-ignored, out of Docker and never sent to an LLM), and a non-infringing source;

where should i store hdb terms of use contents (in https://www.hdb.gov.sg/terms-of-use) or make it lawfully accessible in this project to verify data, licensing and privacy against?

**Store the full copy privately, and track only a paraphrased summary plus its hash.** The Terms of Use page is itself HDB's copyrighted content, so it follows the same rules as the policy pages.

| What | Where | Committed? |
|---|---|---|
| Full copy of the page, captured the same way as before (DevTools → `copy(document.documentElement.outerHTML)`) | `data/private_corpus/raw/rights/<UTC>_hdb_terms_of_use.html` | **No.** Git-ignored, alongside the two 403 block pages already there |
| URL, check time, SHA-256 of the copy, the page's "last updated" date | the `R-HDB-WWW` record in `data/sources_manifest.json` (`terms_url`, `terms_checked_at`, `terms_sha256`) | Yes |
| Your own paraphrase of the clauses that matter, with very short quotes only where the exact wording decides the point | `terms_summary` in the manifest, and the Terms of Use row in [data_sources.md §6.1](docs/data_sources.md) | Yes |
| What the terms mean for this project (local copies, redistribution, LLM use) | [data_sources.md §6.2–6.3](docs/data_sources.md); a decision entry if they change anything | Yes |

**How this keeps it verifiable without redistributing it:**
- Reviewers get the official URL, the date you read it and the hash. They can read the live page themselves, and the hash proves which version your assessment relied on.
- That's the same approach used for the policy pages. Committing the full text would be redistribution, which s 244(2)(c) doesn't cover.

**Clauses to look for when you read it:**
- copyright or IP ownership, and what reuse is allowed (personal, non-commercial, with attribution);
- any ban on automated access, scraping, crawling, data mining or "robots";
- whether reproduction, modification or redistribution is allowed;
- linking terms (the app links to HDB pages);
- disclaimers about accuracy and currency (useful for the README's "not official advice" wording);
- any terms on AI or machine-learning use;
- the "last updated" date.

**The legal significance.** If the terms restrict copying or analysis, s 187 makes those terms void as far as they would block the computational analysis exception. But a breach of the terms could still undermine lawful access under s 244(2)(d), and in practice that depends mainly on how the pages were accessed. Manual browser access with no bypassing of the bot protection is the strongest position. If the terms forbid automated access, that matches the approach you already took.

**Privacy:** HDB's privacy statement covers how HDB handles its own visitors' data. It doesn't govern this project. The project's privacy position rests on using only fictional profiles (REQ-PRIV-001) and on the deployment limitation already recorded, so the privacy statement doesn't need to be stored.

**Who writes the summary.** Reading the terms was part of the rights check you approved, so once you've saved the copy I can read it and draft the paraphrase for you to confirm. If you'd rather no HDB text reached my model provider, read it yourself and give me the key points, and I'll write them up. message.content: This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation. Summary: 1. **Primary Request and Intent** The project is BTO Buddy, an evidence-grounded assistant that helps fictional first-timer couples prepare for HDB BTO applications. Requests across this session, in order: - **Phase 2b (4B brief).** Offline processing of the approved manual snapshots, covering: - extraction that preserves hierarchy, tables, links and conditions; - completeness validation and a policy coverage matrix; - rights-reviewed `data/policy_facts.jsonl` and `data/visual_resources.json`; - freeze, deterministic tests and documentation; - a scope recommendation, then stop at the approval checkpoint. - **D-054 / Q-26:** the user turned off "Help improve Claude" and allowed the agent to read raw and processed text "AS LONG AS my project still complies with data provenance regulations". - **Scope follow-up:** - keep the recommended scope, with unconfirmed details kept unconfirmed; - approve D-048, with S10 link-only unless its titles show per-status document lists; - D-052: "quickest approach that is compliant"; - S01 and S05 confirmed unedited; - remove the HFE FAQs (S10) from the sources because robots.txt disallows them, and document this honestly; - handle U-01 to U-03 and document what is out of scope and where the evidence gaps are. - **Critical-fact verification:** verify the 47 critical facts via checklist C-01 to C-16 using a policy rule registry: - each rule has an ID, applicability, exceptions, effective scope, required fields, an action and source references; - established facts are kept separate from interpretations; - no undocumented eligibility conditions, and no eligibility decisions; - deterministic validation and boundary tests; - rules cite only verified fact IDs and official metadata. - **Approvals and commits:** approve D-058, D-059 and D-062 with documentation and justification, then suggest commit commands (possibly split). - **Latest request (Phase 3 benchmark design):** - Carry the 3 to-dos into Phase 3: live-page drift check, rights clearance, and the README data section with the D-054/D-057 disclosures. - Design a policy-derived benchmark of 36–48 fictional cases across standard, missing information, policy exceptions, misconceptions, conflicting profiles and out-of-scope requests. - Each case specifies the input profile, user question, expected rule IDs, required missing fields, prohibited conclusions, evidence references and expected behaviour. - Explain the sampling strategy and the limitations of synthetic cases. - Reserve a held-out split before any optimisation, keep held-out labels inaccessible, and prefer a label-free test-input file. - Write the annotation rubric before the cases, plus a separate claim-level protocol. - Prevent near-duplicate leakage, keep every label traceable, mark labels needing manual validation, provide a reviewable annotation template, and **do not freeze until the user approves the labels**. **Standing constraints (verbatim and paraphrased; still in effect):** - "Don't scrape, download or fetch external content (including HDB pages) without approval for that specific action." - "Don't read files in `data/private_corpus/` unless authorised." D-054 as revised lets the agent read in-scope sections for processing and authoring. Source text never goes into tracked files, reports or commit messages. - The developer runs every commit and push. Never run `git commit`, `git push`, merge, rebase or history rewrites. Suggest commits and wait for approval before staging. - Git-ignored and never committed: `references/private/`, `data/private_corpus/`, `.env*`, credentials, and now `evaluation/heldout/`. - Anonymity: tracked files must never name the assessing organisation, the role or the collaborator handle. Never copy `references/private/anonymity_terms.txt` into tracked files. - Never bypass HDB bot protection. - Run the secret and anonymity scans before any suggested push. - **New (D-064, in CLAUDE.md):** never open, read, grep or print anything under `evaluation/heldout/`. Use `dev.jsonl` for development, load `test_inputs.jsonl` only to check schema compatibility, and release labels only via `load_test_labels(final=True)` at final scoring. - Do not modify held-out labels based on model predictions, and do not use model-generated labels as ground truth. 2. **Key Technical Concepts** - **Corpus layers:** L0 raw and L1 processed (private); L2 facts and rules, and L3 metadata (tracked). - **Extraction:** stdlib `html.parser` tree builder (no BeautifulSoup, D-036). The content root is the `DestinationLayout_DestinationPageLayout__Cont` div; chrome classes are excluded. - **Section IDs:** accordion items are `Sxx.a…`, headings outside accordions are `Sxx.hN`, sub-headings are `Sxx.a.N`. There is one passage per section (`…p1`), and the URL uses the nearest ancestor `?anchor=`. - **Completeness checks:** raw-HTML toggle and table counts, `__NEXT_DATA__` sentence coverage (0 rendered-content gaps), heading classification, and links resolved or classified. - **Overlap check:** flags 8+ shared consecutive words; the maximum found was 7. - **D-058 verified:** a number and term-anchor check (≤6 words) on the cited section plus agent reading. It is not a live-page check. 53 facts are verified (47 critical plus PRI-FTPMC-002, DOC-MULTIJOB-001/002, HH-OTHER-001, CTX-HFE-001, CTX-GRANT-001). - **`usable()`:** a critical fact must be verified; a non-critical fact needs at least `snapshot_checked`; rights must be at least `overlap_checked`. - **Rule registry:** - D-038 operators only (eq, ne, lt, gte, in, is_null, all, any) and three-valued logic: a missing field gives `cannot_determine`, and an unknown exception also gives `cannot_determine`. - Each rule has a kind (preparation, caution, evidence_gap), a basis (source_established or interpretation), and interpretation rules always need human review. - Derived field `hfe_days_to_expiry`: issue date + 9 calendar months, clamped to month end (I-02). - **Profile changes (D-062):** `employment` takes the six S07 statuses, and a `job_count` field is added. - **Benchmark:** - 48 cases, 6 categories × 8; 18 dev / 30 held-out (3/5 per category); group-aware families (34). - Cross-split near-duplicates use a Jaccard threshold of 0.6; none found, maximum 0.49. - Held-out labels are sealed with a SHA-256 commitment; the manifest status is "candidate". - `as_of` is 2026-11-01. - **Decision status:** D-044 to D-062 are approved. D-063 to D-065 are PROPOSED. 3. **Files and Code Sections** - **`scripts/corpus.py`** (stdlib; ~1450 lines after ruff format) - Commands: `extract | validate | facts | verify | freeze`, imported from `snapshots.py` (MANIFEST, RAW, ROOT, STAMP, Snapshot, json_strings, norm, short, strip_html). - Key functions: - parsing and extraction: `parse`, `Walker` (accordion, list_items with `without`/`outermost`, table with spans/nested, media blocks), `build_record`, `nearest_anchor`; - validation: `validate_source`, `canon`, `html_segments`, `chrome_text`, `resolve_link`; - facts: `check_facts`, `longest_shared_run`, `words`; - verification: `verify_fact` and `run_verify`, which set `validation.status="verified"` and refresh `max_shared_run_words`; - freeze: `run_freeze` writes `corpus_version.json`, including the rules_version and the hashes of the facts, visuals, coverage, manifest, expected_sections, rules, review, verification and reports. - `NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?` were missed; they are now media blocks; - list nesting was buggy; rewritten with `outermost`/`without`. - **Lint and type errors:** ruff (E501, RUF001 curly quote replaced with `\u2019`, RUF100, SIM) and mypy (untyped lambda dict replaced with if/elif). - **Edit assertion failures** after ruff reformatted files: re-located the text and re-edited. - **Number regex** matched "S01", "S05" and "D-013": fixed with the lookbehind `(?/.claude/projects//b764a348-0454-427c-92e3-8af4cd9828e5.jsonl Continue the conversation from where it left off without asking the user any further questions. Resume directly — do not acknowledge the summary, do not recap what was happening, do not preface with "I'll continue" or similar. Pick up the last task as if the break never happened. The messages after this summary are the most recent messages from before compaction, kept verbatim. The summary was written without seeing them, so something it says has not happened yet may already have happened in them.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

# BTO Buddy — Project Instructions

## Objective
Build an evidence-grounded BTO pre-application preparation assistant for **fictional
first-timer couple profiles**. It gives preparation guidance, **not** official eligibility
determinations. It is a public-sector AI prototype: a hybrid of structured profiling,
deterministic rules, BM25 retrieval and claim-level verification, evaluated against direct-LLM
and RAG baselines.

## Source of truth
- Read `docs/project_context/INDEX.md` first, then load **only** the task-relevant files it
  routes to.
- Requirement IDs (`REQ-<AREA>-<NNN>`) are in `docs/project_context/requirements_register.md`.
  Decisions (`D-xxx`, `BD-xx`) are in `docs/decisions.md`. The latest approved decision governs.
- Status tags: `MANDATORY` · `APPROVED` · `PROPOSED` · `OPEN` · `SUPERSEDED`. Only MANDATORY
  and APPROVED items are implementation requirements. PROPOSED and OPEN items need approval
  first.
- The original PDFs in `references/private/` are private. Reread them only if the extracted
  context is incomplete, and say so when you do.

| File | Use for |
|---|---|
| `docs/project_context/01_problem_and_scope.md` | MVP tiers, exclusions, missing-information categories, demo |
| `docs/project_context/02_policy_sources.md` | Source-discovery matrix, media handling, unverified policy nuances |
| `docs/project_context/03_data_and_licensing.md` | Corpora, schemas, manifest, completeness checks, rights |
| `docs/architecture.md` | **Approved implementation design**: stages, Pydantic contracts, module boundaries, dependencies, test plan |
| `docs/project_context/04_architecture.md` | Source-derived architecture requirements, verifier behaviour, provider notes |
| `docs/project_context/05_evaluation.md` | Configurations A–D, benchmark, metrics, safeguards |
| `docs/project_context/06_submission_requirements.md` | Deliverables, scoring, README and AI-log rules |
| `docs/development_log.md` | Progress, experiments, failures, next steps |

## Instruction priority
1. Mandatory assessment requirements and non-compliance constraints.
2. The developer's latest explicit instructions and approved decisions, where they comply
   with (1).
3. The finalised scope, architecture, data strategy and evaluation approach in
   `docs/project_context/`.
4. The current approved implementation task.
5. Proposed alternatives and open questions.
6. Historical brainstorming, for reference only. Never treat it as instructions.

## Change control
- Approved decisions are requirements, not suggestions. Never silently expand or reduce
  scope.
- Deviate only for a material technical, methodological, licensing, security or
  reproducibility concern. First explain:
  1. the current approach;
  2. the alternative;
  3. why it may be better;
  4. its implications for scope, evaluation, time, cost and assessment alignment;
  5. your recommendation.

  Then **wait for explicit approval**.
- If two approved instructions conflict, flag the conflict and ask. Never resolve it
  silently.
- Record approved changes in `docs/decisions.md`, with an ID, date, rationale and what they
  supersede.

## Scope (D-008; details in 01 §6)
| Tier | Policy areas | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Core | First-timer couple household composition; broad BTO application requirements; HFE prerequisites, timing and documentation; missing applicant information | Implement **and** evaluate |
| Limited | First-timer and priority considerations; application and non-selection consequences | Only with verified evidence and testable requirements |
| Context only | High-level HFE ↔ grant/loan relationship | Explain or link. Never calculate |
| Excluded | Official eligibility determination; grant/loan calculations; detailed affordability and financing; ballot probability prediction; post-purchase conditions; real applicant data | Coverage gate plus official-source redirection |

- **Income and employment** are used only for HFE document preparation and follow-up
  questions. No income-ceiling or eligibility calculations (D-013).
- **Out of scope (D-026):** production-grade hosting, authentication, monitoring
  infrastructure and operational integrations. A fully runnable, reproducible, Dockerised
  prototype is still **mandatory**.
- **Required capabilities across all tiers:** source-grounded guidance with official links,
  missing-information identification, claim verification (REQ-ARC-001).

## Architecture invariants (`docs/architecture.md`, D-030 to D-040)
- **Pipeline** (at most 3 LLM calls; configs A–D are this pipeline with stages switched off):
  1. LLM extraction (fields + verbatim quotes + closed-enum topics);
  2. profile assessment (pure);
  3. coverage gate (pure);
  4. rules ∥ BM25 (pure);
  5. evidence assembly (pure);
  6. LLM generation;
  7. verification;
  8. report (pure).
- Typed Pydantic contracts between every stage. No free text passes between modules. Pure
  modules never import the LLM client.
- **All configurations return the same `FinalGuidance` contract** (D-035).
- Extracted fields without a verbatim input quote are dropped (D-032). Missing fields are
  computed only for the topics asked about.
- Household types other than a first-timer couple are out of scope (D-033).
- Rules are declarative YAML with whitelisted operators. **Never `eval`** (D-038).
- Verification runs deterministic checks first, then one batched LLM judge (D-034).
- Every response carries `missing_profile_fields`, `evidence_gaps`, `profile_conflicts` and
  `out_of_scope_reasons`.
- Never assume missing applicant values. Missing evidence never proves a requirement absent.
- The runtime KB is `data/policy_facts.jsonl` (independently authored, fact IDs). Rules in
  `data/policy_rules.yaml` cite fact IDs. Nothing at runtime reads `data/private_corpus/`.
- **Verifier outcomes:**
  - supported → show with a source;
  - contradicted → withhold and flag;
  - insufficient → no definitive guidance, state the gap.

  Never silently rewrite. No regeneration loop unless approved.
- No autonomous agents, orchestration frameworks or vector DBs. Use one generation model.
- Retrieval is BM25 + aliases + topic filter + rule-linked facts. Propose anything else only
  if dev recall@5 < 0.90 because of paraphrase (D-031).
- **Dependencies are limited to D-036.** The Playwright capture group (D-042) was removed by
  D-056, and `scripts/` is stdlib-only. Anything else needs an approved decision.
- Infographics and videos are links in `data/visual_resources.json`, never runtime evidence.

## Engineering rules
- Simple, typed, testable Python modules in `src/bto_buddy/`. Prefer functions and
  composition over class hierarchies.
- Keep deterministic rules separate from LLM reasoning. Hard rules are deterministic;
  interpretations stay evidence-linked.
- Add short comments wherever the *rationale* isn't obvious. The developer must be able to
  defend every choice (REQ-NFR-003).
- **Every new dependency needs a one-line justification** in `pyproject.toml` or the commit.
- Justify model choices on operational grounds (privacy, latency, task fit, cost at scale),
  never on "free" or "convenient".
- Never invent policy facts, citations, statistics or results. Unverified facts are labelled
  as such.
- Never edit held-out labels to improve scores. Annotation-error fixes are documented and
  disclosed.
- Must work within free tiers. Must run from the README on a clean machine.

## Data, privacy and sources
- **Don't scrape, download or fetch external content** (including HDB pages) without
  approval for that specific action.
- Don't read files in `data/private_corpus/` unless authorised (D-054 as revised: the agent
  may read in-scope sections for processing and fact authoring; source text never goes into
  tracked files, reports or commit messages). Don't send source text, private material or
  credentials to other external services without approval.
- Git-ignored, never committed: `references/private/`, `data/private_corpus/`, `.env*`,
  credentials.
- Tracked docs and data contain authored summaries only, never substantial HDB or
  assessment-brief text.
- **Anonymity:** tracked files must never name the assessing organisation, the role or the
  collaborator handle. Those live only in `references/private/submission_private_notes.md`.
- Keep provenance on every fact: source URL, section, retrieval date, effective date where
  known.

## Evaluation (05)
- **Held-out labels are sealed (D-064):** never open, read, grep or print anything under
  `evaluation/heldout/`. Use `evaluation/benchmark/dev.jsonl` for all development. Load
  `test_inputs.jsonl` only to check schema compatibility. Labels are released only by
  `evaluation.benchmark.load_test_labels(final=True)` at final scoring.
- Same model, instructions, cases, labels and policy version across A–D. C vs D reuses
  identical pre-verification outputs.
- Labels are policy-derived and independently checked. The runtime verifier is never ground
  truth.
- Dev and held-out are separated **before** prompt work. The held-out set is frozen.
  Near-duplicates stay on the same side.
- Metric definitions and denominators are frozen before the held-out run. Report raw counts,
  per-category results and paired comparisons.
- Record model IDs, prompt versions, inference settings, KB version and saved predictions for
  every run.
- Report failures and limitations honestly. This is a controlled benchmark, not
  population-level evidence.

## Working protocol
**Before a major change:**
- cite the relevant requirement IDs;
- state assumptions and trade-offs;
- list the affected files and tests;
- get approval for material design changes.

**After a change:**
- run the relevant checks;
- report the actual output;
- map the work to requirement IDs;
- note limitations and open issues.

**At the end of each phase or session:** update `docs/development_log.md` with completed work,
decisions, failures and next steps.

**Token use:** load only task-relevant context. Keep durable knowledge in the docs, not in
chat. Never drop relevant context just to save tokens.

## Git workflow (D-027)
- **The developer runs every commit and push.** Never run `git commit`, `git push`, merge,
  rebase or any history rewrite. Read-only Git commands (`status`, `diff`, `log`, `grep`) and
  `git add` are fine.
- When a coherent, stable milestone is done and its checks pass, **suggest that it's a good
  point to commit**. Include:
  - which files belong in the commit, and anything that should be left out;
  - the check results that make the milestone stable;
  - a suggested conventional-commit message (`feat:`, `data:`, `eval:`, `build:`, `docs:`,
    `chore:`);
  - whether a push to the private remote is advisable.

  Wait for the developer to approve before staging anything.
- **Before any suggested commit:** confirm nothing from `references/private/` or
  `data/private_corpus/`, and no `.env` or credentials, is part of the change.
- **Before any suggested push:** run the secret and anonymity scans below and report the
  results.

## Commands
Environment and dependencies are managed with **uv**. Exact versions are pinned in `uv.lock`,
which must be committed (D-028). Verified on macOS with uv 0.13.6 and Python 3.13.2 (project
requires ≥3.12):

- Install: `uv sync` (creates `.venv` from `uv.lock`: package + dev group)
- Test: `uv run pytest`
- Lint: `uv run ruff check .`
- Format check: `uv run ruff format --check .`
- Type check: `uv run mypy` (strict, `src/bto_buddy`)
- Lockfile check: `uv lock --check`
- Run locally: `uv run streamlit run src/bto_buddy/app.py` → http://localhost:8501
- Build image: `docker build -t bto-buddy .`
- Run container: `cp .env.example .env` (once; fill in values when an LLM is configured), then
  `docker run --rm -p 8501:8501 --env-file .env bto-buddy`
- Health check: `curl -f http://localhost:8501/_stcore/health`

**Docker image:** two-stage build on `python:3.12-slim`, uv 0.13.6, runs as non-root `app`,
port 8501, HEALTHCHECK on `/_stcore/health`. Configuration comes from environment variables
only. `.dockerignore` keeps `references/`, `data/private_corpus/`, `.env*`, docs, tests and
caches out of the build context.

- Add a dependency with `uv add <pkg>` (or `uv add --dev <pkg>`), with a justification comment
  in `pyproject.toml`. Never hand-edit `uv.lock`.
- **Source capture is manual** (D-055; procedure in `docs/data_sources.md` §7). HDB returns
  403 to automated clients, and that block must never be bypassed (lawful access, Copyright
  Act s 244(2)(d)).
  - Only approved pages are captured, by the developer in a normal browser.
  - Rendered DOM via `copy(document.documentElement.outerHTML)`; PDFs downloaded as-is.
  - Saved to `data/private_corpus/raw/<source_id>/<UTC>_<name>`, which is Git-ignored and
    never sent to an LLM (D-054).
- Snapshot audit (offline, prints structure only, never source text):
  `python3 -I scripts/snapshots.py audit`
- Record hashes and timestamps in the manifest: `python3 -I scripts/snapshots.py register`
- Corpus processing (offline, D-059; tracked outputs hold counts and IDs, never source text):
  `python3 -I scripts/corpus.py extract`, then `validate`, `facts` (integrity and 8-word
  overlap check), `verify` (checklist re-verification, D-058) and `freeze`
- Load the KB without the private corpus: `uv run python -c "from bto_buddy.policy import load_kb; print(load_kb().kb_version)"`
- Benchmark validation (dev + held-out inputs; prints IDs and counts only):
  `uv run python -m evaluation.benchmark validate`. The `--heldout` flag is for the
  developer's label review only.
- Evaluation run commands: add them here only after they have been verified.

**Secret scan before a push** (until a dedicated tool is approved):
```bash
git diff --cached --name-only | grep -E '^(references/private|data/private_corpus)/|(^|/)\.env(\.[^/]*)?$' | grep -v '\.env\.example$' && echo "BLOCK"
git diff --cached | grep -inE 'api[_-]?key|secret|token|password|BEGIN .*PRIVATE KEY' || echo "no secret patterns"
# Anonymity: the term list is private (Git-ignored) and must never be copied into tracked files.
git grep -inFf references/private/anonymity_terms.txt || echo "no identifying terms"
```
- [Completion deadline](completion-deadline.md) — finish by 2026-10-29 07:00; the 12–16h estimate is reference only; plan all of A–D

- **Verifier outcomes:**
  - supported → show with a source;
  - contradicted → withhold and flag;
  - insufficient → no definitive guidance, state the gap.

  Never silently rewrite. No regeneration loop unless approved.
- No autonomous agents, orchestration frameworks or vector DBs. Use one generation model.
- Retrieval is BM25 + aliases + topic filter + rule-linked facts. Propose anything else only
  if dev recall@5 < 0.90 because of paraphrase (D-031).
- **Dependencies are limited to D-036.** The Playwright capture group (D-042) was removed by
  D-056, and `scripts/` is stdlib-only. Anything else needs an approved decision.
- Infographics and videos are links in `data/visual_resources.json`, never runtime evidence.

## Engineering rules
- Simple, typed, testable Python modules in `src/bto_buddy/`. Prefer functions and
  composition over class hierarchies.
- Keep deterministic rules separate from LLM reasoning. Hard rules are deterministic;
  interpretations stay evidence-linked.
- Add short comments wherever the *rationale* isn't obvious. The developer must be able to
  defend every choice (REQ-NFR-003).
- **Every new dependency needs a one-line justification** in `pyproject.toml` or the commit.
- Justify model choices on operational grounds (privacy, latency, task fit, cost at scale),
  never on "free" or "convenient".
- Never invent policy facts, citations, statistics or results. Unverified facts are labelled
  as such.
- Never edit held-out labels to improve scores. Annotation-error fixes are documented and
  disclosed.
- Must work within free tiers. Must run from the README on a clean machine.

- **Don't scrape, download or fetch external content** (including HDB pages) without
  approval for that specific action.
- Don't read files in `data/private_corpus/` unless authorised (D-054 as revised: the agent
  may read in-scope sections for processing and fact authoring; source text never goes into
  tracked files, reports or commit messages). Don't send source text, private material or
  credentials to other external services without approval.
- Git-ignored, never committed: `references/private/`, `data/private_corpus/`, `.env*`,
  credentials.
- Tracked docs and data contain authored summaries only, never substantial HDB or
  assessment-brief text.
- **Anonymity:** tracked files must never name the assessing organisation, the role or the
  collaborator handle. Those live only in `references/private/submission_private_notes.md`.
- Keep provenance on every fact: source URL, section, retrieval date, effective date where
  known.

## Evaluation (05)
- **Held-out labels are sealed (D-064):** never open, read, grep or print anything under
  `evaluation/heldout/`. Use `evaluation/benchmark/dev.jsonl` for all development. Load
  `test_inputs.jsonl` only to check schema compatibility. Labels are released only by
  `evaluation.benchmark.load_test_labels(final=True)` at final scoring.
- Same model, instructions, cases, labels and policy version across A–D. C vs D reuses
  identical pre-verification outputs.
- Labels are policy-derived and independently checked. The runtime verifier is never ground
  truth.
- Dev and held-out are separated **before** prompt work. The held-out set is frozen.
  Near-duplicates stay on the same side.
- Metric definitions and denominators are frozen before the held-out run. Report raw counts,
  per-category results and paired comparisons.
- Record model IDs, prompt versions, inference settings, KB version and saved predictions for
  every run.
- Report failures and limitations honestly. This is a controlled benchmark, not
  population-level evidence.

## Working protocol
**Before a major change:**
- cite the relevant requirement IDs;
- state assumptions and trade-offs;
- list the affected files and tests;
- get approval for material design changes.

**After a change:**
- run the relevant checks;
- report the actual output;
- map the work to requirement IDs;
- note limitations and open issues.

**At the end of each phase or session:** update `docs/development_log.md` with completed work,
decisions, failures and next steps.

**Token use:** load only task-relevant context. Keep durable knowledge in the docs, not in
chat. Never drop relevant context just to save tokens.

  rebase or any history rewrite. Read-only Git commands (`status`, `diff`, `log`, `grep`) and
  `git add` are fine.

  point to commit**. Include:

  - the check results that make the milestone stable;

- **Before any suggested commit:** confirm nothing from `references/private/` or

which must be committed (D-028). Verified on macOS with uv 0.13.6 and Python 3.13.2 (project

- Lockfile check: `uv lock --check`

- Build image: `docker build -t bto-buddy .`
- Run container: `cp .env.example .env` (once; fill in values when an LLM is configured), then
  `docker run --rm -p 8501:8501 --env-file .env bto-buddy`
- Health check: `curl -f http://localhost:8501/_stcore/health`

**Docker image:** two-stage build on `python:3.12-slim`, uv 0.13.6, runs as non-root `app`,
port 8501, HEALTHCHECK on `/_stcore/health`. Configuration comes from environment variables
only. `.dockerignore` keeps `references/`, `data/private_corpus/`, `.env*`, docs, tests and
caches out of the build context.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh.
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.
